metadata.title: Existence and classification of overtwisted contact structures in all dimensions

extraction_notes.note: Several proofs contain enumerate/itemize lists inside a single sentence whose items the parser reports as author labels; to let every label start a step, the sentence is a container step whose children are the item texts, so some child steps end at a comma or semicolon.

Parametric versions and routine lemmas are stated with no proof or only 'the proof is analogous/straightforward'; kept as results with rigor semi_formal, and the 'analogous' sentences became short proof nodes (their \ref to the model result marked as a mention).
Claim or external theorem: the itemized consequences restate results proved for plastikstufe manifolds [Ni06, AlHo09, MuNiPlaSti12] and transfer them via the paper's claim; kept as a paper claim.
These definitions span two sentences (a construction followed by the sentence naming it, or a definition followed by 'More precisely ...'), kept together as one node.

The dependency diagram of the main propositions in the introduction is omitted from the source; dependencies were taken from the text and \refs only. Figures (keyhole model, saucers, stack) are referenced but not available.

The plan of the paper, section overviews, acknowledgements and sentences that only announce or motivate a later result (e.g. 'up to conjugation any somewhere negative Hamiltonian is minimal') were not made nodes.

metadata.extraction_comment: The finishing step's warning that DP41 introduces two symbols in separate sentences is a false positive: the period sits inside the display defining Delta_cyl. Remaining defined-term warnings are uses of the same symbol or word in another sense (e.g. a locally redefined K', Delta' or xi_0, 'homotopy equivalence', general generating Hamiltonians).

nodes.name: Contact structure
nodes.statement: A {\em contact structure} on a $(2n+1)$-dimensional manifold $M$ is a completely non-integrable hyperplane field $\xi\subset TM$.

nodes.name: Almost contact structure
nodes.statement: The corresponding formal homotopy counterpart of a contact structure is an {\it almost contact structure}, which is a defined up to a scalar factor pair $(\alpha,\omega)$ where $\alpha$ is non-vanishing 1-form on $M$, possibly with local coefficients in a non-trivial 1-bundle, and $\omega$ is a non-degenerate two-form on the hyperplane field $\xi=\{\alpha=0\}$ with coefficients in the same local system.
nodes.statement_short: An almost contact structure is a pair $(\alpha,\omega)$ up to scale: a nowhere-zero 1-form and a nondegenerate 2-form on its kernel.

nodes.name: Eliashberg's classification of overtwisted contact 3-manifolds
nodes.statement: D. Bennequin \cite{Bennequin} showed that the 1-parametric $h$-principle fails for contact structures on $S^3$ and Y.~Eliashberg in \cite{Eli89} introduced a dichotomy of $3$-dimensional contact manifolds into {\it tight} and {\it overtwisted} and established a parametric $h$-principle for overtwisted ones: {\em any almost contact homotopy class on a closed $3$-manifold contains a unique up to isotopy overtwisted contact structure.}
nodes.statement_short: The 1-parametric h-principle fails on $S^3$ (Bennequin); every almost contact class on a closed 3-manifold has a unique overtwisted contact structure (Eliashberg).

nodes.name: Colin-Giroux-Honda finiteness theorem
nodes.statement: V.~Colin, E.~Giroux and K.~Honda proved in \cite{CoGiHo} that any atoroidal contact 3-manifold admits at most finitely many non-isotopic tight contact structures.

nodes.name: Existence of contact structures on 5-manifolds
nodes.statement: Significant progress in the problem of construction of contact structures on closed manifolds was achieved in the $5$-dimensional case beginning from the work of H.~Geiges \cite{Ge91, Ge97} and H.~Geiges and C.B.~Thomas \cite{GeTh98, GeTh01}, and followed by the work of R.~Casals, D.M.~Pancholi and F.~Presas \cite{CaPaPr13} and J.~Etnyre \cite{Etn13}, where there was established existence of contact structures on any $5$-manifolds in any homotopy class of almost contact structures.

nodes.name: Contact structures on boundaries of almost complex manifolds
nodes.statement: The work \cite{Eli90} implied existence of contact structures on all closed $(2n+1)$-dimensional manifolds that bound almost complex manifolds with the homotopy type of $(n+1)$-dimensional cell complexes, provided $n \geq 2$.

nodes.name: Bourgeois' theorem on contact structures on products with surfaces
nodes.statement: F.~Bourgeois \cite{Bourg02} proved that for any closed contact manifold $M$ and any surface $\Sigma$ with genus at least one, the product $M\times\Sigma$ admits a contact structure, using work of E.~Giroux~\cite{Gir02G}.

nodes.name: Existence h-principle for contact structures
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ be a closed set, and $\xi$ be an almost contact structure on $M$. If $\xi$ is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$ then $\xi$ is homotopic relative to $A$ to a genuine contact structure. In particular, any almost contact structure on a closed manifold is homotopic to a genuine contact structure.
nodes.statement_short: An almost contact structure that is genuine near a closed set $A$ is homotopic rel $A$ to a genuine contact structure; closed almost contact manifolds are contact.
assumptions: $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ be a closed set, and $\xi$ be an almost contact structure on $M$
$\xi$ is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$
conclusions: $\xi$ is homotopic relative to $A$ to a genuine contact structure
any almost contact structure on a closed manifold is homotopic to a genuine contact structure
nodes.label: thm:main-existence

nodes.name: Gromov's notation Op A
nodes.statement: Here we are using Gromov's notation ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\,A$ for any unspecified open neighborhood of a closed subset $A\subset M$.

nodes.name: 3-dimensional overtwisted discs agree with Eliashberg's
nodes.statement: In the $3$-dimensional case this notion is equivalent to the standard notion introduced in \cite{Eli89}.

nodes.name: Relative setting $(M, A, \xi_0)$
nodes.statement: Given a $(2n+1)$-dimensional manifold $M$, let $A$ be a closed subset such that $M \setminus A$ is connected, and let $\xi_0$ be an almost contact structure $M$ that is a genuine contact structure on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A$.

nodes.name: Space of overtwisted contact structures relative to A
nodes.statement: Define $\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0)$ to be the space of contact structures on $M$ that are overtwisted on $M\setminus A$ and coincide with $\xi_0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A$.

nodes.name: Space of almost contact structures relative to A
nodes.statement: The notation $\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$ stands for the space of {\em almost} contact structures that agree with $\xi_0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A$.

nodes.name: Inclusion map j
nodes.statement: Let $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0)\to\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$$ be the inclusion map.

nodes.name: Spaces with a fixed overtwisted disc embedding
nodes.statement: For an embedding $\phi:D_{\mathrm{ot}}\to M\setminus A$, let $\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)$ and $\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)$ be the subspaces of $\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0)$ and $\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0)$ of contact and almost contact structures for which $\phi:(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\zeta_{\mathrm{ot}})\to(M,\xi)$ is a contact embedding.

nodes.name: Parametric h-principle for overtwisted contact structures
nodes.statement: The inclusion map induces an isomorphism $$j_*:\pi_0(\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0))\to\pi_0(\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0))$$ and moreover the map $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)\to\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)$$ is a (weak) homotopy equivalence.
nodes.statement_short: Overtwisted contact structures relative to $A$ satisfy a parametric h-principle: $\pi_0$-bijection, and weak homotopy equivalence with a fixed overtwisted disc.
conclusions: The inclusion map induces an isomorphism $$j_*:\pi_0(\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0))\to\pi_0(\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0))$$
the map $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)\to\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)$$ is a (weak) homotopy equivalence
nodes.label: thm:main

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of overtwisted contact structures in each almost contact class
nodes.statement: On any closed manifold $M$ any almost contact structure is homotopic to an overtwisted contact structure which is unique up to isotopy.
assumptions: On any closed manifold $M$
conclusions: any almost contact structure is homotopic to an overtwisted contact structure which is unique up to isotopy
nodes.label: cor:main

nodes.name: Isocontact embeddings into overtwisted manifolds
nodes.statement: Let $(M^{2n+1},\xi)$ be a connected overtwisted contact manifold and let $(N^{2n+1},\zeta)$ be an open contact manifold of the same dimension. Let $f:N\to M$ be a smooth embedding covered by a contact bundle homomorphism $\Phi:TN\to TM$, that is $\Phi(\zeta_x) = \xi|_{f(x)}$ and $\Phi$ preserves the conformal symplectic structures on $\zeta$ and $\xi$. If $df$ and $\Phi$ are homotopic as injective bundle homomorphisms $TN\to TM$, then $f$ is isotopic to a contact embedding $\widetilde f:(N,\zeta)\to (M,\xi)$. In particular, an open ball with any contact structure embeds into any overtwisted contact manifold of the same dimension.
nodes.statement_short: A formally contact embedding of an open contact manifold into a connected overtwisted one is isotopic to a genuine contact embedding.
assumptions: $(M^{2n+1},\xi)$ be a connected overtwisted contact manifold
$(N^{2n+1},\zeta)$ be an open contact manifold of the same dimension
$f:N\to M$ be a smooth embedding covered by a contact bundle homomorphism $\Phi:TN\to TM$
$df$ and $\Phi$ are homotopic as injective bundle homomorphisms $TN\to TM$
conclusions: $f$ is isotopic to a contact embedding $\widetilde f:(N,\zeta)\to (M,\xi)$
an open ball with any contact structure embeds into any overtwisted contact manifold of the same dimension
nodes.label: cor:isocontact

nodes.name: Overtwisting is the strongest exotic notion
nodes.statement: We claim that our notion is stronger than any other possible notions, in the sense that any exotic phenomenon, e.g.\ a plastikstufe \cite{Ni06}, can be found in any overtwisted contact manifold.
nodes.statement_short: Any exotic open contact model (e.g. a plastikstufe) embeds in every overtwisted manifold of the same dimension.

nodes.name: Proof that overtwisting is the strongest notion
nodes.statement: Indeed suppose we are given some exotic model $(A, \zeta)$, which is an open contact manifold, and assume it formally embeds into an equidimensional $(M, \xi_{ot})$, then by Corollary~\ref{cor:isocontact} $(A, \zeta)$ admits a genuine contact embedding into $(M, \xi_{ot})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Corollary 1.4 to a formal embedding of the exotic model.

nodes.name: Plastikstufe consequences for overtwisted manifolds
nodes.statement: In particular, the known results about contact manifolds with a plastikstufe apply to overtwisted manifolds as well: \begin{itemize}{\em \item Overtwisted contact manifolds are not (semi-positively) symplectically fillable \cite{Ni06}; \item The Weinstein conjecture holds for any contact form defining an overtwisted contact structure on a closed manifold \cite{AlHo09}; \item Any Legendrian submanifold whose complement is overtwisted is loose \cite{MuNiPlaSti12}. Conversely, any loose Legendrian in an overtwisted ambient manifold has an overtwisted complement.}
nodes.statement_short: Overtwisted manifolds are not semi-positively fillable, satisfy the Weinstein conjecture, and Legendrians with overtwisted complement are loose.

nodes.name: Foliation setting
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a smooth $(2n+1)$-dimensional foliation on a manifold $V$ of dimension $m=2n+1+q$.

nodes.name: Existence of leafwise contact structures on foliations
nodes.statement: Any leafwise almost contact structure on $\mathcal{F}$ is homotopic to a genuine leafwise contact structure.
conclusions: Any leafwise almost contact structure on $\mathcal{F}$ is homotopic to a genuine leafwise contact structure
nodes.label: thm:existence-fol

nodes.name: Overtwisted leafwise contact structure
nodes.statement: A leafwise contact structure $\xi$ on a codimension $q$ foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on a manifold $V$ of dimension $2n+1+q$ is called {\em overtwisted} if there exist disjoint embeddings $$ \mbox{$h_i:T_i\times B \to V$ for $i=1,\dots, N$,} $$ where $(B, \zeta)$ is a $(2n+1)$-dimensional overtwisted contact ball and each $T_i$ is a compact $q$-dimensional manifold with boundary, such that \begin{itemize} \item each leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ is intersected by one of these embeddings, and \item for each $i=1,\dots, N$ and $\tau\in T_i$ the restriction $h_i|_{\tau \times B}$ is a contact embedding of $(B, \zeta)$ into some leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ with its contact structure.
nodes.statement_short: A leafwise contact structure is overtwisted if families of overtwisted balls, parametrized by compact $T_i$, meet every leaf contactly.

nodes.name: Overtwisted basis
nodes.statement: The set of embeddings $h_1,\dots, h_N$ is called an {\em overtwisted basis} of the overtwisted leafwise contact structure $\xi$ on $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: Relative foliated setting
nodes.statement: For a closed subset $A \subset V$, let $\xi_0$ be a leafwise contact structure on $\mathcal{F}|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A}$, and let $h_i:T_i\times B \to V\setminus A$ for $i=1,\dots, N$ be a collection of disjoint embeddings.

nodes.name: Space of overtwisted leafwise contact structures
nodes.statement: Define $$\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F};A,\xi_0,h_1,\dots, h_N)$$ to be the space of leafwise contact structures $\mathcal{F}$ that coincide with $\xi_0$ over ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A$ and such that $\{h_i\}_{i\in\{1,\dots, N\}}$ is an overtwisted basis for $\mathcal{F}_{V\setminus A}$.

nodes.name: Space of leafwise almost contact structures
nodes.statement: Define $$\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F};A,\xi_0,h_1,\dots, h_n))$$ to be the analogous space of leafwise almost contact structures on $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: h-principle for overtwisted leafwise contact structures
nodes.statement: The inclusion map $$\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F};A,\xi_0,h_1,\dots, h_N)\to \mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F};A,\xi_0,h_1,\dots, h_N)$$ is a (weak) homotopy equivalence.
conclusions: is a (weak) homotopy equivalence
nodes.label: thm:classif-fol

nodes.name: Gray-Moser theorem for leafwise contact structures
nodes.statement: {\rm If $V$ is closed then an analog of Gray-Moser's theorem still holds even though the leaves could be non-compact. Indeed, the leafwise vector field produced by Moser's argument is integrable because $V$ is compact, and hence it generates the flow realizing the prescribed deformation of the leafwise contact structure. Therefore, a homotopical classification of leafwise contact structures coincides with their isotopical classification. }
nodes.statement_short: On a closed manifold, leafwise homotopic contact structures are leafwise isotopic, since Moser's vector field integrates.
nodes.label: rem:foliations

nodes.name: Dimension conventions for discs
nodes.statement: For the sake of clarity, we will always use the convention $\dim B=2n+1$, $\dim D = 2n$, and $\dim \Delta = 2n-1$.

nodes.name: Notation I and S^1
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, the notation $I$ stands for the interval $I= [0,1]$ and $S^1$ for the circle $S^1 = {\mathbb{R}}/{\mathbb{Z}}$.

nodes.name: Compact inclusion
nodes.statement: The notation $A \Subset B$ stands for compact inclusion, meaning $\overline A \subset {\rm Int\,} B$.

nodes.name: Standard contact structure on R^{2n-1}
nodes.statement: As the standard model of contact structures in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}={\mathbb{R}}\times({\mathbb{R}}^2)^{n-1}$ we choose $$\xi_{\rm st}:=\left\{\lambda_{\rm st}^{2n-1}:=dz+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} u_id\varphi_i=0\right\}$$ where $(r_i,\varphi_i)$ are polar coordinates in copies of ${\mathbb{R}}^2$ with $\varphi_i \in S^1$ and $u_i:=r_i^2$.

nodes.name: Standard contact structure on R^{2n+1}
nodes.statement: On ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ we will use two equivalent contact structures, both defined by $$ \xi_{\rm st}:= \{\lambda_{\rm st}^{2n-1} + vdt = 0\} $$ where the coordinates $(v,t)$ have two possible meanings.

nodes.name: Coordinates (v,t)
nodes.statement: For ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times {\mathbb{R}}^2$ we will take $v := r^2$ and $t \in S^1$ where $(r,t)$ are polar coordinates on ${\mathbb{R}}^2$, while for ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times T^*{\mathbb{R}}$ we will take $v := -y_n$ and $t:= x_n$.

nodes.name: Star-shaped domain
nodes.statement: A compact domain in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm std})$ will be called {\em star-shaped} if its boundary is transverse to the contact vector field $Z = z\frac{\partial}{\partial z}+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}u_i\frac{\partial}{\partial u_i}$.
differentia: its boundary is transverse to the contact vector field

nodes.name: Star-shaped abstract contact ball
nodes.statement: An abstract contact $(2n-1)$-dimensional closed ball will be called star-shaped if it is contactomorphic to a star-shaped domain in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$.

nodes.name: Characteristic distribution
nodes.statement: A hypersurface $\Sigma \subset (M, \xi = \ker \lambda)$ in a contact manifold has a singular $1$-dimensional {\em characteristic distribution} $\ell\subset T\Sigma\cap\xi$, defined to be the kernel of the $2$-form $d\lambda|_{T\Sigma\cap\xi}$, with singularities where $\xi = T\Sigma$.

nodes.name: Characteristic foliation
nodes.statement: The distribution $\ell$ integrates to a singular characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ with a transverse contact structure, that is contact structures on hypersufaces $Y \subset \Sigma$ transverse to $\mathcal{F}$, which is invariant with respect to monodromy along the leaves of $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: Characteristic foliation determines the contact germ
nodes.statement: The characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ and its transverse contact structure determines the germ of $\xi$ along $\Sigma$ up to a diffeomorphism fixed on $\Sigma$.

nodes.name: Contact shell
nodes.statement: A \emph{contact shell} will be an almost contact structure $\xi$ on a ball $B$ such that $\xi$ is genuine near $\partial B$.

nodes.name: Solid contact shell
nodes.statement: A contact shell $(B,\xi)$ is called {\em solid} if $\xi$ is a genuine contact structure.

nodes.name: Equivalence of contact shells
nodes.statement: An {\em equivalence} between two contact shells $(B,\xi)$ and $(B',\xi')$ is a diffeomorphism $g:B\to B'$ such that $g_*\xi$ coincides with $\xi'$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B'$ and $g_*\xi$ is homotopic to $\xi'$ through almost contact structures fixed on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B'$.

nodes.name: Domination of contact shells
nodes.statement: Given two shells $\zeta_+=(B_+,\xi_+)$ and $\zeta_-=(B_-,\xi_-)$ we say that $\zeta_+$ {\em dominates} $\zeta_-$ if there exists both \begin{itemize} \item a shell $\widetilde\zeta=\left( B, \xi\right)$ with an equivalence $g:(B,\xi)\to (B_+,\xi_+)$ of contact shells, \item an embedding $h: B_- \to B$ such that $h^*\xi=\xi_-$ and $ \xi$ is a genuine contact structure on $ B \setminus {\rm Int\,} h(B_-).$
nodes.statement_short: $\zeta_+$ dominates $\zeta_-$ if a shell equivalent to $\zeta_+$ contains $\zeta_-$ with genuine contact structure outside it.

nodes.name: Subordination map
nodes.statement: We will refer to the composition $g\circ h:(B_-,\xi_-)\to (B_+,\xi_+)$ as a {\em subordination} map.

nodes.name: A shell dominating a solid shell is solid
nodes.statement: Notice that, if $ (B_+,\xi_+)$ dominates $(B_-,\xi_-)$ and $(B_-,\xi_-)$ is solid, then $ (B_+,\xi_+)$ is equivalent to a solid shell.

nodes.name: Solid subordination map
nodes.statement: If both shells $(B_-,\xi_-)$ and $ (B_+,\xi_+)$ are solid, then the subordination map is called {\em solid} if it is a contact embedding.

nodes.name: Gluing place
nodes.statement: A \emph{gluing place} on a contact shell $(B, \xi)$ is a smooth point $p \in \partial B$ where $T_{p}\partial B = \xi|_{p}$.

nodes.name: Boundary connected sum of contact shells
nodes.statement: Given two gluing places $p_i \in (B_i, \xi_i)$ on contact shells, the standard topological boundary connected sum construction can be performed in a straightforward way at the points $p_i$ to produce a contact shell $(B_0\#B_1,\xi_0\#\xi_1)$, which we will call the {\em boundary connected sum} of the shells $(B_i,\xi_i)$ at the boundary points $p_i$.

nodes.name: Contact Hamiltonian on a star-shaped domain
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ be a compact star-shaped domain and consider a smooth function \begin{equation} K: \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{with}\quad K|_{\partial \Delta \times S^1} > 0. \end{equation} Throughout the paper we will use the notation $(K, \Delta)$ to refer to a such a contact Hamiltonian on a star-shaped domain.
nodes.statement_short: A contact Hamiltonian $(K,\Delta)$ is a smooth $K$ on $\Delta\times S^1$ positive on $\partial\Delta\times S^1$.

nodes.name: Contact Hamiltonian positive on the boundary (1)
nodes.statement: K: \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{with}\quad K|_{\partial \Delta \times S^1} > 0.
nodes.label: e:KBoundary

nodes.name: Ball B_{K,C}
nodes.statement: For a constant $C \in {\mathbb{R}}$, we can define a piecewise smooth $(2n+1)$-dimensional ball associated to $(K, \Delta)$ by \begin{equation} B_{K,C} := \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 : v \leq K(x,t)+C\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 \end{equation} provided $C + {\rm min}(K) > 0$.

nodes.name: Ball B_{K,C} (2)
nodes.statement: B_{K,C} := \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 : v \leq K(x,t)+C\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times {\mathbb{R}}^2
nodes.label: e:S1ball

nodes.name: Admissible family rho
nodes.statement: Now consider a smooth family of functions \begin{equation} \rho_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{for}\quad (x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1 \quad\mbox{such that} \end{equation} \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho_{(x,t)}(0) = 0$ for all $(x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$\,, \item $\rho_{(x,t)}(v) = v - C$ when $(x,v,t) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{v = K(x,t) +C\}$\,, and \item $\partial_v \rho_{(x,t)}(v) > 0$ when $(x,v,t) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{v \leq K(x,t) + C, x \in \partial\Delta\}$\,.
nodes.statement_short: A family $\rho_{(x,t)}$ with $\rho(0)=0$, $\rho(v)=v-C$ near the top boundary and $\partial_v\rho>0$ over $\partial\Delta$.

nodes.name: Family rho_{(x,t)} (3)
nodes.statement: \rho_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{for}\quad (x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1 \quad\mbox{such that}
nodes.label: e:FamilyRhoS1

nodes.name: Almost contact structure eta_{K,rho}
nodes.statement: Such a family, which exists by \eqref{e:KBoundary}, defines an almost contact structure on $B_{K, C}$ given by \begin{equation} \eta_{K, \rho} := (\alpha_\rho, \omega) \quad\mbox{with}\quad \alpha_\rho := \lambda_{{\rm st}} + \rho\,dt \mbox{ and } \omega := d\lambda_{{\rm st}} + dv\wedge dt \end{equation} where smoothness and condition (i) ensures $\alpha_\rho$ is a well defined $1$-form.

nodes.name: Almost contact structure eta_{K,rho} (4)
nodes.statement: \eta_{K, \rho} := (\alpha_\rho, \omega) \quad\mbox{with}\quad \alpha_\rho := \lambda_{{\rm st}} + \rho\,dt \mbox{ and } \omega := d\lambda_{{\rm st}} + dv\wedge dt
nodes.label: S1ContactForm

nodes.name: Circle model is a contact shell
nodes.statement: The pair $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho})$ is a contact shell, which up to equivalence is independent of the choice of $\rho$ and $C$.
conclusions: The pair $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho})$ is a contact shell
up to equivalence is independent of the choice of $\rho$ and $C$
nodes.label: l:CircleShell

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: One checks $\alpha_\rho$ satisfies the contact condition \begin{equation} \mbox{$\alpha_\rho \wedge (d\alpha_\rho)^n > 0$ whenever $\partial_v \rho > 0$} \end{equation} and hence $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho})$ is a contact shell by conditions (ii) and (iii). Consider the special case of two choices $\rho_0$ and $\rho_1$ as in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoS1} for the same $C$. We can pick a family of diffeomorphisms $\phi_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that $$ \phi_{(x,t)}(v) = (\rho_1^{-1}\circ\rho_0)_{(x,t)}(v) \mbox{ on } {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{v = K(x,t) + C\} \cup {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta $$ and this family induces a diffeomorphism $\Phi: B_{K,C} \to B_{K,C}$ such that $\Phi^*\alpha_{\rho_1} = \alpha_{\rho_1 \circ \phi}$ and $\alpha_{\rho_1 \circ \phi} = \alpha_{\rho_0}$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B_{K,C}$. It follows that $\Phi$ is an equivalence between $\eta_{K, \rho_0}$ and $\eta_{K, \rho_1}$ since we have the straight line homotopy from $\alpha_{\rho_1 \circ \phi}$ to $\alpha_{\rho_0}$. Given two choices $(C_0, \rho_0)$ and $(C_1, \rho_1)$, we can pick a family of diffeomorphisms $\psi_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that $$ \psi_{(x,t)}(v) = v + (C_1 - C_0) \quad \mbox{ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{v = C_0+K(x,t)\}$}. $$ Now to see $(B_{K, C_0}, \eta_{K, \rho_0})$ and $(B_{K, C_1}, \eta_{K, \rho_1})$ are equivalent, just note that $(B_{K, C_0}, \eta_{K, \rho_0})$ and $(B_{K, C_0}, \eta_{K, \rho_1 \circ \psi})$ are equivalent via the previous special case and $\psi$ induces an isomorphism $\Psi: (B_{K, C_0}, \alpha_{\rho_1\circ\psi}) \to (B_{K, C_1}, \alpha_{\rho_1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Check the contact condition where $\partial_v\rho>0$, then compare two choices of $\rho$ by fiberwise reparametrization and a straight-line homotopy.

nodes.name: Contact condition for alpha_rho (5)
nodes.statement: \mbox{$\alpha_\rho \wedge (d\alpha_\rho)^n > 0$ whenever $\partial_v \rho > 0$}
nodes.label: e:CC

nodes.name: Notation (B_K, eta_K)
nodes.statement: We will use the notation $(B_{K, C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ throughout the paper for this specific construction, though we will usually drop $C$ and $\rho$ from the notation and write $(B_K, \eta_{K})$ when the particular choice will be irrelevant.

nodes.name: Circle model contact shell
nodes.statement: We will refer to this contact shell as the \emph{circle model associated to $(\Delta, K)$}.

nodes.name: Circle model is genuine iff K > 0
nodes.statement: {\rm This construction can produce a genuine contact structure on $B_K$ if and only if $K > 0$. If $K > 0$, then from \eqref{e:CC} it follows $(B_{K, 0}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ for $\rho(v) = v$ is a contact ball. Conversely if $K(x_0,t_0) \leq 0$ for some $(x_0, t_0)$, then $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ is never contact by \eqref{e:CC} since since conditions (i) and (ii) on $\rho$ force $\partial_v\rho_{(x_0,t_0)}(v_0) = 0$ for some $v_0$.}

nodes.name: Hypersurfaces Sigma~_{1,K}, Sigma~_{2,K}
nodes.statement: Consider the contact germs on the hypersurfaces \begin{align*} \tilde\Sigma_{1,K} &= \{(x,v,t): v = K(x,t)\} \subset (\Delta \times T^*S^1, \ker(\lambda_{{\rm st}} + v\,dt)) \quad\mbox{and}\\ \tilde\Sigma_{2,K} &= \{(x,v,t): 0 \leq v \leq K(x, t)\,,\,\, x \in \partial \Delta\} \subset (\Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2, \ker(\lambda_{{\rm st}} + v\,dt)). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Contact germ eta~_K
nodes.statement: These germs can be glued together via the natural identification between neighborhoods of their boundaries, to form a contact germ $\tilde{\eta}_K$ on $\tilde{\Sigma}_K := \tilde\Sigma_{1,K} \cup \tilde\Sigma_{2,K}$.

nodes.name: Direct description of the circle model germ
nodes.statement: The contact germs $(\partial B_K, \eta_K)$ and $(\tilde{\Sigma}_K, \tilde{\eta}_K)$ are contactomorphic.
conclusions: The contact germs $(\partial B_K, \eta_K)$ and $(\tilde{\Sigma}_K, \tilde{\eta}_K)$ are contactomorphic
nodes.label: l:EasyCircleGerm

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: We have that the boundary $\partial B_{K, C} = \Sigma_{1,K, C} \cup \Sigma_{2,K, C}$ where \begin{align*} \Sigma_{1,K,C} &:= \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2: v = K(x,t)+C\} \quad\mbox{and} \\ \Sigma_{2,K,C} &:= \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2: 0 \leq v \leq K(x, t)+C\,,\,\, x \in \partial \Delta\}\,. \end{align*} Recalling the $1$-form $\alpha_\rho = \lambda_{{\rm st}} + \rho\,dt$ is a contact form near $\partial B_{K,C} \subset \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2$, just note that $\rho$ induces contactomorphisms of neighborhoods $$ ({\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Sigma_{j,K,C}\,,\,\, \ker \alpha_\rho) \to ({\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \tilde\Sigma_{j,K}\,,\,\, \ker(\lambda_{{\rm st}} + v\,dt)) $$ for $j=0,1$ by construction.
nodes.statement_short: $\rho$ induces contactomorphisms of neighborhoods of the two boundary pieces.

nodes.name: Cylindrical domain Delta_cyl
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper we will often use the following star-shaped cylindrical domain $$ \Delta_{\rm cyl} := D^{2n-2}\times[-1,1] = \{\abs{z} \leq 1\,,\,\, u \leq 1\} \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}}). $$ where $D^{2n-2}:= \{u=\sum_i^{n-1}u_i\leq 1\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-2}$ is the unit ball.

nodes.name: North and south poles
nodes.statement: Also observe for any contact Hamiltonian $(K, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$ the \emph{north pole} and \emph{south pole} $$ P_{\pm 1} := (0, \pm 1, 0) \in (\partial B_K, \eta_K) $$ in the coordinates $(u, z, v) \in {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times {\mathbb{R}}^{2}$ are gluing places in the sense of Section~\ref{sec:shells}.

nodes.name: Reduction to a universal model hole
nodes.statement: For fixed dimension $2n+1$ there exists a contact Hamiltonian $(K_{\mathrm{univ}}, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$, specified in Lemma \ref{lm:universal-eps}, such that the following holds. For any almost contact manifold $(M, \xi)$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:main-existence} there exists an almost contact structure $\xi'$ on $M$, which is homotopic to $\xi$ relative $A$ through almost contact structures, and a finite collection of disjoint balls $B_i\subset M\setminus A$ for $i=1,\dots, L$, with piecewise smooth boundary such that \begin{itemize} \item $\xi'$ is a genuine contact structure on $M\setminus \bigcup_1^L{\rm Int\,} B_i$ \item the contact shells $\xi'|_{B_i}$ are equivalent to $(B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}},\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ for $i=1, \dots, L$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3.1 Construction of contact structures with universal holes
nodes.statement_short: Every almost contact structure is homotopic to one that is genuine outside finitely many balls, each equivalent to the universal circle model $B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}$.
assumptions: For fixed dimension $2n+1$
any almost contact manifold $(M, \xi)$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:main-existence}
conclusions: there exists a contact Hamiltonian $(K_{\mathrm{univ}}, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$
there exists an almost contact structure $\xi'$ on $M$, which is homotopic to $\xi$ relative $A$ through almost contact structures
nodes.label: prop:unique-model

nodes.name: Freedom in the choice of K_univ
nodes.statement: {\rm If $(B_K, \eta_K)$ is dominated by $(B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}},\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$, then we can $K$ in the statement of Proposition~\ref{prop:unique-model} in lieu of $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$. In particular by Lemma~\ref{lm:3-domin}, in {\em the $3$-dimensional case} we can take $K_{\mathrm{univ}}: [-1, 1] \to {\mathbb{R}}$ to be {\em any somewhere negative function.} Our proof in higher dimension is not constructive, and we do not know an effective criterion which would allow one to verify whether a particular function $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ satisfies \ref{prop:unique-model}. Of course, it is easy to construct a $1$-parameter family of Hamiltonians $K^\varepsilon$ so that any Hamiltonian $K$ is less than $K^\varepsilon$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ (see Example \ref{ex:special}). We can then take $K_{\mathrm{univ}} = K^\varepsilon$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. It would be interesting to find such a general criterion for which Hamiltonians can be taken as $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$.}
nodes.section: 3.1 Construction of contact structures with universal holes

nodes.name: Special function
nodes.statement: A smooth function $k: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is called \emph{special} if $k(1)>0$ and \begin{equation} a\,k\left(\tfrac{u}{a}\right) < k(u) \quad\mbox{for all $a > 1$ and $u \geq 0$.} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.statement_short: $k$ is special if $k(1)>0$ and $a\,k(u/a)<k(u)$ for all $a>1$, $u\geq0$.

nodes.name: Subscaling inequality for special functions (6)
nodes.statement: a\,k\left(\tfrac{u}{a}\right) < k(u) \quad\mbox{for all $a > 1$ and $u \geq 0$.}
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.label: e:subscale

nodes.name: Special functions are negative at 0
nodes.statement: This implies that $k(0)<0$, and hence $k(u)$ has a zero in $(0, 1)$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes

nodes.name: Tangent-line condition for special functions (7)
nodes.statement: \quad k(u) - u\,k'(u) < 0 \quad\mbox{for all $u \geq 0$}
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.label: e:specialCon

nodes.name: Spherically symmetric Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: We call a function $K:\Delta_{\rm cyl}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ {\em spherically symmetric} if it depends only on the coordinates $(u, z)$ where $u=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}u_i$, in this case by a slight abuse of notation will write $K(u,z)$, rather than $\widetilde K(u,z)$ for some function $\widetilde K:[0,1]\times[-1,1]\to {\mathbb{R}}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes

nodes.name: Special contact Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: A spherically symmetric piecewise smooth contact Hamiltonian $K: \Delta_{\rm cyl} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is called {\em special} if \begin{description} \item{(i)} $K > 0$ on $\partial\Delta_{{\rm cyl}}$; \item{(ii)} $K(u,-\delta)=K(u,\delta)$ for $\delta \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{1\}$ and $u \in [0,1]$; \item{(iii)} If $\delta \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{1\}$, then $K(u,z)\leq K(u,\delta)$ for $u\in[0,1]$ and $\abs{z} \leq \delta$; \end{description} and there exist $z_D \in (-1, 1)$ and a special function $k: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ such that \begin{description} \item{(iv)} $K$ is non-increasing in the coordinate $z$ for $z\in{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [-1,\,z_D]\subset[-1,1]$; \item{(v)} $K(u,z) \geq k (u)$ {\em with equality} if $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{ z_D\}$. \end{description} When $n=1$, where $\Delta_{\rm cyl} = [-1,1]$, condition (v) can be replaced with $K(z_D) < 0$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.statement_short: A spherically symmetric Hamiltonian on $\Delta_{\rm cyl}$, positive on the boundary, symmetric and maximal near $z=\pm1$, non-increasing in $z$ up to $z_D$, and bounded below by a special function attained near $z_D$.
nodes.label: def:SpecialHam

nodes.name: Existence of special Hamiltonians below any given one
nodes.statement: As the following example shows special contact Hamiltonians exist and furthermore for any particular contact Hamiltonian $(K',\Delta_{\rm cyl})$ positive on $\partial\Delta_{\rm cyl}\times S^1$ there is a special contact Hamiltonian $K: \Delta_{\rm cyl} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ such that $K < K'$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes

nodes.name: Explicit special Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: {\rm For positive constants $a, b, \lambda$ with $b < 1$ and $\lambda > \tfrac{a}{1-b}$, define the special piecewise smooth function $$ k(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda(u-b) - a & \mbox{if $u \geq b$}\\ -a & \mbox{if $u \leq b$} \end{cases} $$ and the special piecewise smooth contact Hamiltonian $$ K(u,z) = {\rm max}\{k(u),\,k(\abs{z})\}. $$ By a perturbation of $K$ near its singular set, we may construct a smooth special contact Hamiltonian $\tilde{K}$ that is $C^0$-close to $K$, though smoothness of $K$ will not be needed in the proof.}
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.label: ex:special

nodes.name: Disc germ (D_K, eta_K)
nodes.statement: Let $K:\Delta_{\rm cyl}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ be a special contact Hamiltonian and define $(D_{K}, \eta_{K})$ to be the contact germ on the $2n$-dimensional disc \begin{equation} D_{K} := \{(x, v, t) \in \partial B_{K}: z(x) \in [-1, z_D]\} \subset (B_{K}, \eta_{K}) \end{equation} where $z_D$ is the constant in Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam}.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes

nodes.name: Disc D_K (8)
nodes.statement: D_{K} := \{(x, v, t) \in \partial B_{K}: z(x) \in [-1, z_D]\} \subset (B_{K}, \eta_{K})
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.label: eq:ot-disc

nodes.name: Overtwisted disc and overtwisted contact manifold
nodes.statement: Let $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ be as in Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model}. An \emph{overtwisted disc} $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\eta_{\mathrm{ot}})$ is a $2n$-dimensional disc with a germ of a contact structure such that there is a contactomorphism $$ (D_{\mathrm{ot}},\eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \cong \left(D_{K}, \eta_{K}\right) $$ where $K$ is some special contact Hamiltonian such that $K < K_{\mathrm{univ}}$. A contact manifold $(M^{2n+1}, \xi)$ is {\em overtwisted} if it admits a contact embedding $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\eta_{\mathrm{ot}})\to (M,\xi)$ of some overtwisted disc.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.statement_short: An overtwisted disc is a $2n$-disc germ contactomorphic to $(D_K,\eta_K)$ for a special $K<K_{\mathrm{univ}}$; a contact manifold is overtwisted if it contains one.
also_stated_at: Deferring the definition until Section \ref{sec:ot-disc}, we will say here that a contact manifold $(M^{2n+1},\xi)$ is called overtwisted if it admits a contact embedding of a piecewise smooth $2n$-disc $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ with a certain model germ $\zeta_{\mathrm{ot}}$ of a contact structure.

Recall the definition of an overtwisted contact structure from Section \ref{sec:ot-disc}: a contact structure $\xi$ on a manifold $M$ is called {\em overtwisted} if there is a contact embedding $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\xi_{\mathrm{ot}})\to (M,\xi)$, see Section \ref{sec:ot-disc}.
nodes.label: def:OTD

nodes.name: Overtwisted discs in dimension 3
nodes.statement: {\rm In the $3$-dimensional case, it follows from Lemma~\ref{lm:3-domin} that the disc $$ D_{K} := \{(z, v, t) \in \partial B_{K}: z \in [-1, z_D]\} \subset (B_{K}, \eta_{K}) $$ is overtwisted in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:OTD} for {\em any} special contact Hamiltonian, i.e a somewhere negative function on the interval $[-1,1]$, positive near the end-points $\pm 1$. }
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes

nodes.name: Dependence of the overtwisted disc on K
nodes.statement: {\rm The definition of the overtwisted disc $(D_K,\eta_K)$ depends on the choice of a special Hamiltonian $K<K_{\mathrm{univ}}$, and the germs $\eta_K$ need not to be contactomorphic when we vary $K$. However, as Corollary~\ref{cor:isocontact} shows, for any two special Hamiltonians $K,K'<K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ any neighborhood of $(D_K,\eta_K)$ contains $(D_{K'},\eta_{K'})$.}
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.label: rem:various-ot-discs

nodes.name: Neighborhoods of overtwisted discs are foliated by overtwisted discs
nodes.statement: Every neighborhood of an overtwisted disc in a contact manifold contains a foliation by overtwisted discs.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
conclusions: Every neighborhood of an overtwisted disc in a contact manifold contains a foliation by overtwisted discs
nodes.label: prop:neighb-ot

nodes.name: Contact ball with D_K on its boundary
nodes.statement: Suppose one has a $(2n+1)$-dimensional contact ball $(B,\xi)$ with piecewise smooth boundary such that $(D_{K}, \eta_{K}) \subset (\partial B, \xi)$ where the co-orientation of $D_{K}$ coincides with the outward co-orientation of $\partial B$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes

nodes.name: Filling a universal hole by an overtwisted disc
nodes.statement: Let $K_0, K, \;K_0\geq K,$ be two contact Hamiltonians and $K$ is special. Then the contact shell $(B_{K_0}\# B, \eta_{K_0} \# \xi)$ given by performing a boundary connected sum at the north pole of $B_{K_0}$ and the south pole of $D_{K} \subset \partial B$ is equivalent to a genuine contact structure.
nodes.section: 3.2 Overtwisted discs and filling of universal holes
nodes.statement_short: The boundary connected sum of a circle model $B_{K_0}$ with a contact ball bounding $D_K$ ($K$ special, $K\leq K_0$) is equivalent to a genuine contact structure.
assumptions: $K_0, K, \;K_0\geq K,$ be two contact Hamiltonians
$K$ is special
conclusions: the contact shell $(B_{K_0}\# B, \eta_{K_0} \# \xi)$ given by performing a boundary connected sum at the north pole of $B_{K_0}$ and the south pole of $D_{K} \subset \partial B$ is equivalent to a genuine contact structure
nodes.label: p:ConnectSumDisc

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: Choose a ball $B\subset M\setminus A$ with piecewise smooth boundary and deform the almost contact structure $\xi$ to make it a contact structure on $B$ with an overtwisted disc $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (\partial B, \xi)$ on its boundary. This can be done since any two almost contact structures on the ball are homotopic if we do not require the homotopy to be fixed on $\partial B$. Using Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model} we deform the almost contact structure $\xi$ relative to $A\cup B$ to an almost contact structure $\xi$ on $M$, which is genuine in the complement of finitely many disjoint balls $B_1,\dots, B_N\subset M\setminus (A\cup B)$ where each $(B_i, \xi|_{B_i})$ is isomorphic to $(B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, \eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ as almost contact structures. According to Proposition \ref{prop:neighb-ot} we can pick disjoint balls $B_i' \subset {\rm Int\,}(B)$, $i=1,\dots, N$, each with an overtwisted disc on their boundary $(D^i_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}^i) \subset (\partial B_i', \xi)$. As we will describe in Section~\ref{sec:BCS} we can perform an ambient boundary connected sum $B_i \# B_i' \subset M \setminus A$ such that the sets $B_i \# B_i'$ are disjoint for $i=1, \dots, N$ and there are isomorphisms of almost contact structures $$ (B_i \# B_i', \xi|_{B_i \# B_i'}) \cong (B_i \# B_i', \xi|_{B_i} \# \xi|_{B_i'}) \cong (B_K \# B_i', \eta_K \# \xi|_{B_i'}). $$ Now for $i=1, \dots, L$ by definition we have $(D^i_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}^i) = (D_{K_i}, \eta_{K_i})$ for special contact Hamiltonians $K_i$ such that $K_i < K_{\mathrm{univ}}$. Therefore we can apply Proposition \ref{p:ConnectSumDisc} to homotope $\xi|_{B_i \# B_i'}$ relative to the boundary to a genuine contact structure on $B_i \# B_i'$ for each $i=1,\dots, N$. The result will be a contact structure on $M$ that is homotopic relative to $A$ to the original almost contact structure.
nodes.statement_short: Make $\xi$ contact near a ball with an overtwisted disc, reduce holes to universal models (Prop 3.1), and fill each hole by a connected sum with an overtwisted ball (Prop 3.9).

nodes.name: Parameter space T
nodes.statement: The parameter space, always denoted by $T$, will be assumed to be a compact manifold of dimension $q$, possibly with boundary, and we will use the letter $\tau$ for points in $T$.

nodes.name: Fibered (almost) contact structure
nodes.statement: A family of (almost) contact structures $\{\xi^\tau\}_{\tau\in T}$ on a manifold $M$ can be equivalently viewed as a fiberwise, or as we also say {\em fibered} (almost) contact structure ${}^T\!\xi$ on the total space of the trivial fibration ${}^TM:=T\times M\to T$, which coincides with $\xi_\tau$ on the fiber $M^\tau:=\tau\times M$, $\tau\in T$.

nodes.name: Fibered contact shell
nodes.statement: A \emph{fibered contact shell} $({}^T M, {}^T\xi)$ is a fibered almost contact structure that is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial({}^T M)$, by which we mean $(M^{\tau}, \xi^\tau)$ is genuine for all $\tau \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial T$ and $({\mathcal O}{\it p}\, M^{\tau}, \xi^{\tau})$ is genuine for all $\tau \in T$.

nodes.name: Equivalence of fibered contact shells
nodes.statement: An {\em equivalence} between fibered contact shells $$ G: ({}^{T_1}B_1 ,{}^{T_1}\xi_1) \to ({}^{T_2}B_2 ,{}^{T_2}\xi_2) $$ is a diffeomorphism covering a diffeomorphism $g:T_1\to T_2$ such that $G^*\left({}^{T_2}\xi_2\right)$ and ${}^{T_1}\xi_1$ are homotopic relative to ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial({}^{T_1}B_1)$ through fibered almost contact structures on ${}^{T_1}B_1$.

nodes.name: Domination of fibered contact shells
nodes.statement: Given fibered contact shells ${}^{T_\pm}\zeta_\pm=\left({}^{T_\pm}B_\pm,{}^{T_\pm}\xi_\pm\right)$ we say ${}^{T_+}\zeta_+$ \emph{dominates} ${}^{T_-}\zeta_-$ if there is a third fibered contact shell $\zeta=\left({}^T B,{}^T\xi\right)$ such that \begin{itemize} \item there is a fibered equivalence $G:{}^{T}\zeta \to {}^{T_+} \zeta_+$ and \item a fiberwise embedding $ H: {}^{T_-}B_-\to{}^{T} B$ covering an embedding $h: T_-\to T$ such that $H^*({}^{T}\zeta)= {}^{T_-}\zeta_{-}$ and ${}^T \xi$ is genuine on $^TB\setminus H({\rm Int\,} ^{T_-}B_-)$.

nodes.name: Fibered subordination map
nodes.statement: We will refer to the embedding $G\circ H:\left({}^{ T_-} B_-,{}^{T_-} \xi_-\right)\to \left({}^{T_+}B_+,{}^{T_+}\xi_+\right)$ as a {\em subordination map}.

nodes.name: Fibered boundary connected sum
nodes.statement: Finally we note that the boundary connected sum construction can be performed in the fibered set-up to define a fibered connected sum $$ ({}^{T}B_1 \# {}^{T}B_2,\, {}^{T}\xi_1\# {}^{T}\xi_2) \quad\mbox{with fibers}\quad (B_1^\tau \# B_2^\tau, \xi_1^{\tau} \# \xi_2^{\tau}) $$ provided that we are given a family of boundary points $p_{1}^\tau \in\partial B_1^\tau$ and $p_{2}^{\tau} \in \partial B_2^\tau$ as in the non-parametric case.

nodes.name: Function E
nodes.statement: Given a special contact Hamiltonian $K:\Delta_{\rm cyl} \to{\mathbb{R}}$ we define a function $E\to{\mathbb{R}}$ by the formula $E(u, z) := K(u,1)$.
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes

nodes.name: Family K^{(s)}
nodes.statement: We further define a family of contact Hamiltonians $K^{(s)}:\Delta_{\rm cyl}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ by \begin{equation} K^{(s)} :=sK+ (1-s)E \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$.} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes

nodes.name: Family K^{(s)} (9)
nodes.statement: K^{(s)} :=sK+ (1-s)E \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$.}
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes
nodes.label: e:ParametricHam

nodes.name: Fibered circular model shell
nodes.statement: Given a disc $T := D^q \subset {\mathbb{R}}^q$ pick a bump function $\delta: T \to [0,1]$ with support in the interior of $T$ and consider the family of contact Hamiltonians $K^{(\delta(\tau))}: \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ parametrized by $\tau \in T$ and the fibered circular model shell over $T$ \begin{equation} \Big({}^T B_{K},\, {}^T\eta_{K}\Big) \quad\mbox{where}\quad {}^T B_{K} = \bigcup_{\tau \in T} \{\tau\} \times B_{K^{\delta(\tau)}} \end{equation} and the fiber over $\tau \in T$ is given by $(B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}}, \eta_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}})$.
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes

nodes.name: Fibered circular model shell (10)
nodes.statement: \Big({}^T B_{K},\, {}^T\eta_{K}\Big) \quad\mbox{where}\quad {}^T B_{K} = \bigcup_{\tau \in T} \{\tau\} \times B_{K^{\delta(\tau)}}
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes
nodes.label: e:FiberHamShell

nodes.name: Parametric reduction to universal model holes
nodes.statement: Let $T = D^q$ and let $A \subset M$ be a closed subset. Every fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\xi_0$ on ${}^TM = T \times M$ that is genuine on $(T\times{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A)\cup ({\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T \times M)$ is homotopic relative to $(T\times A) \cup (\partial T \times M)$ through fibered almost contact structures on ${}^TM$ to some structure ${}^T\xi$ with the following property: There is a collection of disjoint embedded fibered shells ${}^{T_i}B_i \subset {}^TM$ over (not necessarily disjoint) $q$-dimensional discs $T_i \subset T$ for $i = 1, \dots, L$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item the fibers of ${}^T\xi$ are genuine contact structures away from $\bigcup_{i=1}^L {\rm Int\,}({}^{T_i} B_i)$ and \item the fibered contact shells $({}^{T_i}B_i, {}^{T_i}\xi)$ and $({}^{T_i} B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ are equivalent. \end{enumerate} Furthermore for every $C \subset \{1, \dots L\}$ the intersection $\bigcap_{i \in C} T_i$ either empty or a disc.
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes
nodes.statement_short: Parametric version of Proposition 3.1: a fibered almost contact structure over $D^q$ is homotopic to one genuine outside fibered universal circle-model holes over discs $T_i$.
assumptions: $T = D^q$ and let $A \subset M$ be a closed subset
Every fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\xi_0$ on ${}^TM = T \times M$ that is genuine on $(T\times{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A)\cup ({\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T \times M)$
conclusions: is homotopic relative to $(T\times A) \cup (\partial T \times M)$ through fibered almost contact structures on ${}^TM$ to some structure ${}^T\xi$ with the following property

nodes.name: Parametric filling of universal holes
nodes.statement: Let $(K_0, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$ be a contact Hamiltonian and consider the fibered contact shell $$({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$$ given by performing a boundary connected sum on each fiber over $\tau \in T$ at the north pole of $B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}_0}$ and the south pole of $D_{K} \subset \partial B$. If $K \leq K_0$ is special, then $({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ is fibered equivalent to a genuine fibered contact structure.
nodes.section: 3.5 Parametric contact structures with universal holes
nodes.statement_short: Parametric version of Proposition 3.9: the fibered connected sum with an overtwisted ball is fibered equivalent to a genuine fibered contact structure.
assumptions: $(K_0, \Delta_{{\rm cyl}})$ be a contact Hamiltonian
$K \leq K_0$ is special
conclusions: $({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ is fibered equivalent to a genuine fibered contact structure

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:main} is an immediate corollary of the following theorem, which is a fibered version of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-existence}. In particular for each $q \geq 0$, we see that $$ j_*: \pi_q\big(\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)\big) \to \pi_q\big(\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(M;A,\xi_0,\phi)\big) $$ is an isomorphism by applying Theorem~\ref{thm:main-existence-T} in the cases of $D^q$ and $D^{q+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 3.12 over $D^q$ and $D^{q+1}$ to get isomorphisms on all homotopy groups.

nodes.name: Fibered existence theorem with a fixed overtwisted disc
nodes.statement: Let $T = D^q$ and $A \subset M$ be a closed subset such that $M \setminus A$ is connected, and let ${}^T\xi$ be a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^T M$ which is genuine on $(T\times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A) \cup (\partial T\times M)$. If there exists a fixed overtwisted disc $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset M\setminus A$ such that for all $\tau \in T$ the inclusion $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (M \setminus A, \xi^\tau)$ is a contact embedding, then ${}^T\xi$ is homotopic to a fibered genuine contact structure through fibered almost contact structures fixed on $\big(T\times (A\cup D_{\mathrm{ot}})\big)\cup\big(\partial T\times M\big)$
nodes.statement_short: A fibered almost contact structure over $D^q$ with a common overtwisted disc is homotopic, fixed on the disc, $A$ and $\partial T$, to a fibered genuine contact structure.
assumptions: $T = D^q$ and $A \subset M$ be a closed subset such that $M \setminus A$ is connected
${}^T\xi$ be a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^T M$ which is genuine on $(T\times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A) \cup (\partial T\times M)$

there exists a fixed overtwisted disc $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset M\setminus A$ such that for all $\tau \in T$ the inclusion $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (M \setminus A, \xi^\tau)$ is a contact embedding
conclusions: ${}^T\xi$ is homotopic to a fibered genuine contact structure through fibered almost contact structures fixed on $\big(T\times (A\cup D_{\mathrm{ot}})\big)\cup\big(\partial T\times M\big)$
nodes.label: thm:main-existence-T

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.12
nodes.statement: By assumption there is a piecewise smooth disc $D_{\mathrm{ot}}\subset M\setminus A$ such that all almost contact structures $\xi^\tau$ for $\tau\in T$ are genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ and restrict to $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ as $\eta_{\mathrm{ot}}$. Since $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}})$ determines the germ of the contact structure we may pick a ball $B \subset {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ with $D_{\mathrm{ot}} \subset \partial B$ and assume $({}^{T} B, {}^T \xi) = T \times (B, \xi)$. By applying Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model-param} we may assume there is a collection of disjoint fibered balls ${}^{T_i}B_i \subset M \setminus (A \cup B)$ over a collection of discs $T_i \subset T$ for $i = 1, \dots, L$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item ${}^T\xi$ is genuine away from $\bigcup_{i=1}^L {\rm Int\,}({}^{T_i}B_i)$ and \item the fibered shells $({}^{T_i}B_i, {}^{T_i}\xi)$ and $({}^{T_i}B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ are equivalent. \end{enumerate} Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:neighb-ot} to get $L$ disjoint balls $B_i' \subset {\rm Int\,}(B\setminus (D_{\mathrm{ot}}\cup A))$ with an overtwisted disc $(D^i_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (\partial B_i', \xi)$ in each of them. It follows from Lemma \ref{lm:choosing-paths}, proven in Section \ref{sec:foliations-proofs} below, that for each $j$ we can find a parametric family of embedded paths $^{T_j}\gamma_j$ connecting $^{T_j}B_j$ to $^{T_j}B'_j$ in $T\times(M\setminus A\cup D_{\mathrm{ot}})$. Moreover, using Gromov's parametric $h$-principle for transverse paths, see \cite{Gr-PDR}, we can assume the constructed paths are transverse. As we explain in Section~\ref{sec:BCS}, with these parametric paths we can form disjoint parametric ambient boundary connected sums ${}^{T_j}C_j \subset {}^{T_j}(M \setminus (A \cup D_{\mathrm{ot}}))$ for each $j=1, \dots, L$, between the fibered shells $^{T_j}B_j$ and $^{T_j}B'_j$. Furthermore, by Section~\ref{sec:BCS} and property (ii) above we have isomorphisms of fibered almost contact structures $$ ({}^{T_i}C_i, {}^{T_i}\xi) \cong ({}^{T_i}B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}} \# {}^{T_i}B_i',\, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}} \# {}^{T_i}\xi). $$ Applying Proposition~\ref{p:ConnectSumDisc-param} inductively for $j=1,\dots, L$ we deform ${}^T\xi$ on these connected sums relative to their boundary to get a fibered genuine contact structure on ${}^{T}M$.
nodes.statement_short: Standardize holes by Proposition 3.10, find overtwisted balls (Prop 3.8), connect them to the holes by parametric paths (Lemma 9.1), and fill each connected sum (Prop 3.11).

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 1.4
nodes.statement: By an isotopy of $f$ we can arrange that the complement $M\setminus f(N)$ is overtwisted and the closure $f(N)$ is compact. Then, slightly reducing if necessary the manifold $M$, we can assume it non-compact and overtwisted at infinity. Let us exhaust $N$ by compact subsets: $N=\bigcup\limits_1^\infty C_j$, such that $C_j\Subset{\rm Int\,} C_{j+1}$ and $V\setminus C_j$ is connected, $ j=1,\dots $. Set $C_0:=\varnothing$. The result follows by induction from the following claim: {\em Suppose we are given an embedding $f^{j-1}:N\to M$ which is contact on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, C_{j-1}$ and a homotopy of bundle isomorphisms $\Phi^{j-1}_{t} :TN\to TM$ covering $f^{j-1}$ such that the following property ${\rm P}^{j-1}$ is satisfied: \begin{description} \item{${\rm P}^{j-1}:$} The homotopy $\Phi^{j-1}_t$ is contact on $T(N)|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, C_{j-1}}$ for all $t\in[0,1]$, $\Phi^{j-1}_0$ is contact everywhere, and $\Phi^{j-1}_1=df^{j-1}$. \end{description} Then there exists a pair $(f^j,\Phi_t^j)$ which satisfies ${\rm P}^{j}$ and such that $f^{j-1}$ and $f^j$ are isotopic via an isotopy fixed on $C_{j-1}$.} Let $\xi_t$ be a family of almost contact structures on $M$ such that $\xi_t=(\Phi^{j-1}_t)_*\zeta$ on $f^{j-1}(C_j)$ and $\xi_t=\xi$ outside $f^{j-1}(C_{j+1})$. We note that $\xi_0=\xi$ on $f^{j-1}(C_j)$, and $\xi_t=\xi$ on $f^{j-1}(C_{j-1})$ for all $t\in[0,1]$. Theorem \ref{thm:main} allows us to construct a compactly supported homotopy $\widetilde \xi_{t}$ of {\em genuine} contact structures on $M$, $t\in[0,1]$, connecting $\widetilde \xi_0=\xi$ and a contact structure $\widetilde\xi_1$ which coincides with $\xi_1$ on $f^{j-1}(C_j)$. Moreover, this can be done to ensure existence of a homotopy $\Psi_t:TM\to TM$ of bundle isomorphisms such that $\Psi_0=\mathrm {Id}$, $\Psi_t^*\widetilde\xi_t=\xi_t$, and $\Psi_t|_{f^{j-1}(C_{j-1})}=\mathrm {Id}$, $t\in[0,1]$. Then Gray's theorem \cite{Gray59} provides us with a compactly supported diffeotopy $\phi_t:M\to M$, $t\in[0,1]$, such that $\phi_0=\mathrm {Id}$, $\phi_t^*\xi =\widetilde \xi_{t}$ and $\phi_t|_{f^{j-1}(C_{j-1})}=\mathrm {Id}$. Set $f^j:=\phi_1\circ f^{j-1}$ and $\Phi^j_{t}:= d\phi_t\circ \Psi_t^*\circ\Phi^{j-1}$, $t\in[0,1]$. Then $\Phi^j_1=df^j$, $(\Phi^j_t)^*\xi= (\Phi^{j-1}_t)^*\circ(\Psi_{t}) \circ (d\phi_t)^*\xi= (\Phi^{j-1}_t)^*\circ\Psi_t^*\widetilde\xi_{t}= (\Phi^{j-1}_t)^*\xi_t$. Hence, $(\Phi^j_t)^*\xi|_{C_j}=\zeta$ for all $t\in[0,1]$. We also have $(\Psi^j_0)^*\xi=\zeta$ everywhere. Thus, the pair $(f^j,\Phi^j_t)$ satisfies ${\rm P}^{j}$, and the claim follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: Induction over a compact exhaustion of $N$: Theorem 1.2 gives a homotopy of genuine contact structures, and Gray's theorem turns it into an isotopy of the embedding.

nodes.name: Partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains
nodes.statement: Let us introduce a partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains where $$(K, \Delta) \leq (K', \Delta')$$ is defined to mean $\Delta \subset \Delta'$ together with \begin{align} K(x,t) &\leq K'(x,t) \quad\mbox{for all $x \in \Delta$ and} \\ 0 &< K'(x,t) \quad\mbox{for all $x \in \Delta' \setminus \Delta$.} \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.1 A partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains

nodes.name: Pointwise order condition (11)
nodes.statement: K(x,t) &\leq K'(x,t) \quad\mbox{for all $x \in \Delta$ and}
nodes.section: 4.1 A partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains
nodes.label: e:DirectDomConditon

nodes.name: Positivity on the complementary domain (12)
nodes.statement: 0 &< K'(x,t) \quad\mbox{for all $x \in \Delta' \setminus \Delta$.}
nodes.section: 4.1 A partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains
nodes.label: e:HamDomBasicCondition

nodes.name: Order of Hamiltonians implies domination of shells
nodes.statement: If $(K, \Delta) \leq (K', \Delta')$, then $(B_{K}, \eta_{K})$ is dominated by $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$. More specifically, given a contact shell $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ there is a shell $(B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!, \rho'})$ such that $$(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho}) \subset (B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!, \rho'})$$ the inclusion is a subordination map.
nodes.section: 4.1 A partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains
assumptions: $(K, \Delta) \leq (K', \Delta')$
conclusions: $(B_{K}, \eta_{K})$ is dominated by $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: If $C' \geq C$, then by \eqref{e:DirectDomConditon} we have $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}) \subset (B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!,\rho'})$ and it will be an embedding of almost contact structures whenever $$ \mbox{$\rho' = \rho$ \quad on \quad ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, B_{K,C} \subset B_{K',C'}$.} $$ If we pick the extension so that $$ \mbox{$\partial_v \rho'_{(x,t)}(v) > 0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{x \in \Delta, v \geq K(x,t) +C\} \cup {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{x \in \Delta' \setminus {\rm Int\,} \Delta\}$\,,} $$ which is possible on the latter region by \eqref{e:HamDomBasicCondition}, it follows that $\eta_{K'\!,\rho'}$ is contact on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, (B_{K'\!,C'} \setminus {\rm Int\,} B_{K,C})$ and hence the inclusion is a subordination map.
nodes.section: 4.1 A partial order on contact Hamiltonians with domains
nodes.statement_short: Extend $\rho$ to $\rho'$ increasing in $v$ outside $B_{K,C}$, which is possible by positivity, so the inclusion is a subordination map.

nodes.name: Contact isotopy generated by K
nodes.statement: Given a contact manifold $(M, \alpha)$ and a contact Hamiltonian $K: M \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}}$ let $\{\phi^t_K\}_{t \in [0,1]}$ be the unique contact isotopy with $\phi^0_K = {{\mathchoice {\rm 1\mskip-4mu l} {\rm 1\mskip-4mu l} {\rm 1\mskip-4.5mu l} {\rm 1\mskip-5mu l}}}$ and $$\alpha(\partial_t \phi^t_K(x)) = K(\phi^t_K(x), t).$$

nodes.name: Push-forward Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: For a contactomorphism $\Phi : (M, \alpha) \to (M', \alpha')$ define the push-forward Hamiltonian \begin{equation} \Phi_*K: M' \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{by}\quad (\Phi_*K)(\Phi(x),t) = c_{\Phi}(x)\,K(x,t)\,. \quad \end{equation} where $c_\Phi: M \to {\mathbb{R}}_{> 0}$ satisfies $\Phi^*\alpha' = c_\Phi\, \alpha$.

nodes.name: Push-forward Hamiltonian (13)
nodes.statement: \Phi_*K: M' \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{by}\quad (\Phi_*K)(\Phi(x),t) = c_{\Phi}(x)\,K(x,t)\,. \quad
nodes.label: e:ContPushK

nodes.name: Push-forward is conjugation
nodes.statement: One can verify $$ \{\Phi \phi^t_K \Phi^{-1}\}_{t \in [0,1]} = \{\phi^t_{\Phi_*K}\}_{t \in [0,1]} $$ so $\Phi_*$ corresponds with conjugating by $\Phi$.

nodes.name: Push-forward preserves boundary positivity
nodes.statement: It is clear that if $(K, \Delta)$ satisfies \eqref{e:KBoundary}, then $(\Phi_*K, \Delta')$ does as well.

nodes.name: Conjugation induces equivalence of circle models
nodes.statement: A contactomorphism between star-shaped domains $\Phi: \Delta \to \Delta'$ in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}})$ induces an equivalence of the contact shells $$ \widehat\Phi: (B_{K}, \eta_{K}) \to (B_{\Phi_*K}, \eta_{\Phi_*K}) $$ defined by $(K, \Delta)$ and $(\Phi_*K, \Delta')$.
assumptions: A contactomorphism between star-shaped domains $\Phi: \Delta \to \Delta'$ in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}})$
conclusions: induces an equivalence of the contact shells
nodes.label: l:PhiToTildePhi

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: For a given model $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ we will build a model $(B_{\Phi_*K,\tilde{C}}, \eta_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{\rho}})$ such that the two models are isomorphic as almost contact structures. For $\tilde{C} + {\rm min}(\Phi_*K) > 0$, pick a family of diffeomorphisms for $(x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$ $$ \phi_{(x,t)}: [0, K(x,t)+C] \to [0, c_{\Phi}(x)K(x,t) + \tilde{C}] $$ and define a smooth family of functions for $(x, t) \in \Delta \times S^1$ $$ \tilde{\rho}_{(\Phi(x), t)}: [0, c_{\Phi}(x)K(x,t) + \tilde{C}] \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad \mbox{by}\quad \tilde{\rho}_{(\Phi(x), t)}(v) = c_\Phi(x) \rho_{(x,t)}(\phi_{(x,t)}^{-1}(v)). $$ One see one $\tilde{\rho}$ satisfies the conditions in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoS1} to define $(B_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{C}}, \eta_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{\rho}})$ provided $$ \mbox{$\phi_{(x,t)}(v) = c_{\Phi}(x)(v - C)+ \tilde{C}$ \quad for \quad $(x,t,v) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{v = K(x,t) +C\}$.} $$ It follows by construction that the diffeomorphism $$ \widehat\Phi: (B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}) \to (B_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{C}}, \eta_{\Phi_*K,\tilde{\rho}}) \quad\mbox{defined by}\quad \widehat\Phi(x,v,t) = (\Phi(x), \phi_{(x,t)}(v), t) $$ is an isomorphism of almost contact structures.
nodes.statement_short: Build $\tilde\rho$ from $\rho$ via fiberwise diffeomorphisms scaled by $c_\Phi$ and lift $\Phi$ to an isomorphism of almost contact structures.

nodes.name: Scaling contactomorphism C_delta
nodes.statement: For $\delta \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{1\}$ observe the contactomorphism $C_\delta: {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \to {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ given by $$ C_\delta(u_1, \dots, u_{n-1},\phi_1, \dots, \phi_{n-1}, z) = \left(\frac{u_1}{\delta}, \dots, \frac{u_{n-1}}{\delta}, \phi_1, \dots, \phi_{n-1}, \frac{z}{\delta}\right) $$ maps $C_{\delta}(\Delta_\delta) = \Delta_{{\rm cyl}}$ where $\Delta_\delta := \{\abs{z} \leq \delta,\, u \leq \delta\}$.

nodes.name: Rescaled special Hamiltonians remain special
nodes.statement: Let $K:\Delta_{\rm cyl} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ a special contact Hamiltonian and define $$ K_{\delta}: \Delta_\delta \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{by}\quad K_{\delta}:= K + (\delta-1). $$ If $\delta < 1$ is sufficiently close to $1$, then $\tilde{K}_\delta:= (C_\delta)_* K_{\delta} : \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is also a special contact Hamiltonian.
assumptions: $K:\Delta_{\rm cyl} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ a special contact Hamiltonian
$\delta < 1$ is sufficiently close to $1$
conclusions: $\tilde{K}_\delta:= (C_\delta)_* K_{\delta} : \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is also a special contact Hamiltonian
nodes.label: lem:Scale

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: Provided $\delta$ is sufficiently close to $1$, it is clear that $$ \tilde{K}_\delta := (C_\delta)_* K_{\delta} = \frac{K \circ C_\delta^{-1}}{\delta} + \frac{\delta -1}{\delta} $$ satisfies items (i)-(iv) in Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam} with $\tilde{z}_D = z_D / \delta$. If $k: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is the special function for $K$, then let $\tilde{k}_\delta(u) := \tfrac{k(\delta u)}{\delta} + \tfrac{\delta-1}{\delta}$. Using that $k$ is special, computing for $a > 1$ and recalling $\delta < 1$, we see $$ a\,\tilde{k}_\delta(u/a) -\tilde{k}_{\delta}(u) < (a-1)\tfrac{\delta - 1}{\delta} < 0 $$ so therefore $\tilde{k}_\delta$ is special provided $\delta$ is close enough to $1$ so that $\tilde{k}_\delta(1) > 0$. Therefore item (v) in Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam} holds for $\tilde{K}_\delta$ with respect to $\tilde{k}_\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Check conditions (i)-(iv) directly and verify that the rescaled function $\tilde k_\delta$ is again special.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.8
nodes.statement: Consider an overtwisted disc $(D_{K}, \eta_{K})$ defined by a special contact Hamiltonian $K: \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$. For $\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]$, let $\Delta_\delta = \{\abs{z} \leq \delta,\, u \leq \delta\}$ and consider the family of contact Hamiltonians $$ K_{\delta}: \Delta_\delta \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{where}\quad K_{\delta}:= K + (\delta - 1). $$ Observe any neighborhood of $(\partial B_{K}, \eta_{K})$ contains a foliation $\{(\partial B_{K_{\delta}}, \eta_{K_{\delta}})\}_{\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]}$ provided $\varepsilon > 0$ is small enough. Furthermore, when $\varepsilon > 0$ is sufficiently small, Lemmas~\ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} and \ref{lem:Scale} give us a family of special contact Hamiltonians $\{\tilde{K}_\delta: \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}\}_{\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]}$ such that $\tilde{K}_\delta < K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ together with contactomorphisms $$ (\partial B_{K_{\delta}}, \eta_{K_{\delta}}) \cong (\partial B_{\tilde{K}_{\delta}}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_{\delta}})\,. $$ Therefore every neighborhood of $(D_{K}, \eta_{K})$ contains a foliation $\{(D_{K_{\delta}}, \eta_{K_{\delta}})\}_{\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]}$ of overtwisted discs.
nodes.statement_short: Shrink $K$ by constants to get nested shells $B_{K_\delta}$ and rescale them back to special Hamiltonians via Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3.

nodes.name: Embeddings of circle model shells
nodes.statement: Let $(B_{K, C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ be a contact shell structure for $(K, \Delta)$. For any other $(K', \Delta')$ there exists a contact shell structure $(B_{K', C'}, \eta_{K', \rho'})$ together with an embedding of almost contact structures $$ (B_{K, C}, \eta_{K, \rho}) \to (B_{K'\!, C'}, \eta_{K'\!, \rho'}). $$ If $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta'$, then the embedding can be taken to be an inclusion map.
assumptions: $(B_{K, C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ be a contact shell structure for $(K, \Delta)$
conclusions: there exists a contact shell structure $(B_{K', C'}, \eta_{K', \rho'})$ together with an embedding of almost contact structures
If $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta'$, then the embedding can be taken to be an inclusion map
nodes.label: lem:contain

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Since $\Delta'$ is star-shaped, there is a contactomorphism $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1})$ such that $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Phi(\Delta')$ and therefore by Lemma~\ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} without loss of generality we may assume $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta'$. Given the contact shell structure $(B_{K, C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$, pick any contact shell $(B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!,\rho'})$ subject to the additional conditions that \begin{equation} K'(x,t) + C' > K(x,t) + C \mbox{ for all $(x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$} \end{equation} and the smooth family of functions $\rho'_{(x,t)} : {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ for $(x,t) \in \Delta' \times S^1$ satisfy \begin{equation} \rho' = \rho \quad\mbox{on\quad ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, B_{K,C} \subset B_{K',C'}$}, \end{equation} where the latter is always possible since $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,}(\Delta')$. By \eqref{e:containCon} we have an inclusion \begin{equation} (B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}) \subset (B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!,\rho'}) \end{equation} and by \eqref{e:embed} it is an embedding of almost contact structures.
nodes.statement_short: Conjugate so that $\Delta\subset{\rm Int}\,\Delta'$, then choose $C'$ large and $\rho'=\rho$ near $B_{K,C}$.

nodes.name: Height condition (14)
nodes.statement: K'(x,t) + C' > K(x,t) + C \mbox{ for all $(x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$}
nodes.label: e:containCon

nodes.name: Matching condition rho' = rho (15)
nodes.statement: \rho' = \rho \quad\mbox{on\quad ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, B_{K,C} \subset B_{K',C'}$},
nodes.label: e:embed

nodes.name: Inclusion of shells (16)
nodes.statement: (B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}) \subset (B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!,\rho'})
nodes.label: e:inclusion

nodes.name: Embeddings that are subordinations force K' > K
nodes.statement: {\rm If the inclusion \eqref{e:inclusion} was a subordination map, then $$ \partial_v \rho'_{(x,t)}(v) > 0 \quad\mbox{ for all $(x,v,t) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{x \in \Delta\,, v \geq K(x,t) + C\}$} $$ which together with \eqref{e:containCon} and \eqref{e:embed} imply $K'(x,t) > K(x,t)$ for all $x \in \Delta$ since $$ K'(x,t) - K(x,t) = \rho'_{(x,t)}(K'(x, t)+C') - \rho'_{(x,t)}(K(x, t)+C) > 0 \,. $$ A similar argument shows why assuming $\Delta \subset \Delta'$ is not sufficient, since the conditions \eqref{e:containCon}, \eqref{e:embed}, and $\partial_v\rho' > 0$ on $\partial\Delta'$ imply $K'(x,t) > K(x,t)$ for all $x \in \partial \Delta \cap \partial\Delta'$}

nodes.name: Flow notation X^t
nodes.statement: Recall that star-shaped domains $\Delta \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$ are ones for which the contact vector field $Z = z \tfrac{\partial}{\partial z} + u \tfrac{\partial}{\partial u}$ is transverse to $\partial\Delta$ and we denote the flow of a vector field $X$ by $X^t$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain

nodes.name: Changing the domain of a circle model
nodes.statement: For any contact Hamiltonian $(K, \Delta)$ and star-shaped domain $\Delta'$ there is a contact Hamiltonian $(K', \Delta')$ such that $(B_K, \eta_K)$ dominates $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
assumptions: any contact Hamiltonian $(K, \Delta)$ and star-shaped domain $\Delta'$
conclusions: there is a contact Hamiltonian $(K', \Delta')$ such that $(B_K, \eta_K)$ dominates $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$
nodes.label: lm:changing-B

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement: For any neighborhood $U\supset \partial \Delta$ there is a contactomorphism $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1})$ such that $\Phi(\Delta') \subset \Delta$ and $\Phi(\partial \Delta')\subset U$. To see this first note without loss of generality we may assume $\Delta' \subset \Delta$ by replacing $\Delta'$ with $Z^{-N}(\Delta')$ for $N$ sufficiently large. After this reduction, the required contactomorphism is given by $\tilde{Z}^T$ for $T$ sufficiently large, where $\tilde{Z}$ is a contact vector field with ${\rm supp}(\tilde{Z}) \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$ and $\tilde{Z} = Z$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, Z^{-\varepsilon}(\Delta)$ where $\Delta \setminus Z^{-\varepsilon}(\Delta) \subset U$. Now pick $U \supset \partial \Delta$ to be such that $K|_{U \times S^1} > 0$, take the constructed contactomorphism $\Phi$ above, and consider the contact Hamiltonian $K' = \Phi^{-1}_*(K|_{\Phi(\Delta')})$ on $\Delta'$. It follows from Lemmas~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} and \ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} that $(B_K, \eta_K)$ dominates $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
nodes.statement_short: Squeeze $\Delta'$ into a collar of $\partial\Delta$ where $K>0$ by a contact isotopy and pull back $K$; conclude with Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2.

nodes.name: Argument for domination up to conjugation
nodes.statement: If we want to prove the contact shell $(B_K, \eta_K)$ is dominated by the shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$ then Lemmas~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} and \ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} instruct us to care about the partial order from Section~\ref{sec:PartialOrder} up to conjugation.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemma 4.1 (order gives domination) with Lemma 4.2 (conjugation gives equivalence).

nodes.name: Domination via conjugation criterion
nodes.statement: In particular it is enough to find a contact embedding $\Phi: \Delta \to \Delta'$ such that $(\Phi_*K, \Phi(\Delta)) \leq (K', \Delta')$ to prove $(B_K, \eta_K)$ is dominated $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$.

nodes.name: Somewhere negative Hamiltonians are minimal up to conjugation in dimension 3
nodes.statement: Let $(K, \Delta)$ be somewhere negative where $\Delta = [-1, 1]$. For any other contact Hamiltonian $(\widetilde{K}, \Delta)$ there is a contactomorphism $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0(\Delta)$ such that $(\Phi_*K,\Delta) \leq (\widetilde K,\Delta)$, and hence $(B_K,\eta_K)$ is dominated by $(B_{\widetilde K},\eta_{\widetilde K})$.
nodes.section: 4.3.1 Minimal elements up to conjugation in the $3$-dimensional case
assumptions: $(K, \Delta)$ be somewhere negative where $\Delta = [-1, 1]$
conclusions: there is a contactomorphism $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0(\Delta)$ such that $(\Phi_*K,\Delta) \leq (\widetilde K,\Delta)$
$(B_K,\eta_K)$ is dominated by $(B_{\widetilde K},\eta_{\widetilde K})$
nodes.label: lm:3-domin

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.7
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality assume $K(0) < 0$ and pick a $\delta > 0$ such that \begin{align*} K(z) &< -\delta \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [0,a]$ for some $a \in (0,1)$, and}\\ \tilde{K}(z) &> \delta \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]$ for some $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$.} \end{align*} For $0 < \sigma \ll 1$, pick a diffeomorphism $\Phi: [-1,1] \to [-1, 1]$ such that linearly $$ \mbox{$[-\sigma,\sigma]$ maps onto $[-1+2\sigma,1-2\sigma]$\quad and\quad $\pm [2\sigma, 1]$ maps onto $\pm [1-\sigma, 1]$.} $$ Since $(\Phi_*K)(\Phi(z)) = \Phi'(z) K(z)$ we can pick $\sigma$ sufficiently small so that \begin{align*} (\Phi_*K)(z) &< -\tfrac{1-2\sigma}{\sigma}\, \delta < \tilde{K}(z) & \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [0, 1-2\sigma]$}\\ (\Phi_*K)(z) &< 0 < \tilde{K}(z) & \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [1-2\sigma, 1-\sigma]$}\\ (\Phi_*K)(z) &\leq \tfrac{\sigma}{1-2\sigma}\, {\rm max}(K) < \delta < \tilde{K}(z) &\mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [1-\sigma, 1]$} \end{align*} and hence get that $\Phi_*K < \tilde{K}$.
nodes.section: 4.3.1 Minimal elements up to conjugation in the $3$-dimensional case
nodes.statement_short: Stretch the negative region of $K$ by a diffeomorphism of the interval so that $\Phi_*K$ falls below $\tilde K$ everywhere.

nodes.name: 3-dimensional simplification and higher-dimensional obstacle
nodes.statement: As a consequence of this lemma, the $3$-dimensional case simplifies by making Section~\ref{sec:universal} unnecessary and allows us to give an effective description of an overtwisted disc. It seems unlikely to us (though we do not have a proof) disc that the generalization of Lemma~\ref{lm:3-domin} holds when $\dim(\Delta_{{\rm cyl}}) \geq 3$. The immediate obstacle to adapting the proof is essentially that ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\Delta_{{\rm cyl}}$ is not a star-shaped domain in higher dimensions, while for $\Delta_{\rm cyl} = [-1, 1]$ we get two intervals which are star-shaped.
nodes.section: 4.3.1 Minimal elements up to conjugation in the $3$-dimensional case

nodes.name: Positive cone F_+ and its conjugation action
nodes.statement: Given a domain $\Delta\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}_{\rm st}$ let $$ F_+(\Delta) := \{K \in C^0(\Delta): {\rm supp}(K) \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta,\, K \geq 0\,, \mbox{ and } K \not= 0\} $$ and consider the action of ${\frak D}_0(\Delta):=\mbox{Cont}^c_0({\rm Int\,}\Delta)$ on $F_+(\Delta)$ given by $$ \Phi_*K :=(c_{\Phi} \cdot K) \circ \Phi^{-1} \quad\mbox{for $K\in F_+(\Delta)$ and $\Phi\in{\frak D}_0(\Delta)$} $$ i.e.\ the push-forward operation from \eqref{e:ContPushK}.

nodes.name: Disorderability of the positive cone up to conjugation
nodes.statement: If $\Delta \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}})$ is star-shaped, then for any two $K, H\in F_+(\Delta)$ there is a contactomorphism $\Phi\in{\frak D}_0(\Delta)$ such that $\Phi_*K\geq H$.
assumptions: $\Delta \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}})$ is star-shaped
conclusions: for any two $K, H\in F_+(\Delta)$ there is a contactomorphism $\Phi\in{\frak D}_0(\Delta)$ such that $\Phi_*K\geq H$
nodes.label: prop:disorder

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.8
nodes.statement: Without loss of generalize assume $\Delta$ is star-shaped with respect to the radial vector field $Z$ and that $K(0) > 0$. Pick a sufficiently small neighborhood $U \ni 0$ so that for some $T >0$: $$ \mbox{$\inf_U(K) > 0$\,, \quad ${\rm supp}(H) \subset Z^T(U)\subset{\rm Int\,} \Delta$\,, \quad and \quad $e^T \inf_U(K) > {\rm max}(H)$} $$ where $Z^t:{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ is the flow of $Z$ and satisfies $(Z^t)^*\lambda_{{\rm st}} = e^t \lambda_{{\rm st}}$. Let $\tilde{Z}$ be another contact vector field supported in ${\rm Int\,}(\Delta)$ and equal to $Z$ on $Z^T(U)$. It follows the contactomorphism $\Phi := \tilde{Z}^T \in {\frak D}_0(\Delta)$ satisfies $\Phi_* K \geq H$ since $$ (\Phi_*K)(x) = (c_\Phi \cdot K)(\Phi^{-1}(x)) \geq e^T \inf_U(K) \geq H(x) \quad\mbox{if $x \in {\rm supp}(H)$} $$ and $\Phi_*K \geq 0$ otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: Push a small neighborhood where $K>0$ by the Liouville-type contact flow $Z$ to cover ${\rm supp}(H)$; the conformal factor $e^T$ makes $\Phi_*K\geq H$.

nodes.name: Triviality of the order on conjugacy classes
