nodes.statement: Note that Proposition \ref{prop:disorder} shows that on the conjugacy classes of elements of the positive cone $\mathcal{C}:=\{f\in{\frak D}_0;\; f\geq\mathrm {Id},\;f\neq\mathrm {Id}\}$ partial order from \cite{EliPolt00} is trivial and it would be to understand for which contact manifolds the analog of Proposition \ref{prop:disorder} holds.

nodes.name: Obstruction to Proposition 4.9 from bi-invariant metrics
nodes.statement: As pointed out to us by L.~Polterovich, a non-trivial bi-invariant metric on $\mathrm{Cont}_0^c$ compatible with the notion of order on $\mathrm{Cont}_0^c$ from \cite{EliPolt00} provides an obstruction to Proposition \ref{prop:disorder}. For instance Sandon's metric \cite{Sandon} shows Proposition \ref{prop:disorder} does not hold for $D^{2n}_R\times S^1$ with contact form $dz+\sum_{i=1}^n u_id\phi_i$ where $D^{2n}_R$ is a $2n$-disc of a sufficiently large radius $R$.

nodes.name: Domination with shallow negative part
nodes.statement: Consider contact Hamiltonians $K_i: \Delta \to{\mathbb{R}}$ defining contact shells $(B_{K_i}, \eta_{K_i})$ for $i=1,2$. If there is a star-shaped domain $\tilde\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$ such that $$ K_0 \leq K_1 \mbox{ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\Delta \setminus {\rm Int\,} \tilde\Delta)$,} \quad 0 \leq K_1 \mbox{ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial \tilde\Delta$,} \quad \mbox{and}\quad K_0 \leq 0 \mbox{ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \tilde\Delta$} $$ with $K_0|_{{\rm Int\,} \Delta} \not\equiv 0$, then the contact shell $(B_{K_0}, \eta_{K_0})$ is dominated by $(B_{K_1}, \eta_{K_1})$.
nodes.statement_short: If $K_0\leq K_1$ near $\Delta\setminus\tilde\Delta$, $K_1\geq0$ near $\partial\tilde\Delta$ and $K_0\leq0$ on $\tilde\Delta$, then $B_{K_0}$ is dominated by $B_{K_1}$.
assumptions: there is a star-shaped domain $\tilde\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$ such that
with $K_0|_{{\rm Int\,} \Delta} \not\equiv 0$
conclusions: the contact shell $(B_{K_0}, \eta_{K_0})$ is dominated by $(B_{K_1}, \eta_{K_1})$
nodes.label: prop:shallow

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.9
nodes.statement: The assumptions ensure we can pick contact Hamiltonians $\tilde{K}_i: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$ defining contact shells $(B_{\tilde{K}_i}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_i})$ so that \begin{enumerate} \item $K_0 \leq \tilde{K}_0$ and $\tilde{K}_1 \leq K_1$, \item $\tilde{K}_0 \leq \tilde{K}_1$ on $\Delta \setminus \tilde{\Delta}$, and \item $-\tilde{K}_i|_{\tilde{\Delta}} \in F_+(\tilde{\Delta})$ for $i=1,2$. \end{enumerate} By item (i) and Lemma~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} it suffices to show $(B_{\tilde{K}_0}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_0})$ is dominated by $(B_{\tilde{K}_1}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_1})$. Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:disorder} to item (iii) gives a $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\rm Int\,} \tilde{\Delta})$ such that $$ \Phi_*(\tilde{K}_0|_{\tilde{\Delta}}) \leq \tilde{K}_1|_{\tilde{\Delta}}. $$ Together with item (ii) this means $\Phi_*\tilde{K}_0 \leq \tilde{K_1}$ where we think of $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\rm Int\,} \Delta)$ and therefore $(B_{\tilde{K}_0}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_0})$ is dominated by $(B_{\tilde{K}_1}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_1})$ by Lemmas~\ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} and \ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus}.
nodes.statement_short: Modify both Hamiltonians, then apply Proposition 4.8 on $\tilde\Delta$ to conjugate $\tilde K_0$ below $\tilde K_1$, and conclude by Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2.

nodes.name: Parametric shallow domination
nodes.statement: Assume that $\Delta \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ is a star-shaped domain. Let $\Delta' \subset \Delta$ be a smooth star-shaped subdomain and let $K^\tau: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$, $\tau\in T$, be a family time-independent functions satisfying $K^\tau|_{\Delta \setminus {\rm Int\,} \Delta'} > 0$. Suppose that $K^\tau>0$ for $\tau$ in a closed subset $A\subset T$. Then for any $\delta > 0$, there exists a family $\widetilde K^\tau$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde K^\tau=K^\tau$ on $\Delta \setminus {\rm Int\,} \Delta'$ and $\widetilde{K^\tau} > -\delta$, $\tau\in T$; \item $\widetilde K^\tau= K^\tau$ for $\tau\in A$ \item there exists a family of subordination maps $h^\tau: \eta_{{\widetilde K}^\tau}\to \eta_{ {K^\tau}}$ which are identity maps for $\tau\in A$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Parametric version of Proposition 4.9: a family $K^\tau$ can be raised above $-\delta$ inside $\Delta'$ via a family of subordination maps, unchanged where $K^\tau>0$.
nodes.label: prop:shallow-param

nodes.name: Time-independent spherically symmetric Hamiltonians
nodes.statement: All contact Hamiltonians $(K, \Delta)$ will be assumed time indepedent and spherically symmetric, i.e. functions $K(u,z)$ of only the $u$ and $z$ variables.
nodes.section: 5 Filling of the universal circular models

nodes.name: Translation Z_tau
nodes.statement: The contactomorphism of $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}})$ that is translation in the $z$-coordinate will be $$ \mbox{$Z_\tau : {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \to {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ \quad where \quad $Z_\tau(q,z) = (q, z +\tau)$} $$ using coordinates $(q, z) \in {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-2} \times {\mathbb{R}}$.
nodes.section: 5 Filling of the universal circular models

nodes.name: Radial Liouville form and flow
nodes.statement: Consider the ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n}$ with polar coordinates $(u_1, \varphi_1, \dots, u_{n-1}, \varphi_{n-1}, v, t)$ equipped with the radial Liouville form and vector field $$ \theta := \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} u_i\, d\varphi_i + v\, dt\,\quad\mbox{and}\quad L := \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} u_i \tfrac{\partial}{\partial u_i} + v \tfrac{\partial}{\partial v}. $$ and denote by $L^t:{\mathbb{R}}^{2n}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n}$ the Liouville flow.

nodes.name: Gluing disc
nodes.statement: A \emph{gluing disc} for a contact shell $(W, \zeta)$ is a smooth embedding $\iota: D \to \partial W$, where $D \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n}$ is compact domain, star-shaped with respect to $L$, and with piecewise smooth boundary such that $\iota^* \alpha = \theta$ for a choice of a contact form $\alpha$ for $\zeta$ in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial W$.

nodes.name: Reeb-flow Darboux embeddings Phi_pm
nodes.statement: Given contact shells $(W^{2n+1}_\pm, \zeta_\pm)$ with gluing discs $\iota_\pm: D \to \partial W_\pm$ such that $\iota_+$ preserves and $\iota_-$ reverses orientation, the Reeb flows define contact embeddings \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\Phi_+: D \times (-\varepsilon, 0] \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \iota_+(D) \quad\mbox{with} \;\Phi_+^*\alpha_+ = dz + \theta,\\ & \Phi_-: D \times [0, \varepsilon) \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \iota_-(D) \quad\mbox{with} \; \Phi_-^*\alpha_- = dz + \theta, \end{split} \end{equation} such that $\Phi_\pm|_{D \times 0} = \iota_\pm$.

nodes.name: Reeb-flow Darboux embeddings (17)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\Phi_+: D \times (-\varepsilon, 0] \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \iota_+(D) \quad\mbox{with} \;\Phi_+^*\alpha_+ = dz + \theta,\\ & \Phi_-: D \times [0, \varepsilon) \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \iota_-(D) \quad\mbox{with} \; \Phi_-^*\alpha_- = dz + \theta, \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:Darboux-gluing

nodes.name: Shrunken discs D(z)
nodes.statement: For $\ell > 0$ pick a smooth function $\beta: [-\ell,\ell]\to{\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that $\beta(z)=0$ for $z$ near $\pm\ell$ and denote $D(z):=L^{-\beta(z)}(D)$.

nodes.name: Abstract boundary connected sum
nodes.statement: Define the \emph{abstract boundary connected sum} to be the almost contact manifold \begin{equation} (W_+ \#_{T} W_-\,, \zeta_+ \#_{T} \zeta_-) := \Big((W_+, \zeta_+) \cup (T, \ker(dz+\theta)) \cup (W_-, \zeta_-)\Big)/\sim \end{equation} where \begin{equation} T = \{(p,z) \in {\mathbb{R}}^{2n} \times [-\ell, \ell]: p \in D(z)\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1} \end{equation} and one identifies $$ \Phi_+(p, 0) \sim (p, -\ell) \in T \quad\mbox{and}\quad \Phi_-(p,0) \sim (p,\ell) \in T\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Glue $W_+$ and $W_-$ along a tube $T$ of shrinking discs in the standard contact $\mathbb{R}^{2n+1}$ via Reeb-flow collars.

nodes.name: Abstract boundary connected sum (18)
nodes.statement: (W_+ \#_{T} W_-\,, \zeta_+ \#_{T} \zeta_-) := \Big((W_+, \zeta_+) \cup (T, \ker(dz+\theta)) \cup (W_-, \zeta_-)\Big)/\sim
nodes.label: e:ABCS

nodes.name: Tube T (19)
nodes.statement: T = \{(p,z) \in {\mathbb{R}}^{2n} \times [-\ell, \ell]: p \in D(z)\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}
nodes.label: e:Tube

nodes.name: Canonical gluing discs of circle models
nodes.statement: There are canonical gluing discs $$ D_{\pm} = \{ u \leq 1,\, v \leq K(u,\pm 1)\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n} $$ with maps $\iota_{\pm}: D_{\pm} \to (\partial B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ $$ \iota_\pm(q, v, t) = (q, \pm 1, \rho_{(q,\pm1)}^{-1}(v), t) \in {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times {\mathbb{R}}^{2}, $$ where $\iota_\pm(0, 0) = (0, \pm1, 0)$ are the north and south poles of $B_K$.
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells

nodes.name: Common end function E(u)
nodes.statement: For two contact Hamiltonians $K_\pm: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$ assume $E(u) = K_\pm(u, \pm 1)$ is well defined.
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells

nodes.name: Connected sum of contact Hamiltonians
nodes.statement: For any $\ell > 0$ and a smooth function $\beta: [-\ell, \ell] \to {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that $\beta = 0$ near $z = \pm\ell$, define the domain \begin{equation} \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta := Z_{1+\ell}^{-1}(\Delta) \cup T_{\beta, \ell} \cup Z_{1+\ell}(\Delta) \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \end{equation} where \begin{equation} T_{\beta, \ell} := \{u \leq e^{-\beta(z)},\, \abs{z} \leq 1\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \end{equation} and define the contact Hamiltonian $K_+ \#_{\beta} K_-: \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$ by $$ (K_+\#_\beta K_-)(u,z) = \begin{cases} (K_+ \circ Z_{1+\ell})(u,z)&\quad\mbox{on $Z_{1+\ell}^{-1}(\Delta)$}\\ e^{-\beta(z)} E(u) &\quad\mbox{for $(z,q) \in T_{\beta, \ell}$}\\ (K_- \circ Z_{1+\ell}^{-1})(u,z) &\quad\mbox{on $Z_{1+\ell}(\Delta)$} \end{cases} $$
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Join two translated copies of $\Delta$ by a thin tube and define $K_+\#_\beta K_-$ as $K_\pm$ on the ends and $e^{-\beta}E$ on the tube.

nodes.name: Connected-sum domain (20)
nodes.statement: \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta := Z_{1+\ell}^{-1}(\Delta) \cup T_{\beta, \ell} \cup Z_{1+\ell}(\Delta) \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells
nodes.label: e:ConnectedSumDomain

nodes.name: Tube domain T_{beta,ell} (21)
nodes.statement: T_{\beta, \ell} := \{u \leq e^{-\beta(z)},\, \abs{z} \leq 1\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells
nodes.label: e:domaintube

nodes.name: Connected-sum domain is star-shaped
nodes.statement: It follows from Example~\ref{ex:domain} below that $\Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta$ is star-shaped since it is contactomorphic to $\Delta\#_{\ell} \Delta$, which is star-shaped with respect to $Z = \tfrac{\partial}{\partial z} + L$, and hence $(K_+ \#_\beta K_-, \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta)$ defines an $S^1$-model contact shell $$(B_{K_+ \#_\beta K_-}, \eta_{K_+ \#_\beta K_-})$$ as in Section~\ref{sec:ContactHamShell}.
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1 (routine check)
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to check that we have the following lemma.
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Asserted as a straightforward check.

nodes.name: Connected sum of Hamiltonians realizes abstract connected sum
nodes.statement: The contact shell $(B_{K_+ \#_\beta K_-}, \eta_{K_+ \#_\beta K_-})$ is equivalent to the abstract connected sum $(B_{K_+} \#_T B_{K_-}, \eta_{K_+} \#_T \eta_{K_-})$ with tube $$ T = \{u \leq e^{-\beta(z)},\, v \leq e^{-\beta(z)}E(u)\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1} $$ where the connected sum is done at the north pole of $B_{K_+}$ and the south pole of $B_{K_-}$.
nodes.section: 5.1.2 Abstract connected sum of $S^1$-model contact shells
conclusions: is equivalent to the abstract connected sum $(B_{K_+} \#_T B_{K_-}, \eta_{K_+} \#_T \eta_{K_-})$
nodes.label: l:abstract=S1

nodes.name: Submanifolds W_pm
nodes.statement: Suppose in an almost contact manifold $(W^{2n+1}, \xi)$ there are disjoint codimension $0$ submanifolds $W_\pm \subset {\rm Int\,} W$ with piecewise smooth boundary such that $\xi$ is a genuine contact structure in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial W_\pm$.

nodes.name: Gluing discs iota_pm
nodes.statement: Assume the contact shells $(W_\pm, \xi)$ are equipped with gluing discs $\iota_\pm: D \to \partial W_\pm$ where $\iota_{\pm}^* \alpha = \theta$ for a contact form $\alpha$ for $\xi$ such that $\iota_+$ preserves and $\iota_-$ reverses orientation.

nodes.name: Ambient boundary connected sum
nodes.statement: For a smooth embedding $\gamma: [0,1] \to {\rm Int\,} W$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $\gamma(0) = \iota_+(0)$, $\gamma(1) = \iota_-(0)$, and $\gamma(t) \notin W_+ \cup W_-$ otherwise; \item $\xi$ is a genuine contact structure on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma$ where $\Gamma:=\gamma([0,1])$; \item $\gamma$ is transverse to $\xi$, \end{itemize} we can think of $(W_+ \cup {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma \cup W_-, \xi)$ as an ambient boundary connected sum of the shells $(W_\pm, \xi)$.

nodes.name: Ambient connected sum contains abstract connected sum
nodes.statement: Every neighborhood $(W_+ \cup {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma \cup W_-, \xi)$ contains the image of an almost contact embedding of an abstract connected sum $(W_+ \#_{T} W_-, \xi \#_{T} \xi)$.
conclusions: Every neighborhood $(W_+ \cup {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma \cup W_-, \xi)$ contains the image of an almost contact embedding of an abstract connected sum $(W_+ \#_{T} W_-, \xi \#_{T} \xi)$
nodes.label: l:Ambient=Abstract

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: The gluing discs $\iota_\pm:D \to\partial W_\pm$ extend to Darboux embeddings \begin{equation*} \Phi_\pm: D \times (\mp\ell-\varepsilon, \mp\ell+\varepsilon) \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \iota_\pm (D) \quad\mbox{with } \;\Phi_\pm^* \alpha = dz + \theta \mbox{ and } \Phi_\pm|_{D \times \mp \ell} = \iota_\pm \end{equation*} and moreover one can ensure $\Phi_+^{-1} (\Gamma)=0 \times [-\ell,-\ell+\varepsilon )$ and $\Phi_-^{-1}(\Gamma)=0 \times (\ell-\varepsilon,\ell]$. By the neighborhood theorem for transverse curves in a contact manifold, for $N > 0$ sufficiently large the embeddings $\Phi_\pm$ can be extended (after possibly decreasing $\varepsilon$) to a contact embedding $$ \Phi: \Big(D \times (-\ell-\varepsilon, \ell+\varepsilon)\Big)\cup \Big(L^{-N}(D) \times [-\ell,\ell] \Big)\cup \Big(D \times (\ell-\varepsilon, \ell+\varepsilon)\Big) \to {\rm Int\,} W, $$ whose image is contained in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\iota_+(D) \cup \Gamma \cup \iota_-(D))$ and such that $\Phi(0 \times [-\ell,\ell])=\Gamma$. Picking $\beta:[-\ell,\ell]\to{\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that the tube $$T= \{(p,z) \in [-\ell, \ell] \times {\mathbb{R}}^{2n} : p \in L^{-\beta(z)}D \} $$ is contained in the domain of $\Phi$, we can now use $\Phi$ to define the required contact embedding $(W_+ \#_{T} W_-, \xi \#_{T} \xi) \to (W,\xi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the gluing discs to Darboux charts and use the neighborhood theorem for transverse curves to embed the tube.

nodes.name: Standing special Hamiltonian with flat zone
nodes.statement: For the rest of this section we will let $(K, \Delta)$ be a special Hamiltonian associated to a special function $k: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ such that \begin{equation} \mbox{$K(u,z) = k(u)$ when $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D', z_D]$} \end{equation} where $z_D' \in (-1, z_D)$ is sufficiently close to $z_D$ and recall that $E(u) := K(u, \pm 1)$ is well-defined and satisfies $K \leq E$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Filling a connected sum of a shell with a neighborhood of an overtwisted disc

nodes.name: Flat zone of the special Hamiltonian (22)
nodes.statement: \mbox{$K(u,z) = k(u)$ when $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D', z_D]$}
nodes.section: 5.2 Filling a connected sum of a shell with a neighborhood of an overtwisted disc
nodes.label: e:special3

nodes.name: Shrunken Hamiltonian K' on Delta'
nodes.statement: For $\varepsilon' > 0$, define $$ K' = K - \varepsilon' \quad\mbox{and}\quad \Delta' = \{u \leq 1-\varepsilon',\, \abs{z} \leq 1-\varepsilon'\} $$ and assume $\varepsilon' > 0$ is small enough so that $K'|_{\partial \Delta'} > 0$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Filling a connected sum of a shell with a neighborhood of an overtwisted disc

nodes.name: Contact annulus (A, xi_A)
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} we can arrange the inclusion $$(B_{K'\!,C}, \eta_{K'\!, \rho}) \hookrightarrow (B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$$ to be a subordination map, so that we have a $(2n+1)$-dimensional contact annulus $$ ({\bf A}, \xi_{{\bf A}}) := (B_{K,C} \setminus {\rm Int\,} B_{K'\!,C},\, \ker \eta_{K, \rho}|_{{\bf A}}). $$
nodes.section: 5.2 Filling a connected sum of a shell with a neighborhood of an overtwisted disc

nodes.name: Model overtwisted ball (B, xi_B)
nodes.statement: Define the contact ball $({\bf B}, \xi_{\bf B}) \subset ({\bf A}, \xi_{\bf A})$ given by \begin{equation} {\bf B}:= \{(x,v,t) \in {\bf A} : z(x) \in [-1, z_D]\} \end{equation} and by design the $2n$-dimensional disc $(D_K, \eta_K) \subset (\partial{\bf B}, \xi_{\bf B})$ appears with the correct coorientation.
nodes.section: 5.2 Filling a connected sum of a shell with a neighborhood of an overtwisted disc

nodes.name: Model ball B (23)
nodes.section: 5.2 Filling a connected sum of a shell with a neighborhood of an overtwisted disc
nodes.label: e:ModelOtBall

nodes.name: Contact embeddings Theta_sigma
nodes.statement: Denoting by $\iota\colon \Delta \to \Delta \# \Delta$ the inclusion into the right hand factor, we will prove in Lemma~\ref{p:ContEmb}(i) below that there is a family of contact embeddings \begin{equation} \Theta_\sigma: \Delta \to {\rm Int\,}(\Delta \# \Delta) \quad\mbox{for $\sigma \in [0,1]$ with $\Theta_0 = \iota$} \end{equation} such that $\Theta_\sigma = \iota$ in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$ for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$ and $\Theta := \Theta_1$ satisfies $$(\Theta_*K' , \Theta(\Delta')) < (K \# K, \Delta \# \Delta).$$

nodes.name: Embeddings Theta_sigma (24)
nodes.statement: \Theta_\sigma: \Delta \to {\rm Int\,}(\Delta \# \Delta) \quad\mbox{for $\sigma \in [0,1]$ with $\Theta_0 = \iota$}
nodes.label: e:Theta

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.9
nodes.statement: It suffices to prove $(B_K \# {\bf B}, \eta_K \# \xi_{\bf B})$ is equivalent to a genuine contact structure, since it is dominated by $(B_{K_0} \# B, \eta_{K_0} \# \xi)$ if we pick $\varepsilon' > 0$ sufficiently small in the definition of $({\bf B}, \xi_{\bf B})$. By Lemmas~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus}, \ref{l:PhiToTildePhi}, and \ref{lem:contain} we can pick a family of contact shell structures on $(B_{K} \# B_{K}, \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho^{\sigma}})$ such that there is a family of contact shell embeddings \begin{equation} \widehat\Theta_\sigma: (B_{K'}, \eta_{K'}) \to (B_{K} \# B_{K}, \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}}) \end{equation} with $\widehat\Theta_1$ a subordination map. We can arrange that $\eta_{K\#K, \hat\rho_0} = \eta_K \# \eta_K$ and for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$ to have $$ \mbox{$\eta_{K\#K, \hat\rho_{\sigma}} = \eta_{K} \# \eta_{K}$ \quad on \quad ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota\{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$} $$ where $\hat\iota: B_{K} \to B_K \# B_K$ is the inclusion into the right hand factor. We can pick an isotopy $\{\Psi_{\sigma}\}_{\sigma \in [0,1]}$ of $B_K \# B_K$ based at the identity and supported away from the boundary such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\Psi_\sigma \circ \hat\iota = \widehat\Theta_\sigma: B_{K'} \to B_K \# B_K$\,, \item $\Psi_\sigma = \mathrm {Id}$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota\{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$\,, \mbox{ and} \item $\Psi_1(B_K \# {\bf A}) = (B_K \# B_K) \setminus {\rm Int\,} \widehat\Theta(B_{K'})$. \end{enumerate} Observe that a point in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_K \# {\bf B})$ is one of the following regions \begin{enumerate} \item ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_K \# B_K)$ where $\Psi_\sigma = \mathrm {Id}$ and $\eta_K \# \eta_{\bf B} = \eta_K \# \eta_K = \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}}$ \item ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota(\{z = z_D\})$ where $\Psi_\sigma = \mathrm {Id}$ and $\eta_K \# \eta_{\bf B} = \eta_K \# \eta_K = \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}}$ \item ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota(\partial B_{K'})$ where $\eta_{K}\#\eta_{\bf B} = \hat\iota_*\eta_{K'} = \hat\iota_* \widehat\Theta_{\sigma}^*(\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho^{\sigma}}) = \Psi_{\sigma}^*(\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}})$ \end{enumerate} This shows $\xi_{\sigma} := \Psi_{\sigma}^*(\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}})$ is a family of equivalent contact shells on $B_K \# {\bf B}$ with $\xi_0 = \eta_K \# \eta_{\bf B}$. We know $\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_1}$ is a contact structure away from ${\rm Int\,} \widehat\Theta(B_{K'})$, since $\widehat\Theta_1$ is a subordination map, and therefore $\xi_1$ is a genuine contact structure on $B_K \# {\bf B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $B_K\#{\bf B}$; Lemma 5.4 gives embeddings $\widehat\Theta_\sigma$ of $B_{K'}$ into $B_K\#B_K$ ending in a subordination map, and an isotopy $\Psi_\sigma$ transports the structure to a genuine one.

nodes.name: Shell embeddings Theta^_sigma (25)
nodes.statement: \widehat\Theta_\sigma: (B_{K'}, \eta_{K'}) \to (B_{K} \# B_{K}, \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}})
nodes.label: e:hatTheta

nodes.name: Fibered family of shells ^I zeta
nodes.statement: Let $({\bf B}, \xi)$ be the contact ball from \eqref{e:ModelOtBall} and let $({}^I B_K \# {}^I {\bf B}, {}^I \zeta)$ be the family of contact shells fibered over $I = [0,1]$ with fiber $(B_{K^{(s)}} \# {\bf B}, \zeta^s)$ over $s \in [0,1]$ where $$ \zeta^s = \eta_{K^{(s)}} \# \xi_{\bf B} \quad\mbox{ and }\quad (B_{K^{(s)}}\# {\bf B}, \eta_{K^{(s)}} \# \xi) \subset (B_{K^{(s)}}\# B_{K}, \eta_{K^{(s)}} \# \eta_K). $$

nodes.name: Local parametric filling
nodes.statement: The fibered family of contact shells ${}^I \zeta$ is homotopic relative to $$ {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{s = 0\} \cup \bigcup_{s \in [0,1]} {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_{K^{(s)}}\# {\bf B}) \subset {}^I B_{K}\# {}^I {\bf B} $$ through fibered families of contact shells on ${}^I B_{K}\# {}^I {\bf B}$ to a fibered family of genuine contact structures.
conclusions: The fibered family of contact shells ${}^I \zeta$ is homotopic relative to
nodes.label: p:LocalConnectSumDisc-param

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.3
nodes.statement: Inspecting the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:ConnectSumDisc} shows that it can be done parametrically. In particular we can get a family of contact shell embeddings $$ \widehat\Theta_\sigma^s: (B_{K'}, \eta_{K'}) \to (B_{K^{(s)}}\#B_K, \eta_{K^{(s)}\#K, \hat\rho_\sigma^s}) $$ and associated isotopies $\{\Psi_\sigma^s\}_{\sigma \in [0,1]}$ of $B_{K^{(s)}} \# B_K$, which lead to contact shell structures $$ \hat\zeta_\sigma^s := (\Psi_\sigma^s)^*(\eta_{K^{(s)}\#K, \hat\rho^\sigma_s}) \mbox{ on $B_{K^{(s)}} \# {\bf B}$} $$ that define a family of fibered contact shells ${}^I \hat\zeta_\sigma$ on ${}^I B_{K}\#{}^I {\bf B}$. It follows from the second part of Lemma~\ref{p:ContEmb} that \begin{equation} \Big((\Theta_\sigma)_*K', \Theta_\sigma(\Delta')\Big) < (K^{(s)}\#K, \Delta \# \Delta) \quad\mbox{if $s \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{0\}$,} \end{equation} and therefore we can arrange for $\widehat\Theta_\sigma^s$ to be a subordination map when $s \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{0\}$. With this set-up the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:ConnectSumDisc} shows we can ensure the family of fibered contact shells ${}^I \hat\zeta_\sigma$ is such that ${}^I \hat\zeta_0 = {}^I \zeta$ as well as \begin{enumerate} \item $\hat\zeta_\sigma^s = \zeta^s$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_{K^{(s)}}\# {\bf B})$ for all $s$ and $\sigma$, \item $\hat\zeta_1^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $s$, and \item $\hat\zeta_\sigma^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $(\sigma, s) \in [0,1] \times [0, 3a]$ for some $a > 0$. \end{enumerate} Pick any smooth function $$ f: [0,1] \times [0,1] \to [0,1] \quad\mbox{with}\quad f(\sigma, s) = \begin{cases} 0 & \mbox{ if $\sigma = 0$}\\ 0 & \mbox{ if $s \in [0, a]$}\\ 1 & \mbox{ if $s \in [2a, 1]$ and $\sigma =1$} \end{cases} $$ and define the family of contact shells $\zeta_\sigma^s := \hat\zeta_{f(\sigma, s)}^s$ on $B_{K^{(s)}}\#{\bf B}$, which represents a homotopy of fibered families of contact shells $$ \{{}^I \zeta_\sigma\}_{\sigma \in [0,1]} \quad\mbox{on}\quad {}^I B_K\# {}^I {\bf B}. $$ It follows from item (i) and the fact $f(\sigma, s) = 0$ if $s \in [0,a]$, that this homotopy is relative is the appropriate set. Observe that $\zeta_1^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $s \in [0,1]$, since either $s \leq 3a$ and $\zeta_1^s := \hat\zeta_{f(1,s)}^s$ is a genuine by item (iii), or $s \geq 2a$ and $\zeta_1^s := \hat\zeta_{f(1,s)}^s = \hat\zeta_{1}^s$ is genuine by item (ii). Therefore we have the desired homotopy between ${}^I \zeta = {}^I \zeta_0$ and a fibered family of genuine contact structures ${}^I \zeta_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Run the proof of Proposition 3.9 in the parameter $s$, using part (ii) of Lemma 5.4 near $s=0$, and reparametrize by a cut-off function $f(\sigma,s)$.

nodes.name: Order condition near s = 0 (26)
nodes.statement: \Big((\Theta_\sigma)_*K', \Theta_\sigma(\Delta')\Big) < (K^{(s)}\#K, \Delta \# \Delta) \quad\mbox{if $s \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{0\}$,}
nodes.label: e:Embed2

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.11
nodes.statement: Recall that $({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ is the fibered contact shell, which at the point $\tau \in T = D^q$ is given by $$ (B_{K_{0}^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# B, \eta_{K_{0}^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# \xi) $$ where $\delta: T \to [0,1]$ is a bump function that vanishes near the boundary. It suffices to prove $({}^TB_K \# {}^T{\bf B}, {}^T\eta_{K} \# {}^T\xi_{\bf B})$ is fibered equivalent to a fibered contact structure over $T$, since it is dominated by $({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ if we pick $\varepsilon' > 0$ sufficiently small in the definition of $({\bf B}, \xi_{\bf B})$. In the notation of Proposition~\ref{p:LocalConnectSumDisc-param} we have the identification $$ \zeta^{\delta(\tau)} = \eta_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# \xi_{\bf B} \quad\mbox{as contact shell structures on $B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# {\bf B}$} $$ and a fibered contact structure on $({}^TB_K \# {}^T{\bf B}, {}^T\zeta_1)$ with contact structure $$ \zeta^{\delta(\tau)}_1 \mbox{ on the fiber } B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# {\bf B}. $$ Since $\delta(\tau) = 0$ if $\tau \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial T$, the homotopy constructed in Proposition~\ref{p:LocalConnectSumDisc-param} when used fiberwise gives a homotopy between ${}^T\eta_{K} \# {}^T\xi_{\bf B}$ and ${}^T\zeta_1$ that shows they are fibered equivalent.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the model ball and apply the homotopy of Proposition 5.3 fiberwise via the bump function $\delta(\tau)$.

nodes.name: Main lemma: embeddings below the connected sum
nodes.statement: There is a family of contact embeddings for $\sigma\in[0,1]$ $$ \Theta_\sigma: \Delta \to \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta \quad\mbox{with $\Theta_\sigma = Z_{1+\ell}$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$} $$ based at $\Theta_0 := Z_{1+\ell}$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\left((\Theta_1)_*K' ,\Theta_1(\Delta')\right) < \left(K\#_\beta K, \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta\right)$ and \item $\left((\Theta_\sigma)_*K',\Theta_\sigma(\Delta')\right) < \left(E\#_\beta K, \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta\right)$ for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: There are contact embeddings $\Theta_\sigma$ of $\Delta$ into $\Delta\#\Delta$, fixed near the top, pushing $K'$ below $K\#K$ at $\sigma=1$ and below $E\#K$ for all $\sigma$.
nodes.label: p:ContEmb

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:ChangeNeck} that it suffices to prove this lemma when $\beta \equiv 0$ and this special case is proved in Lemma~\ref{p:ContEmb1}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\beta\equiv0$ by Lemma 5.7 and apply Lemma 5.9.

nodes.name: 3-dimensional case of the main lemma
nodes.statement: In the $3$-dimensional case, where $\Delta = [-1,1]$, this lemma essentially follows from Lemma \ref{lm:3-domin}.

nodes.name: Transverse scaling contactomorphism
nodes.statement: A orientation preserving diffeomorphism $h: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ defines a contactomorphism $\Phi_h$ of $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$ by $$ \Phi_h(u_i, \varphi_i, z) = (h'(z)u_i, \varphi_i, h(z)) $$ where $\Phi_{h}^{-1} = \Phi_{h^{-1}}$.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region

nodes.name: Push-forward under transverse scaling (27)
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.label: e:PushS

nodes.name: Transverse scaling of domains
nodes.statement: {\rm For our purposes $\Phi$ should be thought of as a way to manipulate the $z$-variable at the cost of a scaling factor on the $u$-variable, in particular we have a contactomorphism between domains in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$ $$ \Phi_h: \{ u \leq f(z),\, z \in [a,b]\} \to \{u \leq (h' \cdot f)(h^{-1}(z)),\, z \in [h(a), h(b)]\} $$ where $f: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$.}
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.label: ex:Scaledomain

nodes.name: Simplifying the neck region
nodes.statement: For every connected sum $(K \#_{\beta} K, \Delta \#_{\beta, \ell} \Delta)$, if $\ell' > \ell$ is sufficiently large, then there is a a contact embedding $$ \Phi: \Delta\#_{\ell'}\Delta \to \Delta\#_{\beta, \ell}\Delta \quad\mbox{with}\quad \Phi = Z_{\pm(\ell-\ell')} \mbox{ on } {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{\pm z \geq \ell'\} $$ such that $(\Phi_*(K \# K), \Phi(\Delta\#_{\ell'}\Delta)) \leq (K \#_{\beta} K, \Delta \#_{\beta, \ell} \Delta).$
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
assumptions: $\ell' > \ell$ is sufficiently large
conclusions: there is a a contact embedding
nodes.label: l:ChangeNeck

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.7
nodes.statement: Recall $E(u) := K(u, \pm 1) > 0$ with $K \leq E$ and pick a constant \begin{equation} 0 < C < \frac{{\rm min}(E)}{{\rm max}(E)} \leq 1. \end{equation} Pick a diffeomorphism $h:[-\ell', \ell'] \to [-\ell, \ell]$ with $h'(z) = 1$ on $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{\pm \ell\}$ and \begin{equation} h'(h^{-1}(z)) \leq C e^{-\beta(z)} \end{equation} which is possible provided $$ \ell' > \frac{1}{2C} \int_{-\ell}^{\ell} e^{\beta(z)}dz $$ Extend $h$ by translation to get a diffeomorphism $h: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ and consider the associated contactomorphism $\Phi_h: ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi) \to ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi)$ from \eqref{e:PushS}. This is the desired contact embedding for by \eqref{e:hprime} we have $$ \Phi_h(\Delta\#_{\ell'}\Delta) = \{u \leq h'(h^{-1}(z))\,,\,\, z \in [-2-\ell, 2+\ell]\} \subset \Delta\#_{\beta,\ell}\Delta\,. $$ To check the order on the Hamiltonians, it suffices to check on $\Phi_h(T_{\ell'})$ where we have $$ (\Phi_h)_*E(u,z) = h'(h^{-1}(z)) E(\tfrac{u}{h'(h^{-1}(z))}) < e^{-\beta(z)} E(u) = (K\#_{\beta}K)(u,z) $$ by \eqref{e:CE} and \eqref{e:hprime}.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.statement_short: Use a transverse scaling $\Phi_h$ with $h'$ small on the neck to squeeze the long neck $\Delta\#_{\ell'}\Delta$ into $\Delta\#_{\beta,\ell}\Delta$ below $K\#_\beta K$.

nodes.name: Constant C (28)
nodes.statement: 0 < C < \frac{{\rm min}(E)}{{\rm max}(E)} \leq 1.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.label: e:CE

nodes.name: Derivative bound for h (29)
nodes.statement: h'(h^{-1}(z)) \leq C e^{-\beta(z)}
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.label: e:hprime

nodes.name: Twist contactomorphism
nodes.statement: For $g \in C^\infty({\mathbb{R}})$ and $z_0 \in {\mathbb{R}}$, define $$ \Psi_{g,z_0}(u_i, \varphi_i, z) := \left(\frac{u_i}{1+g(z)u},\,\varphi_i - \int_{z_0}^z g(s)\,ds,\, z \right) $$ which is a contactomorphism between the subsets of $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$ $$ \Psi_{g, z_0}: \{1+g(z)u > 0\} \to \{1-g(z)u > 0\} $$ where $\Psi_{g, z_0}^{-1} = \Psi_{-g, z_0}$.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Push-forward under twist (30)
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:PushT

nodes.name: Twist of domains
nodes.statement: {\rm For our purposes $\Psi$ should be thought of as a way to manipulate the $u$-variable at the cost of a rotation in the angular coordinates, in particular we have a contactomorphism between domains in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$ $$ \Psi_{g}: \{u \leq f_2(z)\} \to \{u \leq f_1(z)\} $$ where $f_j: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}_{>0}$ and $g(z) = \tfrac{1}{f_1(z)} - \tfrac{1}{f_2(z)}$.}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: ex:domain

nodes.name: Twist function g
nodes.statement: Fix an orientation preserving diffeomorphism $h:{\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ and define $g(z) := 1 - \frac{1}{h'(h^{-1}(z))}$.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Composed twist-scaling contactomorphism Gamma_{h,z_0}
nodes.statement: It follows from Examples~\ref{ex:Scaledomain} and \ref{ex:domain} \begin{equation} \Gamma_{h, z_0}:= \Psi_{g,z_0} \circ \Phi_{h} : \{u \leq 1,\, z \in [a,b]\} \to \{u \leq 1,\, z \in [h(a), h(b)]\} \end{equation} is a contactomorphism of these domains in $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{{\rm st}})$.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Twist-scaling contactomorphism Gamma (31)
nodes.statement: \Gamma_{h, z_0}:= \Psi_{g,z_0} \circ \Phi_{h} : \{u \leq 1,\, z \in [a,b]\} \to \{u \leq 1,\, z \in [h(a), h(b)]\}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:Gamma

nodes.name: Gamma is a translation where h is
nodes.statement: Computing shows that $$ \Gamma_{h, z_0}(u_i, \varphi_i, z) = \left(\frac{h'(z)u_i}{1+(h'(z) -1)u}\,,\,\, \varphi_i - \int_{z_0}^z \Big(1 - \tfrac{1}{h'(h^{-1}(z))}\Big)\,ds\,,\,\, h(z)\right) $$ so if $h(z) = z + \tau$ on $z \in A \subset {\mathbb{R}}$ and $z_0 \in h(A)$, then $\Gamma_{h, z_0}$ is just translation \begin{equation} \Gamma_{h, z_0} = Z_{\tau} \quad\mbox{on}\quad \{z \in A\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Gamma is a translation (32)
nodes.statement: \Gamma_{h, z_0} = Z_{\tau} \quad\mbox{on}\quad \{z \in A\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:GammaZ

nodes.name: Factor h~ and push-forward formula for Gamma
nodes.statement: If we define \begin{equation} \tilde{h}(u,z) := h'(h^{-1}(z)) - \big(h'(h^{-1}(z)) - 1\big)u \end{equation} then for a contact Hamiltonian $H(u,z): {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ we have that \begin{equation} (\Gamma_{h,z_0})_*H(u,z) = \tilde{h}(u,z)\,\, H\!\left(\frac{u}{\tilde{h}(u,z)}, h^{-1}(z)\right). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Factor h~ (33)
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:PushTh

nodes.name: Push-forward under Gamma (34)
nodes.statement: (\Gamma_{h,z_0})_*H(u,z) = \tilde{h}(u,z)\,\, H\!\left(\frac{u}{\tilde{h}(u,z)}, h^{-1}(z)\right).
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:PushH

nodes.name: Family of diffeomorphisms h_sigma
nodes.statement: Pick a family of diffeomorphisms $h_\sigma: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ for $\sigma \in [0,1]$ such that \begin{equation} h_\sigma(z) = \begin{cases} z+(1-2\sigma)(1+\ell) & \mbox{ for $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, (-\infty, z_D']$}\\ h_\sigma'(z) \geq 1 & \mbox{ for $z \in [z_D', z_D]$}\\ z+1+\ell & \mbox{ for $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D, \infty) $} \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Diffeomorphisms h_sigma (35)
nodes.statement: h_\sigma(z) = \begin{cases} z+(1-2\sigma)(1+\ell) & \mbox{ for $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, (-\infty, z_D']$}\\ h_\sigma'(z) \geq 1 & \mbox{ for $z \in [z_D', z_D]$}\\ z+1+\ell & \mbox{ for $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D, \infty) $} \end{cases}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:defh

nodes.name: Contact embeddings Gamma_sigma
nodes.statement: Recall the contactomorphism $\Gamma_{h, z_0}$ from \eqref{e:Gamma} and define the contact embeddings \begin{equation} \Gamma_\sigma := \Gamma_{h_\sigma, 2+\ell}: \Delta \to \Delta\#_{\ell}\Delta \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$.} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Embeddings Gamma_sigma (36)
nodes.statement: \Gamma_\sigma := \Gamma_{h_\sigma, 2+\ell}: \Delta \to \Delta\#_{\ell}\Delta \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$.}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:GammaS

nodes.name: Gamma_sigma is translation near the top
nodes.statement: By \eqref{e:GammaZ}, we see $\Gamma_0 = Z_{1+\ell}$ and on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$ we have $\Gamma_\sigma = Z_{1+\ell}$ for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4

nodes.name: Gamma_sigma push K below the connected sums
nodes.statement: The family of contact embeddings $\Gamma_\sigma: \Delta \to \Delta \#_{\ell} \Delta$ for $\sigma \in [0,1]$ satisfy: \begin{enumerate} \item $(\Gamma_\sigma)_*K \leq E\# K$ on $\Gamma_\sigma(\Delta)$ for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$, and \item $(\Gamma_1)_*K \leq K\# K$ on $\Gamma_1(\Delta)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
conclusions: $(\Gamma_\sigma)_*K \leq E\# K$ on $\Gamma_\sigma(\Delta)$ for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$
$(\Gamma_1)_*K \leq K\# K$ on $\Gamma_1(\Delta)$
nodes.label: p:ContEmb1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.9
nodes.statement: By \eqref{e:PushH} we have $$ (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) = \tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)\,\, K\!\left(\frac{u}{\tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)}, h^{-1}_\sigma(z)\right), $$ where recall from \eqref{e:PushTh} that $$\tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z):= h_\sigma'(h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) - \big(h_\sigma'(h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) - 1\big)u \geq 1$$ where the inequality follows from $h'_\sigma(h^{-1}_\sigma(z)) \geq 1$ and $u \leq 1$. Bringing these two together, we have \begin{equation} (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, h_\sigma([-1,\, z_D'])\\ \leq k(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in h_\sigma([z_D',\, z_D])\\ K(u,z -(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D+1+\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} \end{equation} using that $h_\sigma$ is translations on the ends, while on the middle we have \begin{align*} (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) &= (\Gamma_\sigma)_*k(u,z) = \tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)\,\, k\!\left(\frac{u}{\tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)}\right) \leq k(u) \end{align*} using \eqref{e:special3} and \eqref{e:subscale}. To verify $(i)$, since $$ (E\# K)(u,z) = \begin{cases} E(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in [-2-\ell,\, \ell]\\ K(u,z-(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in [\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} $$ it follows from \eqref{e:GsK} and the inequalities \begin{equation} k(u) \leq K(u,z) \leq E(u). \end{equation} that it suffices to check $$ K(u, h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) \leq K(u, z-(1+\ell)) \quad\mbox{when}\quad z \in [\ell,\, h_\sigma(z_D')]. $$ Since $h_\sigma^{-1}(z) = z-(1-2\sigma)(1+\ell)$ here, this is equivalent to $$ K(u, z+2\sigma(1+\ell)) \leq K(u, z) \quad\mbox{when}\quad z \in [-1,\, z_D' -2\sigma(1+\ell)] $$ and this latter condition follows from Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam}. To verify $(ii)$, using \eqref{e:defh} we see \eqref{e:GsK} at $\sigma=1$ becomes $$ (\Gamma_1)_*K(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,z+(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [-2-\ell,\, z_D'-1-\ell]\\ \leq k(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in [z_D' -1-\ell,\, z_D + 1+\ell]\\ K(u,z-(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D+1+\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} $$ while by definition $$ (K\# K)(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,z+(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in [-2-\ell,\, -\ell]\\ E(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in [-\ell,\, \ell]\\ K(u,z-(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in [\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} $$ so $(ii)$ follows from \eqref{e:INEM}.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.statement_short: Compute $(\Gamma_\sigma)_*K$ piecewise via (34) and compare with $E\#K$ and $K\#K$ using the subscaling property of $k$ and the monotonicity of special Hamiltonians.

nodes.name: Piecewise formula for (Gamma_sigma)_*K (37)
nodes.statement: (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, h_\sigma([-1,\, z_D'])\\ \leq k(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in h_\sigma([z_D',\, z_D])\\ K(u,z -(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D+1+\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases}
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:GsK

nodes.name: Inequalities k <= K <= E (38)
nodes.statement: k(u) \leq K(u,z) \leq E(u).
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.label: e:INEM

nodes.name: Closed manifold Sigma
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a closed $2n$-dimensional manifold.

nodes.name: Semi-contact structure on an annulus
nodes.statement: A {\em semi-contact} structure on an annulus $C=\Sigma\times[a,b]$ is smooth family $\{\zeta_s\}_{s \in [a,b]}$ such that $\zeta_s$ is a germ of a contact structure along the slice $\Sigma_s:=\Sigma\times s$.

nodes.name: Construction of the almost contact structure of a semi-contact family
nodes.statement: If $\{\alpha_s\}_{s \in [a,b]}$ is a smooth family of $1$-forms with $\zeta_s = \ker \alpha_s$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Sigma_s$, then one gets an almost contact structure $(\lambda, \omega)$ on $C$ where $$ \mbox{$\lambda(x,s) = \alpha_s(x,s)$ and $\omega(x,s) = d\alpha_s(x,s)$.} $$
nodes.statement_short: Define $\lambda=\alpha_s$, $\omega=d\alpha_s$ slice by slice.

nodes.name: Semi-contact structures define almost contact structures
nodes.statement: It follows that every semi-contact structure on $C$ defines an almost contact structure on $C$ that equals $\zeta_s$ on $TC|_{\Sigma_s}$.

nodes.name: Semi-contact structure of immersion type
nodes.statement: Given a contact structure $\xi$ on $\Sigma\times{\mathbb{R}}$ and a smooth family of functions $\psi_s:\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ for $s\in[a,b]$, if we pick $\Psi_s: {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Sigma_s \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\mbox{graph } \psi_s) \subset \Sigma \times {\mathbb{R}}$ to be a smooth family of diffeomorphisms such that $\Psi_s|_{\Sigma_s} = \mathrm {Id} \times \psi_s$, then we can define a semi-contact structure on $\Sigma\times[a,b]$ by $\zeta_s := \Psi_s^*\xi$. Any semi-contact structure of this form will be said to be of {\em immersion type}.

nodes.name: Motivation for the term immersion type
nodes.statement: {\rm The term is motivated by the fact that on the boundary of each domain $\Sigma^{[a',b']}:=\Sigma\times[a',b']$ for $a\leq a'<b'<b$ the structure $\zeta|_{\partial \Sigma^{[a',b']}} $ is induced from the genuine contact structure $\xi$ by an immersion $\partial \Sigma^{[a',b']}\to \Sigma\times{\mathbb{R}}$. Of course, this is an immersion of a very special type, which maps the boundary components $\Sigma\times a'$ and $\Sigma\times b'$ onto intersecting graphical hypersurfaces. }

nodes.name: Saucer
nodes.statement: A {\it saucer} is a domain $B \subset D\times{\mathbb{R}}$, where $D$ is a $2n$-disc possibly with a piecewise smooth boundary, of the form $$B=\{(w,v)\in D\times{\mathbb{R}}:\; f_-(w)\leq v\leq f_+(w)\}$$ where $f_\pm:D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ are smooth functions such that $f_-<f_+$ on ${\rm Int\,} D$ and whose $\infty$-jets coincide along $\partial D$.

nodes.name: Border of a saucer
nodes.statement: Observe that every saucer comes with a family of discs $$ D_s=\{(w,v) \in D \times {\mathbb{R}}:\; v=(1-s)f_-(w)+s f_+(w)\} \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$} $$ such that the interiors ${\rm Int\,} D_s$ foliate ${\rm Int\,} B$ and the family of discs $D_s$ coincide with their $\infty$-jets along their common boundary $S=\partial D_s$, which is called the {\em border} of the saucer $B$.

nodes.name: Semi-contact structure on a saucer
nodes.statement: A \emph{semi-contact} structure on a saucer $B$ is a family $\{\zeta_s\}_{s \in [0,1]}$ of germs of contact structures along the discs $D_s$ for $s\in[0,1]$, which coincide as germs along the border $S$.

nodes.name: Semi-contact saucers are contact shells
nodes.statement: As in Section~\ref{sec:semi-holonomic} a semi-contact structure on a saucer $B$ defines an almost contact structure $\xi$ on $B$. Furthermore $(B, \xi)$ is a contact shell since $\zeta_0$ and $\zeta_1$ are germs of contact structures on $D_0$ and $D_1$ and the family $\zeta_s$ coincide along the border of $B$.

nodes.name: Hyperplane Pi
nodes.statement: In $({\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1},\xi^{2n+1}_{\rm st}= \{\lambda_{\rm st}^{2n-1} + vdt=0\})$ where $v := -y_n$ and $t:= x_n$, define the hyperplane $\Pi:=\{v=0\}$.

nodes.name: Characteristic foliation of Pi is the projection fibration
nodes.statement: Observe the characteristic foliation on $\Pi \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1},\xi^{2n+1}_{\rm st})$ is formed by the fibers of the projection $\pi: \Pi\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ given by $\pi(x, t)=x$ for $x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$.

nodes.name: Disc D and function phi
nodes.statement: Let $D\subset\Pi$ be a $2n$-disc and let $\phi:D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ be a smooth function such that $\phi>0$ on ${\rm Int\,} D\cap{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\partial D)$ and whose $\infty$-jet vanishes on $\partial D$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary function F
nodes.statement: Let $F: D \to {\mathbb{R}}$ be a function, compactly supported in ${\rm Int\,} D$, so that $\phi + F$ is positive on ${\rm Int\,} D$.

nodes.name: Saucer over a disc in Pi
nodes.statement: Define the saucer $B := \{(w,v) \in D \times {\mathbb{R}} : w \in D,\; 0\leq v \leq \phi(w) + F(w)\}$.

nodes.name: Graphs Gamma_{s phi}
nodes.statement: There is a natural family of diffeomorphisms between $D_s \subset B$ and the graphs $$\Gamma_{s\phi}:= \{v = s\phi(w),\;w\in D\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$$ whose $\infty$-jets coincide along the border.

nodes.name: Semi-contact structure sigma_phi
nodes.statement: Define $\sigma_\phi = \{\zeta_s\}$ to be the semi-contact structure on $B$ where $\zeta_s$ is the pullback of the germ of the contact structure on $\Gamma_{s\phi} \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}, \xi_{{\rm std}}^{2n+1})$.

nodes.name: sigma_phi is genuine when phi is positive
nodes.statement: Parametrize $B$ with coordinates $(w,s) \in D \times [0,1]$, so that $D_{s_0}=\{s=s_0\}$ and consider the map $$ \Phi: B \to {\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1} \quad\mbox{where}\quad \Phi(w,s) = (w, s\phi(w)). $$ If $\phi$ is positive everywhere on ${\rm Int\,} D$, then $\Phi$ is an embedding, and hence $\sigma_\phi$ is a genuine contact structure since it can be identified with $\Phi^*\xi_{{\rm st}}^{2n+1}$.

nodes.name: Domination of saucer shells
nodes.statement: Similarly for $2n$-discs $D' \subset D$ and associated semi-contact structures $\sigma_{\phi'}$ and $\sigma_{\phi}$ a contact shell $\sigma_{\phi'}$ is dominated by a shell $\sigma_{\phi}$ if $\phi' \leq \phi|_{D'}$ and $\phi|_{{\rm Int\,} D \setminus D'} > 0$.

nodes.name: Regular disc in Pi
nodes.statement: An embedded $2n$-disc $D \subset \Pi$ is called {\em regular} if \begin{itemize} \item the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $D \subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}, \xi_{\rm st}^{2n+1})$ is diffeomorphic to the characteristic foliation on the standard round disc in $\Pi$; \item the ball $\Delta:= D/\mathcal{F}$ with its induced contact structure is star-shaped.

nodes.name: Regular disc in a contact manifold
nodes.statement: An embedded $2n$-disc $D \subset (M^{2n+1}, \xi)$ in a contact manifold is {\em regular} if the contact germ of $\xi$ on $D$ is contactomorphic to the contact germ of a regular disc in $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Regular semi-contact saucer
nodes.statement: A semi-contact saucer is \emph{regular} if it is equivalent to a semi-contact saucer of the form $(B, \sigma_\phi)$ defined over a regular $2n$-disc $D \subset \Pi$.

nodes.name: Reduction to regular semi-contact saucers
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ a closed subset, and $\xi_0$ an almost contact structure on $M$ that is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$. There exists a finite number of embedded saucers $B_i\subset M$ for $i=1, \dots, N$ such that $\xi_0$ is homotopic relative to $A$ to an almost contact structure $\xi_1$ which is genuine on $M\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^N B_i$ and whose restriction to each saucer $B_i$ is semi-contact and regular.
assumptions: $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ a closed subset, and $\xi_0$ an almost contact structure on $M$ that is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$
conclusions: There exists a finite number of embedded saucers $B_i\subset M$ for $i=1, \dots, N$ such that $\xi_0$ is homotopic relative to $A$ to an almost contact structure $\xi_1$ which is genuine on $M\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^N B_i$ and whose restriction to each saucer $B_i$ is semi-contact and regular
nodes.label: prop:to saucers

nodes.name: Fibered saucer
nodes.statement: A domain ${}^TB \subset T \times D\times{\mathbb{R}}$ is called a {\it fibered saucer} if $T=D^q$ and it has a form $${}^TB=\{(\tau, x,v)\in T\times D\times{\mathbb{R}}: f_-(\tau,x)\leq v\leq f_+(\tau,x)\},$$ where $f_\pm:T\times D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ are two $C^\infty$-functions such that $f_-(\tau,x)<f_+(\tau,x)$ for all $(\tau,x) \in {\rm Int\,}(T \times D)$ and $f_\pm$ coincide along $\partial\left(T \times D\right) $ together with their $\infty$-jet.

nodes.name: Discs D^tau_s of a fibered saucer
nodes.statement: Every fibered saucer comes with a family of discs $$ D^\tau_s=\{(\tau, x,v): x\in D,\; v=(1-s)f_-(\tau,x)+sf_+(\tau, x)\} $$ where for fixed $\tau\in T$ the discs $\{D^\tau_s\}_{s \in [0,1]}$ coincide with their $\infty$-jets along their common boundary $S^\tau=\partial D^\tau_s$.

nodes.name: Border of a fibered saucer
nodes.statement: We call the union ${}^TS:=\bigcup_{\tau\in T}S^\tau$ the {\em border} of the fibered saucer ${}^TB$.

nodes.name: Fibered semi-contact structure
nodes.statement: A fibered semi-contact structure ${}^T\xi$ on a fibered saucer $B$ is a family $\zeta^\tau_s$ of germs of contact structures along discs $D^\tau_s $ for $s\in[0,1]$ and $\tau\in T$, which coincide along the border ${}^TS$.

nodes.name: Fibered semi-contact saucers are fibered shells
nodes.statement: A fibered semi-contact structure defines a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^TB$. In particular, any fibered semi-contact structure on a fibered saucer ${}^TB$ defines a fibered contact shell.

nodes.name: Regular fibered semi-contact saucer
nodes.statement: A fibered semi-contact structure on a fibered saucer $B$ is called {\em regular} if the saucer $(B^\tau,\xi^\tau)$ is regular for each $\tau\in{\rm Int\,} T$. More precisely a fibered semi-contact saucer ${}^T\zeta=\left({}^TB, {}^T\xi\right)$ is regular if there exists a regular $2n$-ball $D\subset\Pi$ and a $C^\infty$-function $\phi:{}^TD=\bigcup\limits_{\tau\in T}\{\tau\times D\}\to{\mathbb{R}} $ such that \begin{description} \item{-} $\phi$ vanishes with its $\infty$-jet along $\partial ({}^TD)$, and $\phi >0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial({}^T D)\cap{\rm Int\,} {}^T D$; \item{-} for each $s\in[0,1]$ the contact structure $\zeta_s$ is induced by an embedding onto a neighborhood of the graph $\{y_n=s\phi(\tau,x), \tau\in T, x\in D^\tau\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}_{\rm std};$ \item{-} the disc $D$ is regular.

nodes.name: Notation ^T sigma_phi
nodes.statement: Thus a fibered regular semi-contact saucer is determined by the function $\phi$, and we will denote it by ${}^T\sigma_\phi$.

nodes.name: Coordinates (v,t) on T^*I
nodes.statement: In this section the notation $(v,t)$ stands for canonical coordinates on the cotangent bundle $T^*I$.

nodes.name: Interval model contact shell
nodes.statement: For $\Delta \subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ a compact star-shaped domain and a contact Hamiltonian \begin{equation} K: \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{such that \quad $K|_{\partial \Delta \times S^1} > 0$ and $K|_{\Delta \times \{0\}} > 0$} \end{equation} we will build a contact shell structure, similar to the circle model, on a piecewise smooth $(2n+1)$-dimensional ball $$(B^{I}_K, \eta_K^{I}) \subset \Delta \times T^*I$$ which we will refer to as the \emph{interval model contact shell} for $K$.

nodes.name: Interval model Hamiltonian condition (39)
nodes.statement: K: \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{such that \quad $K|_{\partial \Delta \times S^1} > 0$ and $K|_{\Delta \times \{0\}} > 0$}
nodes.label: e:KBoundaryInterval

nodes.name: Ball B^I_{K,C}
nodes.statement: For any constant $C > - {\rm min}(K)$, define the domain $$ B_{K,C}^{I} := \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times T^*I : 0 \leq v \leq K(x,t)+C\} $$ which is a piecewise smooth $(2n+1)$-dimensional ball in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times T^*I$ whose diffeomorphism type is independent of the choice of $C$.

nodes.name: Boundary pieces of B^I_{K,C}
nodes.statement: Denote the boundary by \begin{align*} \Sigma_{K,C}^{I} &= \partial B_{K,C}^{I} = \Sigma_{0,K,C}^I \cup \Sigma_{1,K,C}^I \cup \Sigma_{2,K,C}^I \quad\mbox{where}\\ \Sigma_{0,K,C}^I &= \{(x,v,t): v = 0\} \subset \Delta \times T^*I\\ \Sigma_{1,K,C}^I &= \{(x,v,t): v = K(x,t)+C\} \subset \Delta \times T^*I\\ \Sigma_{2,K,C}^I &= \{(x,v,t): 0 \leq v \leq K(x,t)+C\,,\,\, (x,t) \in \partial(\Delta \times I) \} \subset \Delta \times T^*I\,. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Family rho and form alpha_rho for the interval model
nodes.statement: Now pick a smooth family of functions \begin{equation} \rho_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{for $(x,t) \in \Delta \times I$} \quad\mbox{such that} \end{equation} \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho_{(x,t)}(v) = v$ when $v \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{0\}$, \item $\rho_{(x,t)}(v) = v - C$ for $(x,t,v) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{v \geq K(x,t) +C\}$, and \item $\partial_v \rho_{(x,t)}(v) > 0$ for $(x,t) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(\Delta \times I)$ \end{enumerate} which is possible by \eqref{e:KBoundaryInterval}, and consider the distribution on $\Delta \times T^*I$ $$ \ker \alpha_\rho \quad\mbox{for the $1$-form}\quad \alpha_\rho = \lambda_{{\rm st}} + \rho\,dt. $$

nodes.name: Family rho for the interval model (40)
nodes.statement: \rho_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{for $(x,t) \in \Delta \times I$} \quad\mbox{such that}
nodes.label: e:FamilyRhoI

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.3 (by analogy)
nodes.statement: We now have the following lemma, whose proof is analogous to Lemma~\ref{l:CircleShell}.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Interval model is a contact shell
nodes.statement: The almost contact structure given by $\alpha_\rho$ defines a contact shell $(B^{I}_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}^{I})$ that is independent of the choice of $\rho$ and $C$, up to equivalence. If $K > 0$, then the contact germ $(\Sigma^{I}_K, \eta_K^{I})$ extends canonically to a contact structure on $B^{I}_K$.
conclusions: The almost contact structure given by $\alpha_\rho$ defines a contact shell $(B^{I}_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}^{I})$ that is independent of the choice of $\rho$ and $C$, up to equivalence
the contact germ $(\Sigma^{I}_K, \eta_K^{I})$ extends canonically to a contact structure on $B^{I}_K$
The almost contact structure given by $\alpha_\rho$ defines a contact shell $(B^{I}_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}^{I})$ that is independent of the choice of $\rho$ and $C$, up to equivalence
the contact germ $(\Sigma^{I}_K, \eta_K^{I})$ extends canonically to a contact structure on $B^{I}_K$

nodes.name: Contact germ on Sigma~^I_K
nodes.statement: Similarly, we also have a direct description of the contact germ $(\Sigma_K^{I}, \eta_K^{I})$ without the shell given by gluing together the contact germs on the hypersurfaces \begin{align*} \tilde\Sigma_{0,K}^I &= \{(x,v,t): v = 0\} \subset \Delta \times T^*I\\ \tilde\Sigma_{1,K}^I &= \{(x,v,t): v = K(x,t)\} \subset \Delta \times T^*I\\ \tilde\Sigma_{2,K}^I &= \{(x,v,t): 0 \leq v \leq K(x,t)\,,\,\, (x,t) \in \partial(\Delta \times I) \} \subset \Delta \times T^*I \end{align*} to form a contact germ on $\tilde{\Sigma}_K^{I} := \tilde\Sigma_{0,K}^{I} \cup \tilde\Sigma_{1,K}^{I} \cup \tilde\Sigma_{2,K}^{I}$.

nodes.name: Direct description of the interval model germ
nodes.statement: The contact germs on $\Sigma_K^{I}$ and $\tilde{\Sigma}_K^{I}$ are contactomorphic.
nodes.label: l:EasyIntervalGerm

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4 (by analogy)
nodes.statement: The proof is completely analogous to Lemma \ref{l:EasyCircleGerm}.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Interval model is given by a global immersion
nodes.statement: Notice one important distinction compared to the circle model: the contact germ on $\tilde{\Sigma}_K^I$ is defined by a global immersion of the sphere into $\Delta \times T^*I$ (piecewise smooth, topologically embedded at the non-smooth points). This property allows us to use the interval model as a bridge between regular contact saucers and the circle model.

nodes.name: Interval model dominates circle model
nodes.statement: For star-shaped domains $\Delta' \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$, let $K : \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}}$ be such that $K|_{\Delta \times 0} > 0$ and $K|_{\Delta\setminus\Delta' \times S^1} > 0$. For $K' := K|_{\Delta' \times S^1}$, the interval model contact shell $(B_K^I, \eta^I_K)$ dominates the circle model contact shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
assumptions: star-shaped domains $\Delta' \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$
$K : \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}}$ be such that $K|_{\Delta \times 0} > 0$ and $K|_{\Delta\setminus\Delta' \times S^1} > 0$
conclusions: the interval model contact shell $(B_K^I, \eta^I_K)$ dominates the circle model contact shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$
nodes.label: l:equiv12

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.5
nodes.statement: Fix a $C > -{\rm min}\, K$ and a $\rho$ as in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoI} that defines contact shell models $$ \mbox{$(B_K, \eta_{K, \rho})$, $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'\!, \rho})$, and $(B_K^{I}, \eta_{K, \rho}^{I})$.} $$ Take any $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $K|_{\Delta \times [-\varepsilon, \varepsilon]} > \varepsilon$ and consider the domain \begin{align} B_{K}^{\varepsilon} &:= B_K^I\setminus\left(\{v\leq\varepsilon\}\cup\{t\in[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\}\right) \cr&= \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times T^*I : \varepsilon\leq v \leq K(x,t)+C\,,\,\, \varepsilon\leq t\leq1-\varepsilon\}. \end{align} Note that $\eta^I_{K, \rho}$ restricted to $B_{K}^{\varepsilon}$ defines a contact shell $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K,\rho})$ that we will call the {\em keyhole} model, and it follows from \eqref{eq:keyhole} that $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K, \rho})$ is dominated by $(B^I_K,\eta^I_{K, \rho})$. It remains to show for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ the shell $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K,\rho})$ dominates $(B_{K'},\eta_{K'\!,\rho})$. Note that $(B_{K}^{\varepsilon}, \eta_{K,\rho}^\varepsilon)$ can be cut out of $(B_K, \eta_{K,\rho})$ by the same inequalities \eqref{eq:keyhole} where $(v,t)$ are viewed as coordinates $v=r^2$ and $t=\frac{\phi}{2\pi}$ on ${\mathbb{R}}^2$, rather then on $T^*I$. This embedding is shown on Figure \ref{fig:keyhole} and explains the term `keyhole'. \begin{figure}\begin{center} \includegraphics[scale=.5]{keyhole.pdf} \caption{The keyhole model inside $B_K$.} \end{center}\end{figure} For standard coordinates $(q, p) \in {\mathbb{R}}^2$ where $q = \sqrt{v}\cos(2\pi t)$ and $p = \sqrt{v}\sin(2\pi t)$, by the assumptions on $\rho$ in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoI}, the $1$-form on $\Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2$ defining $\eta_{K, \rho}$ can be written as $$ \alpha_\rho = \lambda_{\rm st} + \frac{\rho(v)}{2\pi v}(qdp-pdq) $$ and on $\Delta \times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{(q,0) \in {\mathbb{R}}^2: q \geq -2\delta\}$ is a genuine contact form for some $\delta >0$. Pick a smooth function $k: \Delta \to [-\delta, \infty)$ such that both $k(x) = -\delta$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial \Delta$ and $k(x) = K(x,0)$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Delta'$, and $$ \Gamma_k := \{(x, q, 0) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 : -2\delta \leq q \leq k(x)\} \subset B_K. $$ Consider a smooth isotopy $\{\psi_s\}_{s \in [0,1]}$ of $\Delta \times \{q \geq -2\delta,\, p = 0\}$ of the form $\psi_s(x,q) = (x, g_s(x,q))$, supported away from $\partial B_K$, and such that $$ \psi_1(\Gamma_k) = \{(x, q, 0) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 : -2\delta \leq q \leq -\delta\} \subset B_K. $$ Since this isotopy preserves $\alpha_\rho|_{\Delta \times \{p=0\}} = \lambda_{{\rm st}}$, it follows from a Moser-method argument (c.f.\ \cite[Theorem 2.6.13]{Gei08}) that $\psi_s$ can be extended to a contact isotopy $\Psi_s$ of $B_K$ supported in $\Delta \times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{(q,0) \in {\mathbb{R}}^2: q \geq -2\delta\}$. If $\varepsilon$ is small enough, then the contactomorphism $\Psi_1$ satisfies $\Psi_1(B_{K'})\subset B_K^\varepsilon$ and hence the keyhole model shell $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K, \rho})$ dominates the circular model shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K', \rho})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Cut the keyhole model out of both the interval and circle models, then isotope $B_{K'}$ into the keyhole by a contact isotopy obtained from a Moser argument.

nodes.name: Keyhole domain (41)
nodes.statement: B_{K}^{\varepsilon} &:= B_K^I\setminus\left(\{v\leq\varepsilon\}\cup\{t\in[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\}\right) \cr&= \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times T^*I : \varepsilon\leq v \leq K(x,t)+C\,,\,\, \varepsilon\leq t\leq1-\varepsilon\}.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.label: eq:keyhole

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.6 (by analogy)
nodes.statement: We also have the following parametric version of Proposition \ref{l:equiv12}, whose proof is analogous.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Parametric repetition of the proof of Proposition 6.5.

nodes.name: Parametric interval-to-circle domination
nodes.statement: Let $K^\tau : \Delta \times S^1 \to {\mathbb{R}}$ be a family of contact Hamiltonians such that $K^\tau|_{\Delta \times 0} > 0, $ and $K^\tau|_{\partial \Delta \times S^1} > 0$. If $\Delta' \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$ is a star-shaped domain and $K'^{\tau}:= K^\tau|_{\Delta' \times S^1}$, then the fibered shell $^{T}\eta^I_{{}^T\!K}$ dominates ${}^T\eta_{{}^T\! K'}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.label: l:equiv12-param

nodes.name: Regular saucers dominate interval models
nodes.statement: Let $\zeta = (B, \xi)$ be a regular semi-contact saucer viewed as a shell, then $\zeta$ dominates an interval model $\eta^I_K$ for some $K:\Delta\times I \to {\mathbb{R}}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.label: lm: saucer dom interval

nodes.name: Hamiltonians with prescribed boundary behavior
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta$ be a compact contact manifold with boundary with a fixed contact form. Suppose $h, g:\Delta\to\Delta$ are contactomorphisms that are the time $1$ maps of isotopies generated by contact Hamiltonians $H,G:\Delta\times I\to{\mathbb{R}}$ that vanish with their $\infty$-jet on $\partial\Delta$. If $h=g$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial \Delta$, then $h$ can be generated as the time $1$ map of a Hamiltonian $\widetilde H:\Delta\times I\to{\mathbb{R}}$ where $\widetilde H=G$ on $ {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial(\Delta \times I)$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
assumptions: $\Delta$ be a compact contact manifold with boundary with a fixed contact form

$h, g:\Delta\to\Delta$ are contactomorphisms that are the time $1$ maps of isotopies generated by contact Hamiltonians $H,G:\Delta\times I\to{\mathbb{R}}$ that vanish with their $\infty$-jet on $\partial\Delta$
$h=g$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial \Delta$
conclusions: $h$ can be generated as the time $1$ map of a Hamiltonian $\widetilde H:\Delta\times I\to{\mathbb{R}}$ where $\widetilde H=G$ on $ {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial(\Delta \times I)$
nodes.label: lm:boundary-behavior

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.8
nodes.statement: Denote by $h_t$ and $g_t$ the contact diffeotopies generated by $H$ and $G$. Pick a contact diffeotopy such that $\widehat{h}_t = h_t$ on $\partial\Delta$ as $\infty$-jets and $$ \widehat{h}_t =\begin{cases} g_t &\mbox{when $t \in [0,\varepsilon]$}\\ h_t &\mbox{when $t \in [2\varepsilon,1-2\varepsilon]$}\\ g_t \circ g_1^{-1}\circ h_1 &\mbox{when $t \in [1-\varepsilon,1]$} \end{cases} $$ Observe $\widehat{H} = G$ when $t \in [0,\varepsilon] \cup [1-\varepsilon, 1]$ if $\widehat{h}_t$ is generated by $\widehat{H}: \Delta \times I \to {\mathbb{R}}$. Hence without loss of generality we may assume $H = G$ when $t \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial I$. Since $h_t$ and $g_t$ are $C^\infty$-small on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta$, we can pick an isotopy $$ \psi^s: \Delta \times I \to \Delta \times I \quad\mbox{for $s\in [0,1]$ with $\psi^0 = \mathrm {Id}$} $$ supported in $\Delta \times {\rm Int\,} I$ and such that for $x \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta$ we have $$ \mbox{$\psi^s(\cdot, t)$ is a contactomorphism and $\psi^1(h_t(x), t) = (g_t(x), t)$.} $$ Applying the Gray--Moser argument parametrically in $t$ builds a contact isotopy $\tilde{\psi}_t$ such that $\tilde{\psi}_t = \mathrm {Id}$ when $t \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial I$ and $\tilde\psi_1(h_t(x)) = g_t(x)$ when $x \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta$. Defining $\tilde{h}_t:= \tilde\psi_t \circ h_t$ and $\widetilde{H}$ to be its generating contact Hamiltonian gives the result.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Make $H=G$ near $\partial I$, then correct $h_t$ near $\partial\Delta$ by a parametric Gray-Moser isotopy.

nodes.name: Saucers over general discs are equivalent to saucers over products
nodes.statement: For a star-shaped domain $\Delta\subset ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi_{\rm st})$ consider the disc $$D=\{(w,t)\in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}: \; h_-(w)\leq t \leq h_+(w)\} \subset \Pi$$ where $h_\pm:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$ are $C^{\infty}$-functions such that $h_-<h_+$. If $(B,\sigma_\phi)$ is a contact saucer defined over $D$, then it is equivalent to a contact saucer $ (\widetilde B,\sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ defined over $\widetilde D=\Delta\times[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.label: lm:two-saucers

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.9
nodes.statement: We can assume that $B=\{0\leq v\leq\Phi(w,t): (w,t)\in D\}$, where the function $\Phi $ is positive on ${\rm Int\,} D$ and coincides with $\phi$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D$, and hence $\partial B=D\cup\Gamma$ where $\Gamma:=\{v=\Phi(w,t): (w,t)\in D\}$. Given a point $w\in\Delta$, consider a leaf $\ell_w$ through the point $(w,h_-(w)) \in D$ of the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_\phi$ on the graph $\Gamma_\phi:=\{v=\phi(w,t): (w,t)\in D\}$ and let $(w', h_+(w')) \in D$ be the other end of the leaf $\ell_w$. This rule $f_\phi(w):=w'$ defines the holonomy contactomorphism $ f_\phi:\Delta \to\Delta$. Consider the diffeomorphism $G:D\to \widetilde D=\Delta\times[0,1]$ defined by the formula $$G(w,t)=\left(w,\frac{t- h_-(w)}{h_+(w)-h_-(w)}\right).$$ Since $\lambda_{{\rm st}} + vdt$ restricted to $D$ and $\widetilde{D}$ is $\lambda_{{\rm st}}$ and is preserved by $G$, it follows that $G$ extends to a contactomorphism $G:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\widetilde D$. The diffeomorphism $G$ moves the graph of the function $\phi|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D}$ onto a graph of some function $ \widetilde \phi:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\widetilde D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ whose $\infty$-jet vanishes on $\partial\widetilde D$. Pick any smooth extension $\widetilde \phi: \widetilde{D} \to {\mathbb{R}}$. The characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_{\widetilde\phi}$ on the graph $\Gamma_{\widetilde\phi} = \{v=\widetilde\phi(w,t): (w,t)\in \widetilde{D}\}$ is represented by $\tfrac{\partial}{\partial t} - X_{\widetilde\phi_t}$ where $X_{\widetilde\phi_t}$ is the contact vector field on $\Delta$ for $\widetilde\phi_t: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$ thought of as a contact Hamiltonian. It follows that the holonomy contactomorphism $f_{\widetilde\phi}:\Delta\to\Delta$, defined similarly to $f_\phi$, coincides with the time one map of the contact isotopy of $\Delta$ defined by $-\widetilde\phi:\Delta\times[0,1]\to{\mathbb{R}}$ thought of as a time-dependent contact Hamiltonian. According to Lemma \ref{lm:boundary-behavior} we can modify $\widetilde\phi$, keeping it fixed over ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D$, to make the holonomy contactomorphism $f_{\widetilde\phi}$ equal to $f_\phi$. Since the holonomy maps $f_{\widetilde\phi}$ and $f_\phi$ are equal, it follows that there is a diffeomorphism $F:\Gamma_\phi\to \Gamma_{\widetilde\phi}$ equal to $G$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{\partial\Gamma_\phi}$, mapping the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_\phi$ to the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_{\widetilde\phi}$, and with the form $$F(w,t,\phi(v,t))=(f(w,t), \widetilde\phi(f(w,t))) \quad\mbox{for $(v,t)\in D$}$$ for some diffeomorphism $f:D\to\widetilde D$. It follows that $F$ extends to a contactomorphism of neighborhoods $F: {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma_\phi \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma_{\widetilde\phi}$. Let $(\widetilde B,\sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ be a contact saucer over $\widetilde D$, where $\widetilde B=\{0\leq v\leq\widetilde\Phi(w,t),\, (w,t)\in\widetilde D\}$ for some function $\widetilde\Phi:\widetilde D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ that coincides with $\widetilde\phi$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\widetilde D$ and is positive on ${\rm Int\,}\widetilde D$. Note $\partial\widetilde B=\widetilde D\cup\widetilde \Gamma$ where $\widetilde\Gamma:=\{v=\widetilde\Phi(w,t),\, (w,t)\in\widetilde D\}$. Let us define a diffeomorphism $H:\partial B\to\partial\widetilde B$ so that $$ H|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D}=G\;\;\; \hbox{and} \;\;\; H|_{\Gamma}(w,t,\Phi(v,t))=(f(w,t),\widetilde\Phi(f(v,t))).$$ This diffeomorphism matches the traces of contact structures on the boundaries $\partial B$ and $\partial\widetilde B$ of the saucers, and hence extends to a contactomorphism between ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B$ and ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\widetilde B$ which can be further extended to an equivalence between the saucers $(B,\sigma_\phi)$ and $(\widetilde B, \sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Straighten $D$ to $\Delta\times[0,1]$ by a contactomorphism $G$, match holonomies of the characteristic foliations using Lemma 6.8, and extend the resulting boundary map to an equivalence.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.7
nodes.statement: By the definition of regular semi-contact saucer from Section~\ref{sec:saucers}, we may assume that $\zeta = (B, \sigma_\phi)$ where $B$ is defined over a regular domain $D\subset\Pi:=\{v=0\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ and $\sigma_\phi$ is given by a family of contact structures $\zeta_s$ on neighborhoods of graphs $D_s:=\{y_n=s\phi(w),\; w\in D\}$ where $\phi:D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ is a $C^\infty$-function supported in $D$ which is positive on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D\cap{\rm Int\,} D$. By the regularity assumption of $D$ the projection $\pi:D\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ is equivalent to the linear projection of the round ball and the image $\Delta=\pi(D)$ is contactomorphic to a star-shaped domain in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$. Choose a slightly smaller star shaped ball $\Delta'\subset{\rm Int\,} \Delta$ such that $\phi|_{{\rm Int\,} D \setminus {\rm Int\,} D'}>0$ where $D':=\pi^{-1}(\Delta')\cap D$. Note that the characteristic foliation on $D'$ is \emph{not} a regular foliation, rather it is diffeomorphic to the product foliation of the $2n-1$ disc and the interval. There exist functions $h_\pm:\Delta'\to{\mathbb{R}}$, $h_-<h_+$, such that $D'= \{(w,t);\; h_-(w)\leq t\leq h_+(w), \; w\in\Delta'\}\subset\Pi$. Choose a function $\phi':D'\to{\mathbb{R}}$ that defines an immersion type semi-contact saucer $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$ over $D'$ such that $\phi'\leq\phi|_{D'}$ and hence $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$ is dominated by $(B, \sigma_\phi)$. Hence, we can apply Lemma \ref{lm:two-saucers} and find a function $\widetilde\phi:\widetilde D:=\Delta'\times[0,1]\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which is positive near $\partial \widetilde D$ and such that the corresponding saucer $(\widetilde B, \sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ over $\widetilde D$ is equivalent to $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$. Let us rescale the saucer $(\widetilde B,\sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ by an affine contactomorphism of ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}_{\rm st}$ $$(z,u,\varphi, t,v)\mapsto \left((1+\delta)^2z, (1+\delta)^2u, \varphi, (1+\delta) t-\frac\delta2, (1+\delta)v\right)$$ for $\delta > 0$, to an equivalent saucer $(\widehat B, \sigma_{\widehat\phi})$ over the domain $\widehat D:=\widehat \Delta\times[-\frac\delta2,1+\frac\delta2]$. The notation $\varphi$ stands for the tuple $(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_{n-1})$ of angular coordinates. Note that $\Delta'\subset{\rm Int\,}\widehat \Delta$ and we may choose $\delta$ sufficiently small so that $\widehat\phi|_{{\rm Int\,}\widehat D\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widetilde D}>0$. Then the restriction $K:=\widehat\phi|_{\widetilde D} $ of the function $\widehat \phi$ to the domain $\widetilde D=\Delta'\times[0,1]$ defines an interval model shell $(B^I_K,\eta^I_K)$. It is dominated by the saucer $(\widehat B, \sigma_{\widehat\phi})$, which is equivalent to $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$, which is in turn dominated by $(B,\sigma_{\phi})$ .
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Shrink to a product-foliated subdisc, apply Lemma 6.9 to get a saucer over $\Delta'\times[0,1]$, rescale it, and read off an interval model.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.10 (by analogy)
nodes.statement: Similarly, one can prove the following parametric version of Proposition \ref{lm: saucer dom interval}.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Parametric repetition of the proof of Proposition 6.7.

nodes.name: Fibered regular saucers dominate interval models
nodes.statement: Let ${}^T\zeta=({}^TB,{}^T\xi)$ be a fibered regular semi-contact saucer. Then ${}^T\zeta$ dominates a fibered interval model ${}^T\eta^I_K$ for some $K:\left({}^T \Delta\right)\times I \to {\mathbb{R}}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.label: lm:saucer-dom-interval-param

nodes.name: Degeneration of fibered saucers at the boundary
nodes.statement: {\rm Let us point out that the shells $(B^\tau, \xi^\tau)$ degenerate when $\tau$ approaches $\partial T$. Hence, the subordination map $({}^TB^I_K,{}^T\eta^I_K)\to ({}^TB,{}^T\xi)$ has to cover an embedding $T\to{\rm Int\,} T$. }
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells

nodes.name: Regular saucers dominate circle models
nodes.statement: If $(B, \xi) = \sigma_\phi$ is a regular semi-contact saucer viewed as a shell, then there is a time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$ such that $(B, \xi)$ dominates the circle model contact shell $(B_K, \eta_K)$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
assumptions: $(B, \xi) = \sigma_\phi$ is a regular semi-contact saucer viewed as a shell
conclusions: there is a time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$ such that $(B, \xi)$ dominates the circle model contact shell $(B_K, \eta_K)$
nodes.label: prop:saucer-to-circle

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.12
nodes.statement: We first use Proposition \ref{lm: saucer dom interval} to find a dominated by $\zeta$ interval model $\eta^I_{\widetilde K}$ for some ${\widetilde K}:D\times I \to {\mathbb{R}}$. Then, we apply Proposition \ref{l:equiv12} to get a circular model contact shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$ dominated by $\left(B^I_{\widetilde K}, \eta^I_{\widetilde K}\right))$. Finally, choosing a time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K<K'$ and applying Lemma \ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} we get the required circle model contact shell $\left(B_K, \eta_K\right)$ dominated by $ (B, \xi)$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Chain Proposition 6.7, Proposition 6.5 and Lemma 4.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.13
nodes.statement: Similarly, the parametric versions Propositions~\ref{lm:saucer-dom-interval-param} and \ref{l:equiv12-param} prove the following.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Chain Propositions 6.10 and 6.6 as in the proof of Proposition 6.12.

nodes.name: Fibered regular saucers dominate circle models
nodes.statement: Let $({}^TB, {}^T\xi)$ be a fibered regular semi-contact saucer, then there exists a family of time-independent contact Hamiltonians $K^\tau:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$ for $\tau\in T$ which satisfy $K_\tau>0$ for $\tau\in \partial T$, such that $({}^TB, {}^T\xi)$ dominates the corresponding fibered circle model contact shell $({}^TB_K, {}^T\eta_K)$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.label: prop:saucer-to-circle-param

nodes.name: Spaces Cont(M;A,xi_0) and cont(M;A,xi_0)
nodes.statement: Given a $(2n+1)$-dimensional manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, a closet subset $A\subset M$ and a contact structure $\xi_0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$ define $\mathfrak{Cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$ to be the space of contact structures on $M$ that coincide with $\xi_0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A$ and $\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$ to be the space of {\em almost} contact structures that agree with $\xi_0$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers

nodes.name: Inclusion map j (open case)
nodes.statement: Let $j:\mathfrak{Cont}(M;A,\xi_0)\to\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$ be the inclusion map.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers

nodes.name: Relatively open pair
nodes.statement: We say that the pair $(M,A)$ is {\em relatively open} if for any point $x\in M\setminus A$ either there exists a path in $M\setminus A$ connecting $x$ with a boundary point of $M$, or a proper path $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M\setminus A$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers

nodes.name: Gromov's h-principle for contact structures on open manifolds
nodes.statement: {\rm[M. Gromov, \cite{Gro69,Gr-PDR}]} Let $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ a closed subset, and $\xi_0$ a contact structure on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$. Suppose that $(M,A)$ is relatively open. Then the inclusion $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}(M;A,\xi_0)\to\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$$ is a homotopy equivalence.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
