assumptions: $M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold, $A\subset M$ a closed subset, and $\xi_0$ a contact structure on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A\subset M$
$(M,A)$ is relatively open
conclusions: the inclusion $$j:\mathfrak{Cont}(M;A,\xi_0)\to\mathfrak{cont}(M;A,\xi_0)$$ is a homotopy equivalence
also_stated_at: In 1969 M.~Gromov \cite{Gro69} proved a parametric $h$-principle for contact structures on an {\em open} manifold $M$: {\it any almost contact structure is homotopic to a genuine one, and two contact structures are homotopic if they are homotopic as almost contact structures, } see Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open} below for a more precise formulation of Gromov's theorem.
nodes.label: thm:Gromov-open

nodes.name: Semi-contact annuli reduce to regular saucers
nodes.statement: For a closed manifold $\Sigma$, any semi-contact structure $\xi=\{\zeta_s\}$ on the annulus $C=\Sigma\times[0,1]$ is homotopic relative ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial C$ to an almost contact structure $\widetilde \xi$ which is a genuine contact structure in the complement of finitely many saucers $B_1,\dots, B_k\subset C$ and such that the restriction $\widetilde\xi|_{B_j}$ for $j=1,\dots, k$, is semi-contact and regular.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.label: lm:annuli-to-saucers

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement: Choose an embedded annulus $C=S^{2n}\times[0,1]\subset M\setminus A$ and first use the existence part of Gromov's $h$-principle \ref{thm:Gromov-open}, to deform $\xi_0$ relative to $A$ to an almost contact structure which is genuine on $M\setminus C$. Next with use the $1$-parametric part of Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open}, applied to the family of neighborhoods of spheres $S^{2n}\times t$ for $t\in[0,1]$ to make the almost contact structure semi-contact on $C$. Finally we use Lemma \ref{lm:annuli-to-saucers} to complete the proof.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Use Gromov's h-principle to make the structure genuine off an annulus and semi-contact on it, then apply Lemma 7.2.

nodes.name: Partition into immersion-type annuli
nodes.statement: For a closed manifold $\Sigma$ and a semi-contact structure $\{\zeta_s\}$ on $\Sigma\times[0,1]$ there exists $N>0$ such that the restriction of $\{\zeta_s\}$ to $ \Sigma\times[a_i,a_{i+1}]$ for $a_i:=a+ \frac iN$ is of immersion type for each $i=0,\dots, N-1$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.label: lm:partition-to-special

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.3
nodes.statement: Choose $\varepsilon>0$ such that the contact structure $\zeta_s$ is defined on $\Sigma\times[s-\varepsilon,s+\varepsilon]$ for each $s\in[a,b]$. We will view $\zeta_s$ as a family of contact structures on $\Sigma\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$. For each $s_0$ and $\sigma > 0$ sufficiently small, a Darboux-Moser type argument implies there is an isotopy $\phi^{s_0}_s: \Sigma \times [-\sigma, \sigma] \to \Sigma \times [-\varepsilon, \varepsilon]$ such that $\phi^{s_0}_{s_0} = \mathrm {Id}$ and $(\phi^{s}_{s_0})^*\zeta_s = \zeta_{s_0}$ for $s \in [s_0, s_0+\sigma]$. Moreover by shrinking $\sigma$ if necessary we can ensure that the hypersurfaces $\phi_{s_0}^s(\Sigma\times 0)$ are graphical in $\Sigma\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$. Hence for any $s_0\in[a,b]$ the restriction of $\zeta_s$ to $[s_0, s_0+\sigma]$ is of immersion type and therefore choosing $N>\frac1\sigma$ we get the required partition of $\Sigma\times[a,b]$ into the annuli of immersion type.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: A Darboux-Moser argument makes short sub-annuli of immersion type; compactness gives a uniform partition.

nodes.name: Reeb trick: normal form for semi-contact annuli
nodes.statement: Let $\{\xi_s\}$ be a semi-contact structure on $\Sigma\times[0,1]$. Then, after partitioning, $\{\xi_s\}$ is equivalent to a semi-contact structure $\{\zeta_s\}$ which is immersion type satisfying the following properties. There exists a smooth function $\psi:\Sigma\to [-\frac R2,\frac R2]$ and a contact structure $\mu$ on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ such that \begin{itemize} \item the germ of contact structure $\zeta_s = \Psi_s^*\mu$ on $\Sigma\times[s-\delta, s+\delta]$ where $$ \Psi_s: \Sigma\times[s-\delta, s+\delta] \to \Sigma\times[-R,R] \quad $$ by the embedding $(x,s+t)\mapsto (x, s\psi(x)+t)\in\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ where $x\in\Sigma$ and $t\in[-\delta,\delta]$; \item there are closed domains $V\subset\Sigma$ and $\widehat V\subset {\rm Int\,} V$ such that $\psi|_V >0$, and the contact structure $\mu$ is transverse to graphs of functions $s\psi $ over $\widehat W=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,}\widehat V$ for all $s\in[0,1]$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.label: lm:Reeb-trick

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4
nodes.statement: Let us endow $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ with the product metric. Using Lemma \ref{lm:partition-to-special} we may assume, by passing to a partition, that the semi-contact structure $\{\xi_s\}$ on the annulus $C$ is of immersion type. So there is a contact structure $\mu$ on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ and a smooth family of embeddings $$\Psi_s: \widehat{C}:=\Sigma \times [-\delta, \delta] \to \Sigma\times[-R,R] \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$}$$ such that $\Psi_s(x, u) = (x, \psi_s(x)+u)$ for $u\in[-\delta,\delta]$, and $\Psi_s^*\mu$ is identified with $\zeta_s$. Furthermore, the partition argument also allows us to assume that $\psi_0=0$ and that the $C^1$-norm of $\psi_1$ is arbitrary small. We will impose the appropriate bound on its $C^1$-norm further down in the proof. Define a subset \begin{align*} \widehat V&:=\left\{x\in\Sigma: \mbox{ the angle between } \mu_{x,0} \hbox{ and } T_{x,0}\Sigma \;\hbox {in $T_{x,0}\widehat{C}$ is at most } \tfrac\pi4\right\}.\\ \end{align*} Assuming $\mu$ and $\Sigma$ cooriented, we present $\widehat V$ as a disjoint union $\widehat V=\widehat V_+\cup \widehat V_-$ defined by whether the vector field $\frac{\partial}{\partial u}$ defines the same or opposite coorientation of $\mu|_\Sigma $ and $T\Sigma$. We can choose a contact form $\alpha$ for $\mu$ such that its Reeb vector field $\frak{R}$ satisfies $\frak{R}(x,u)=\pm\frac{\partial}{\partial u}$ for $x\in\widehat V_\pm$ and $u\leq\sigma$ for a sufficiently small $\sigma>0$. We will assume $\sigma>0$ small enough to also ensure that $$\abs{\mbox{angle}(\mu_{x,u},\mu_{x,0}) } \leq \tfrac{ \pi}{16}$$ for $x\in\Sigma$ and $|u|\leq\sigma$. Consider any smooth function $H:\Sigma\to[-1,1]$ equal to $\pm 1$ on $\widehat V_{\pm}$. We further extend this function to $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ as independent of the coordinate $u$ and then multiply by the cut-off function $\beta(u)$ equal to $1$ on $[-\frac R3,\frac R3]$ and equal to $0$ outside $[-\frac R2,\frac R2]$. We will keep the notation $H$ for the resulting function on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$. Let $h_t:\Sigma\times[-R,R]\to\Sigma\times[-R,R]$. $t\in[0,1]$, be the contact isotopy generated by $H$ as its contact Hamiltonian. Choose $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac\sigma2)$ so small that $dh_\varepsilon$ rotates any hyperplane by an angle $<\frac\pi{16}$ and $||h_\varepsilon||_{C^0}<\sigma$. Then $\Gamma_\varepsilon:=h_\varepsilon(\Sigma\times0)$ is graphical, $\Gamma_\varepsilon=\{u=\phi_\varepsilon(x)\}$ for a function $\phi_\varepsilon:\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which satisfies the following conditions \begin{itemize} \item $\phi_\varepsilon|_{\widehat V}=\varepsilon$; \item for every $x\in\widehat W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widehat V$ we have ${\mathrm{angle}}(T_{z}\Sigma,\mu_z)>\frac\pi8$, $z=(x,\phi_\varepsilon(x))\in\Gamma_\varepsilon$. \end{itemize} As it was explained above, the function $\psi_1\colon\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ entering the definition of the semi-contact annulus can be chosen arbitrarily $C^1$-small. Hence, by requiring it to satisfy the conditions $|\psi_1|< \frac\varepsilon2$ and $||\psi_1||_{C^1}<\tan\frac\pi{16}$ we can conclude that $\widetilde\Gamma :=h_\varepsilon(\{u= \psi_1(x),\,x\in\Sigma\})$ is graphical, $\widetilde\Gamma =\{u= \widetilde\psi_1 (x)\}$ for a function $\widetilde\psi_1:\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which satisfies the following conditions \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde\psi_1|_{\widehat V}\geq\frac\varepsilon2$; \item for every $x\in \widehat W=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widehat V$ and $s\in[0,1]$ we have $${\mathrm{angle}}(T_{z}\widetilde\Sigma_s,\mu_z)>\frac\pi{16},\;\;z=(x,s\widetilde\psi_1(x))\in\widetilde\Gamma_s= \{u= s\widetilde\psi_1 (x)\}.$$ \end{itemize} Let us denote $ V:=\{\widetilde\psi_1 \geq\frac\varepsilon4\}$, so that $\widehat V\subset{\rm Int\,} V$. Note that the family of contact structures $\widetilde\zeta_s$ on $\Sigma\times s\subset\Sigma\times[0,1]$ induced by $\mu$ on the neighborhoods of graphs $\Gamma_s$ of functions $ s\widetilde\psi$ defines a semi-contact structure $\{\zeta_s\}$ which is equivalent to $\{\xi_s\}$. This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{lm:Reeb-trick}.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: After partitioning, push $\Sigma$ by a contact isotopy generated by a Hamiltonian $\pm1$ on the nearly tangent region, making the graphs transverse to $\mu$ outside a region where $\psi>0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement: According to Lemma \ref{lm:Reeb-trick} we may assume that the semi-contact structure $\{\zeta_s\}$ on $\Sigma\times[0,1]$ is of immersion type with the following properties. There exist a contact structure $\mu$ on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ and a function $\psi:\Sigma\to [-\frac R2,\frac R2]$ such that \begin{description} \item{(i)} the germ of contact structure $\zeta_s$ is induced from $\mu$ on a neighborhood of the $\Sigma\times s$ by an embedding $(x,s)\mapsto (x, s\psi(x)+t)\in\Sigma\times[-R,R] , x\in\Sigma, t\in[-\delta,\delta]$; \item {(ii)} there are closed domains $V\subset\Sigma$ and $\widehat V\subset {\rm Int\,} V$ such that $\psi|_V >0$, and the contact structure $\mu$ is transverse to graphs of functions $s\psi $ over $\widehat W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,}\widehat V$ for all $s\in[0,1]$. \end{description} We will keep the notation $\psi$ for the restriction of $\psi$ to $\widehat W$. Note that $\psi$ can be presented as the difference $\psi=\psi_+-\psi_-$ of two positive functions $\psi_\pm \in C^\infty(\widehat W)$such that the graphs of the functions $s\psi_\pm$ are transverse to $\mu$. Let $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^N$ be a finite covering of $W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} V$ by interiors of balls with smooth boundaries and such that $\bigcup\limits_1^N\overline{U_i}\subset \widehat W$. Let $\{\lambda^\pm_i: \Sigma \to [0,1]\}$ be two partitions of unity on $W$ subordinate to the covering $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^N$, $ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda^\pm_i|_{W}=1$, such that $\mathrm{Support}(\lambda^i_-)\Subset\mathrm{Support}(\lambda^i_+),\, i=1,\dots, N,$ and $ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda^\pm_i|_{\widehat W}\leq 1$. For $0 \leq k \leq N$ define $$L_k:=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda^+_i $$ noting $L_N|_{W}=1$ and $L_N|_{\widehat V}=0$ shows $\widehat V \subset U \subset \Sigma \setminus W$, where $U:= \{L_N < 1\}$. For $1 \leq i \leq N$ define the functions $$\psi^\pm_i:=\psi^\pm\lambda^\pm_i: \Sigma \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{and}\quad \psi_i:=\psi^+_i-\psi^-_i: \Sigma \to {\mathbb{R}}$$ and for $0 \leq k \leq N$ the functions $$ \Psi_k^\pm:=\sum\limits_1^k\psi^\pm_i \quad\mbox{and}\quad \Psi_k:= \Psi_k^+-\Psi_k^-= \sum\limits_1^k\psi_i\,. $$ One can further ensure that the graphs of the functions $\Psi^\pm$ are transverse to $\mu$. Let $\Gamma(\Psi_k):=\{u=\Psi_k(x),\;x\in\Sigma\}\subset\widehat C=\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ be the graph of $\Psi_k$ and likewise $\Gamma(L_k):=\{u=L_k(x),\; x\in\Sigma\}\subset C= \Sigma\times[-1,1]$ be the graph of $L_k$. Set $\Gamma_L:= \bigcup_{k=0}^N \Gamma(L_k)$ and consider the map $p: \Gamma_L \to \Sigma\times[-R,R]$ $$ p(x,u)=(x,\psi^+(x)u -\Psi^-_k(x))\; \hbox{ for}\;(x,u)\in \Gamma(L_k). $$ This map is well defined because if $(x,u)\in \Gamma(L_i)\cap \Gamma(L_j)$ for $0\leq i<j\leq N$ then $\Psi^-_i(x)=\Psi^-_j(x).$ Indeed, $L_i(x)=L_j(x)$ implies that $\psi^+_l(x)=0$ for all $i<l\leq j$, and hence $\psi^-_l(x)=0$ for $i<l\leq j$ because $\mathrm{Support}(\psi^-_l)\subset\mathrm{Support}(\psi^+_l)$. Note that $p({ \Gamma_L})=\bigcup\limits_0^N \Gamma(\Psi_i)$. The map $p$ extends to an immersion $P:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\to \Sigma\times[-R,R]$. See Figure \ref{fig: stack}. \begin{figure}\begin{center} \includegraphics[scale=.5]{stack.pdf} \caption{The set $\Gamma_L$ used in the proof of the lemma. The region below a bump function is a saucer, so a partition of unity decomposes a general region into small saucers. Each saucer comes equipped with a map to $\widehat C$ making it a contact shell.} \end{center}\end{figure} The complement $C\setminus \Gamma_L$ is a union of the domain $\Omega:=\{(x,u);\;\Phi_N(x)\leq u\leq 1, x\in U\}$ and the interiors of saucers $B_i$ bounded by the graphs $\Gamma(L_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma(L_i)$ over the balls $\overline{U_i}$, $i=1,\dots N$. We extend the immersion $P$ to $\Omega$ as a diffeomorphism $\Omega\to\{(x,u); \Psi_N(x)\leq u\leq \psi_1(x),\;x\in U\}$ which is fiberwise linear with respect to the projection to $\Sigma$, It remains to extend the induced contact structure $P^*\mu$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\cup \Omega$ as a regular semi-contact structure on the saucers. The following lemma is obvious. \begin{lemma} Let $\Sigma$ be a hypersurface in a $(2n+1)$-dimensional contact manifold transversal to the contact structure, and $f:D^{2n}\to \Sigma$ a smooth embedding of the unit $2n$-ball. Then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the disc $f(D_\varepsilon^{2n}) $ is regular. \end{lemma} It follows that the covering by balls $U_i^+$ can be chosen to ensure that the discs $(\overline{U}^+_i, \zeta_0)$ are regular. If the function $ \psi$ is sufficiently $C^1$-small then for each $i=1,\dots, N$ the graphs $\Gamma^-_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma^+_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_i)$ of the functions $\Psi_{i-1}|_{\overline U_i^+}$ and $\Psi_{i}|_{\overline U_i^+}$ respectively, are regular as well. Hence there is a contactomorphism $g_i$ between a neighborhood $O_i\supset\Gamma_i^-$ and a neighborhood of a disc in $\Pi=\{y_n=0\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{n+1}$. Again, if $ \psi$ is sufficiently small then the neighborhood $O_i$ contains the disc $\Gamma_i^+$ and, moreover, $g_i(\Gamma^+_i)$ is transverse to the vector field $\frac\partial{\partial y_n}$, which ensures the regularity of the contact saucer $B_i$, $i=1,\dots, N$. Finally, it remains to observe that the required $C^1$-smallness of the function $ \psi$ can be achieved by passing to a partition. This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{lm:annuli-to-saucers}.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the nontransverse region by partitions of unity into small graphs; regions between consecutive graphs are saucers made regular by Lemma 7.5 and $C^1$-smallness.

nodes.name: Small discs in transverse hypersurfaces are regular
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a hypersurface in a $(2n+1)$-dimensional contact manifold transversal to the contact structure, and $f:D^{2n}\to \Sigma$ a smooth embedding of the unit $2n$-ball. Then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the disc $f(D_\varepsilon^{2n}) $ is regular.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.label: lm:foliation

nodes.name: Parametric reduction to regular semi-contact saucers
nodes.statement: Let $ M$ be a $(2n+1)$-manifold and $A\subset M$ a closed set, so that $M\setminus A$ is connected. Let ${}^T\xi_0$ be a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^TM$ which is genuine on $(T\times{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, A)\cup (\partial T\times M)\subset T\times M$. Then there exist a finite number of (possibly overlapping) discs $T_i\subset T$ and disjoint embedded fibered saucers ${}^{T_i}B_i\subset {}^TM$, $i=1,\dots, N$, such that ${}^T\xi_0$ is homotopic rel.\ $(T\times A)\cup \partial T\times M $ to a fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\xi_1$ which is is genuine on ${}^TM\setminus\bigcup B_i$ and whose restriction to each fibered saucer ${}^{T_i}B_i$ is semi-contact and regular. Moreover, we can choose the discs in such a way that any non-empty intersection $T_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap T_{i_k}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_k\leq L$, is again a disc with piecewise smooth boundary.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.label: prop:to-saucers-param

nodes.name: Parametric reduction of semi-contact annuli to saucers
nodes.statement: Any fibered semi-contact structure ${}^T\xi=\{\zeta^\tau_s\}_{s\in[0,1],\tau\in T}$ on the fibered annulus ${}^TC:=T\times \Sigma\times[0,1]$ is homotopic relative $T\times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial C\cup\partial T\times C$ to a fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\widetilde \xi$ which is a genuine contact structure in the complement of finitely many fibered saucers ${}^{T_1}B_1,\dots, {}^{T_k}B_k\subset {}^TC$, and such that the restriction ${}^{T_j}\widetilde\xi|_{{}^{T_j}B_j}$ for each $j=1,\dots, k$ is semi-contact and regular. Moreover, we can choose the discs $T_i\subset T$ in such a way that any non-empty intersection $T_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap T_{i_p}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_p\leq k$, is again a disc with piecewise smooth boundary.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.label: lm:annuli-to-saucers-param

nodes.name: Parametric partition into immersion-type annuli
nodes.statement: Given a fibered semi-contact structure ${}^T\!\xi$ on $T\times\Sigma\times[0,1]$ there exists $N>0$ such that the restriction of ${}^T\xi$ to $ T\times \Sigma\times[a_i,a_{i+1}]$, $a_i:=a+i\frac{b-a}N$ is of immersion type for each $i=0,\dots, N-1$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.label: lm:partition-to-special-param

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.7
nodes.statement: Using Lemma \ref{lm:partition-to-special-param}, we can assume that the fibered semi-contact structure ${}^T\xi$ on the annulus ${}^TC=T\times C$ is of immersion type, i.e.\ there exists a fibered contact structure ${}^T \mu=\{\mu^\tau_{\tau\in T}\}$ on ${}^T\widehat C:=T\times\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ and a family of functions $\psi^\tau_s:\Sigma\to[- r,r]$, $r<R$, $s\in[0,1], \tau\in T$, such that the contact structure $\zeta^\tau_s$ on a neighborhood of $\Sigma^\tau _s$ is induced from $\mu^\tau$ by an embedding of this neighborhood onto a neighborhood of the graph of the function $\psi^\tau_s$. Let $T'\subset{\rm Int\,} T'', T''\subset {\rm Int\,} T$ be two slightly smaller compact parameter spaces such that the semi-contact structure $\mu^\tau$ is contact for $\tau\in T\setminus{\rm Int\,} T'$, i.e.\ $\psi^\tau_s(x)>\psi^\tau_{s'}(x)$ for any $x\in\Sigma, \tau\in T\setminus{\rm Int\,} T'$ and $s>s'$. Similarly to the non-parametric case (see Lemma \ref{lm:Reeb-trick}) we can reduce to the case when the following property holds: $\psi^\tau_0=0,\psi^\tau_s=s\psi^\tau$ and there exist domains $\widehat W, W \subset T\times\Sigma$, ${\rm Int\,} \widehat W\Supset W$ such that $\psi^\tau(x)>0$ for $(x,\tau)\in T'\times\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} W$, and the contact structures $\mu^\tau$ transverse to the graphs $\Gamma^\tau_s $ of the functions $s\psi^\tau$ over $V^\tau:=(\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} W)\cap{\tau\times\Sigma}$. Denote by $\psi$ the function $\psi(\tau,x,s):=\psi^\tau(x,s)$ for $(\tau,x,s)\in W$, and present $\psi$ as the difference of two positive functions, $\psi=\psi^+-\psi^-$. Let us choose a finite covering of $ W$ denoted $\{U_i\}$, such that $U_i={\rm Int\,} T_i\times {\rm Int\,}\Delta^\pm_i $, where $\Delta_i\subset\Sigma,\; T_i\subset T''$, are balls with smooth boundaries, $ i=1,\dots, N$, and $\bigcup\limits_1^N \overline{U_i}\subset \widehat W$. Here we choose the discs $T_i\subset T$ in such a way that any non-empty intersection $T_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap T_{i_k}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_k\leq L$, is again a disc with piecewise smooth boundary. More geometric constraints on the coverings will be imposed below. Let $\lambda^\pm_i$ be two partitions of unity over $\widehat W$ subordinated to $U_i$ so that $\mathrm{Support}(\lambda_i^-)\Subset\mathrm{Support}(\lambda_i^+)$, $$\sum\lambda^\pm_i|_{ W}=1,\;\hbox{ and} \; \sum\lambda^\pm_i|_{\widehat W}\leq 1.$$ Let us denote $$\psi^\pm_i:=\psi^\pm\lambda^\pm_i,\; \psi_i:=\psi^+_i-\psi^-_i,\; i=1,\dots, N.$$ Set $$\Psi_k^\pm:=\sum\limits_1^k\psi^\pm_i,\;\; \Psi_k:= \Psi_k^+-\Psi_k^-=\sum\limits_1^k\psi_i,\;\Phi_k:=\sum\limits_1^k\lambda^+_i.$$ Note that $L_N|_{ W}=1$ and $L_N|_{\widehat V}=0$, so $V \subset U:= \{L_N(x) < 1\} \subset T\times\Sigma \setminus W$. In ${}^TC=T\times\Sigma\times[0,1]$ we let $\Gamma(L_k)$ be the graph of the function $L_k$, and in ${}^T\widehat C = T\times\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ we let $\Gamma(\Psi_k)$ be the graph of the function $\Psi_k$. Set $\Gamma_L=\bigcup\limits_0^N \Gamma(L_i)\subset {}^TC$. Consider the map $p:{ \Gamma_L}\to T\times \Sigma\times[-R,R]$ given by the formula $$p(\tau,x,s)=(\tau,x, \psi^+(\tau,x)s -\Psi^-_i(\tau,x))\; \hbox{ for}\;(\tau,x,s)\in \Gamma(L_i).$$ This map is well defined because if $(\tau, x,s)\in \Gamma(L_i)\cap \Gamma(L_j)$ for $0\leq i<j\leq N$ then $\Psi^-_i(\tau,x)=\Psi^-_j(\tau,x).$ Indeed, $\Phi_i(\tau, x)=\Phi_j(\tau,x)$ implies that $\psi^+_l(\tau,x)=0$ for all $i<l\leq j$, and hence $\psi^-_l(\tau,x)=0$ for $i<l\leq j$ because $\mathrm{Support}(\psi^-_l)\subset\mathrm{Support}(\psi^+_l)$. Note that $p({ \Gamma_L})=\bigcup\limits_0^N \Gamma(\Psi_i)$. The map $p$ extends to an immersion $P:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\to T\times \Sigma\times[-R,R]$. The complement ${}^TC\setminus \Gamma_L$ is a union of the domain $\Omega:=\{(x,s);\;\Phi_N(\tau,x)\leq s\leq 1, \tau\in T, x\in U\}$ and interiors of fibered saucers ${}^{T_i}B_i$ bounded by the graphs $\Gamma(L_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma(L_i)$ over the balls $\overline{U_i}$, $i=1,\dots N$. We extend the immersion $P$ to $\Omega$ as a fiberwise linear, with respect to the projection to $T\times \Sigma$, diffeomorphism $$\Omega\to\{(\tau, x,u); \Psi_N(\tau,x)\leq u\leq \psi(\tau, x),\;(\tau,x)\in U\}.$$ It remains to extend the induced contact structure $P^*\left({}^T\mu\right)$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\cup \Omega$ as a fibered regular semi-contact structure to the saucers. It follows from Lemma \ref {lm:foliation} that the covering by balls $U_i$ can be chosen to ensure that for each $i=1,\dots, N$ and $\tau \in T^+_i$ the disc $(\tau\times\Delta^+_i, \zeta^\tau_0)$ is regular. If the functions $ \psi_1$ and $ \psi_0$ are sufficiently $C^1$-close than for each $i=1,\dots, N$ the graphs $\Gamma^-_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma^+_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_i)$ of the functions $\Psi_{i-1}|_{\overline U_i^+}$ and $\Psi_{i}|_{\overline U_i^+}$, respectively, are fibered over $T_i^+$ by regular discs as well. Hence, there is a fibered over $T_i^+$ contactomorphism $g_i$ between a neighborhood $O_i\supset\Gamma_i^-$ and a neighborhood of a fibered disc in $T_i\times \Pi=\{y_n=0\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{n+1}$. Again, if $ \psi$ is sufficiently close then the neighborhood $O_i$ contains the disc $\Gamma_i^+$ and, moreover, $g_i(\Gamma^+_i)$ is transverse to the vector field $\frac\partial{\partial y_n}$, which ensures the regularity of the fibered contact saucer ${}^{T_i}B_i$, $i=1,\dots, N$. Finally, it remains to observe that the required smallness of the function $ \psi$ can be achieved by passing to a partition.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Parametric repetition of the proof of Lemma 7.2 with coverings by products $T_i\times\Delta_i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.6
nodes.statement: First assume $T = D^q$. Choose an embedded annulus $C=S^{2n}\times[0,1]\subset M\setminus A$ and first use the $q$-parametric part of Gromov's $h$-principle \ref{thm:Gromov-open} to deform ${}^T\xi_0$ rel.\ $(T\times A)\cup(\partial T\times M)$ to a fibered almost contact structure which is genuine fibered contact structure on $T\times M\setminus C$. Next, with use of the $(q+1)$-parametric part of Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open} applied to the family of neighborhoods of spheres $\tau\times S^{2n}\times t, \tau\in T, t\in[0,1]$ we make the fibered almost contact structure semi-contact on ${}^TC=T\times C$. Finally we use Lemma \ref{lm:annuli-to-saucers-param} to complete the proof. For general $T$ we triangulate it and inductively over skeleta apply the previous proof to each simplex.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Apply the parametric Gromov h-principle and Lemma 7.7 over $D^q$; for general $T$ triangulate and induct over skeleta.

nodes.name: Circle models reduce to finitely many universal saucers
nodes.statement: For a fixed dimension, there is a finite list of saucers $\{(B_p,\zeta_p)\}$ for $p=1,\dots, L,$ with the following property. For any circle model contact shell $(B_K, \eta_K)$ defined by a time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K\colon\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$, there exist finitely many disjoint balls $B_i\subset B_K$ for $i=1,\dots, q$ so that the contact shell $(B_K, \eta_K)$ is homotopic relative to ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B_K$ to an almost contact structure $\xi$ that is genuinely contact on $B_K \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{q} B_i$ and each contact shell $\xi|_{B_i}$ is equivalent to one of the saucers $(B_p,\zeta_p)$ for $p=1,\dots, L$.
nodes.statement_short: There is a finite list of saucers such that every time-independent circle model is homotopic to one genuine outside balls each equivalent to a saucer on the list.
nodes.label: prop:circular-to-universal-saucers

nodes.name: Idea of equivariant coverings
nodes.statement: {\rm The proof of Proposition \ref{prop:circular-to-universal-saucers} follows roughly the same scheme as the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:to saucers} but uses the idea of equivariant coverings in a crucial way. The basic idea can be seen in the following trivial observation about real functions. Consider the piecewise constant function $\phi: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ which is equal to $1$ on $[0,1) \cup [2,3)$, equal to $-3$ on $[1,2)$, and $0$ elsewhere. Let the group ${\mathbb{Z}}$ act on ${\mathbb{R}}$ by translation: $j \in {\mathbb{Z}}$ being identified with the map $x \mapsto x + j$. Then the function $\sum\limits_{j=1}^k \phi \circ j$ is equal to $1$ on $[0,1) \cup [k+2, k+3)$ and it is strictly negative on $[1,k+2)$. The key point of this example is two-fold: firstly, that a function which is negative on an arbitrarily large portion of its support can be written as a sum of functions which are negative on a small subset of their support. And secondly, that in fact these functions can be taken to be translations of a single function by a group action.}

nodes.name: Standard contact form alpha on R^{2n+1}
nodes.statement: Consider ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ with the contact structure $\xi_{\rm st}$ given by the form $$\alpha=dz+\sum\limits_1^{n-1}(x_idy_i-y_idx_i)-y_ndx_n = dz + \sum\limits_1^{n-1}u_id\varphi_i - y_ndx_n.$$

nodes.name: Lattice Theta of contactomorphisms
nodes.statement: In the group of contactomorphisms $\mathrm{Diff}({\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1},\xi_{\rm st})$ consider the $2n$-dimensional lattice $\Theta$ generated by the following transformations: \begin{itemize} \item translations $$T_z: (x, y,z)\mapsto (x , y,z+1)$$ $$T_{x_n}: (x_1,\dots, x_n , y ,z)\mapsto (x_1,\dots, x_n+\frac12, y, z),$$ \item sheers $$S_{y_j}:(x , y_1,\dots, y_j,\dots, y_{n},z,t)\mapsto (x , y_1,\dots, y_j+1,\dots, y_{n},z+x_j),\; j=1,\dots, n-1$$ $$S_{x_j}:(x_1,\dots, x_j,\dots, x_n , y ,z)\mapsto (x_1,\dots, x_j+1,\dots, x_n , y, z-y_j),\; j=1,\dots, n-1.$$

nodes.name: Commutation relations in Theta
nodes.statement: Notice that $\Theta$ preserves $\Pi$, we have $S_{y_j}S_{x_j}S_{y_j}^{-1}S_{x_j}^{-1} = T_z^2$, and all other transformations commute.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the commutators of the generators.

nodes.name: Theta acts properly discontinuously on Pi
nodes.statement: Hence every element of $\Theta$ may be written as $$ S_{x_1}^{k_1} \cdots S_{x_{n-1}}^{k_{n-1}} S_{y_1}^{l_1} \cdots S_{y_{n-1}}^{l_{n-1}} T_{x_n}^{k_n}T_{z}^{l_n} $$ and from this it follows that $\Theta$ acts properly discontinuously on $\Pi$, that is for any compact set $Q \subseteq \Pi$, the set \begin{equation} S(Q):=\{g\in\Theta: g(Q)\cap Q\neq\varnothing\}\subset\Theta \end{equation} is finite.

nodes.name: Set S(Q) (42)
nodes.statement: S(Q):=\{g\in\Theta: g(Q)\cap Q\neq\varnothing\}\subset\Theta
nodes.label: eq:SQ

nodes.name: Scaling contactomorphism C_N
nodes.statement: For any positive number $N$, let $C_N$ be the scaling contactomorphism $$(x,y,z)\mapsto (Nx,Ny,N^2z).$$

nodes.name: Rescaled lattice Theta_N
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta_N = C^{-1}_N\Theta C_N$, that is $\Theta_N$ is the group generated by translations $T_{j,N}:=C_N^{-1}\circ T_j\circ C_N, T_{z,N}:=C_N^{-1}\circ T_z\circ C_N$ and sheers $S_{j,N}:=C_N^{-1}\circ S_j\circ C_N$.

nodes.name: Equivariant cover
nodes.statement: Say that a compact set $Q$ \emph{generates a $\Theta_N$-equivariant cover of $\Pi$} if $\Theta_N \cdot {\rm Int\,}(Q) = \Pi$.

nodes.name: Subgroup Upsilon and quotient Theta^_N
nodes.statement: We denote by $\Upsilon$ the normal subgroup in $\Theta_N$ generated by $T_{x_n}^2$, and by $\widehat\Theta_N$ the quotient group $\Theta_N/\Upsilon$.

nodes.name: Sufficiently small set
nodes.statement: We call a compact set $Q\subset\Pi$ {\em sufficiently small} if $T_{x_n}^2(Q)\cap Q=\varnothing$.

nodes.name: Quotient by T_{x_n}^2 is R^{2n-1} x T^*S^1
nodes.statement: Notice that the quotient of ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ by the contactomorphism $T^2_{x_n}$ is the contact manifold $$\left({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times T^*S^1, \ker(dz-\sum\limits_1^{n-1}(x_idy_i-y_idx_i)+vdt)\right)$$ where $v = -y_n$ is identified with the fiber coordinate of $T^*S^1$ and the base coordinate $t \in {\mathbb{R}}/{\mathbb{Z}}$ is given by the quotient by translation $T^2_{x_n}$.

nodes.name: Quotient map pi
nodes.statement: Denote this quotient by $\pi:{\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1} \to {\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times T^*S^1$.

nodes.name: Quotient hyperplane Pi^
nodes.statement: The group $\widehat\Theta_N$ can be viewed as a subgroup of the group of contactomorphisms of ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1} \times T^*S^1$ preserving $\widehat \Pi=\pi(\Pi)\simeq{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}\times {\mathbb{R}}/{\mathbb{Z}}$.

nodes.name: Periodized function Phi^
nodes.statement: Any compactly supported function $\Phi :\Pi \to {\mathbb{R}}$ defines a function $\sum\limits_{h \in \Upsilon} \Phi \circ h^{-1}$ which is 1-periodic in the $x_n$-variable, and therefore defines a function $\widehat\Phi: \widehat\Pi \to {\mathbb{R}}$.

nodes.name: Properties of equivariant coverings
nodes.statement: {\rm \begin{description} \item{a)} If $Q$ generates a $\Theta$-equivariant covering of $\Pi$ then $Q_N:=C_N^{-1}(Q)$ generates a $\Theta_N$-equivariant covering. For a sufficiently large $N$ the set $Q_N$ is sufficiently small. \item{b)} Suppose that $a>\frac12$. Then the parallelepiped $$P=\{|z|\leq a, \;|x_j|, |y_j|\leq a,\ 1\leq j\leq n-1,\; 0<x_n\leq a,\; y_n=0\}\subset\Pi$$ generates a $\Theta$-equivariant covering of $\Pi$. If $a<1$ then $P$ is sufficiently small. In particular, there are sufficiently small sets generating equivariant coverings. \item{c)} If $Q'\subset Q\subset \Pi$ are two compact sets, and $Q'$ generates a $\Theta_N$-equivariant covering of $\Pi$, then so does $Q$. \end{description} }
nodes.label: rm:generator

nodes.name: Fixed discs Q and Q'
nodes.statement: Let us {\bf fix for the rest of the paper} a regular sufficiently small disc $Q\subset\Pi$ and a smaller disc $Q^\prime\subset {\rm Int\,} Q$ which generates a $\Theta$-equivariant covering of $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Cardinality m of S(Q)
nodes.statement: We Denote by $m$ the cardinality $|S(Q)|$ of the set $S(Q)$.

nodes.name: Fixed bump functions phi_pm
nodes.statement: We also fix two non-negative $C^\infty$-functions $\phi_+,\phi_-:\Pi \to {\mathbb{R}}$ which are supported in $Q$ which satisfy the following conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item $\phi_+|_{{\rm Int\,} Q}>0, \phi_-|_{ Q^\prime}>0$, and $\phi_-|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\partial Q)} = 0$; \item ${\rm max}(\phi|_{Q^\prime}) < -(m+1)\mu $, where $\phi:=\phi_+-\phi_-$,\; $\mu:={\rm max}(\phi)$ and $m$ is the cardinality of the set $S(Q)$ defined in \eqref{eq:SQ}; \item denote $\phi^s=\phi_+-s\phi_-$, $s\in[0,1]$, (so that $\phi^s\geq\phi^1=\phi$). For any finite subset $F\subset \Theta$ denote $$\Phi^s_F:=\mu+\sum\limits_{g\in F} \phi^s\circ g^{-1}|_Q,\; \; s\in[0,1].$$ Then the graph $y_n= \Phi^{s}_F(q),\; q\in Q,$ with the induced contact structure is regular.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\phi_\pm\geq0$ supported in $Q$ with $\phi=\phi_+-\phi_-$ very negative on $Q'$ and all graphs of partial sums regular.

nodes.name: Condition (iii) can always be satisfied
nodes.statement: {\rm In condition (iii) elements $g\in F$ with $g(Q) \cap Q=\varnothing$ are irrelevant, so it suffices to verify (iii) only for subsets $F$ of the finite set $ S(Q)$. Hence the condition can always be satisfied by taking $\phi_+$ and $\phi_-$ sufficiently small (e.g.\ replacing the pair $(\phi_+,\phi_-)$ which satisfy (i) and (ii) by $(\varepsilon\phi_+,\varepsilon\phi_-)$ for a sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$.) }

nodes.name: Ordering g_1, g_2, ... of Theta
nodes.statement: Let us linearly order in any way all the elements of $\Theta$: $g_1,g_2,\dots $ and order accordingly $\widehat\Theta_N$, we fix this ordering during the paper.

nodes.name: Partial sums Phi_k and Psi_k
nodes.statement: Define functions $\Pi \to {\mathbb{R}}$ by the formulas $$ \Phi_k:= \mu+ \sum\limits_{j=1}^k\phi\circ g_j^{-1} \quad\mbox{and}\quad \Psi_k= \mu+ \sum\limits_{j=1}^k\phi_+\circ g_j^{-1} $$ for $k=0,1\dots, $ and note $\Phi_0=\Psi_0\equiv \mu$.

nodes.name: Graphs ^Phi Gamma^pm_k
nodes.statement: Let $${}^{\Phi}\Gamma^-_k :=\{y_n= \Phi_{k-1}(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots, y_{n-1},z);\; (x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots, y_{n-1},z) \in g_k(Q)\}$$ be the graph of $ \Phi_{k-1}$ over the set $g_k(Q)$, and similarly denote by ${}^\Phi\Gamma^+_k$ the graph of $\ \Phi_k$ over $g_k(Q)$.

nodes.name: Graphs ^Psi Gamma^pm_k
nodes.statement: Denote by ${}^\Psi\Gamma^+_k$ the graph of $ \Psi_k$ over $g_k(Q)$ and by ${}^\Psi\Gamma^-_k$ the graph of $ \Psi_{k-1}$ over $g_k(Q)$.

nodes.name: Saucers B_k
nodes.statement: Define $B_k$ to be the saucer \begin{align*} B_k: &= \{ \Psi_{k-1}(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots, y_{n-1},z)\leq y_n\leq \Psi_{k}(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots, y_{n-1},z),\\ & (x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots, y_{n-1},z) \in g_k(Q)\} \end{align*} bounded by ${}^\Psi\Gamma_k^-$ and ${}^\Psi\Gamma_k^+$ .

nodes.name: Immersion of the saucer boundary
nodes.statement: Similar to the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:to saucers} we observe that there is an immersion ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B_k\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ which maps ${}^\Psi\Gamma_k^\pm\to {}^\Phi\Gamma_k^\pm$ diffeomorphically.

nodes.name: Shell structure zeta_k on B_k
nodes.statement: The induced contact structure $\zeta_k$ with its canonical semi-contact extension to $B_k$ defines a shell structure on the saucer $B_k$.

nodes.name: Interpolated sums Phi^s_k
nodes.statement: More generally for $s \in [0,1]$ set $$\Phi^{s}_k:=\mu+ \sum_{j=1}^k\phi^u\circ g_j^{-1} $$ so that $\Phi^1_k=\Phi_k$ and $\Phi^0_k=\Psi_k$.

nodes.name: Regular contact saucers (B_k, zeta_k^s)
nodes.statement: Define the regular contact saucer $(B_k, \zeta_k^s)$ , $k=1,\dots,$ as induced by an immersion of ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, B_k\to {\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ that maps $\partial B_k = {}^\Psi\Gamma_k^+ \cup {}^\Psi\Gamma_k^-$ diffeomorphically onto the graphs of $ \Phi^{s}_k$ and $ \Phi^{s}_{k-1}$ over $ g_k(Q)$.

nodes.name: Finitely many saucer families up to equivalence
nodes.statement: Up to equivalence the above construction builds at most $L=2^m$, $m= \abs{S(Q)}$, one-parametric families of regular contact saucers $(B_k,\zeta^{u}_k)$.
conclusions: Up to equivalence the above construction builds at most $L=2^m$, $m= \abs{S(Q)}$, one-parametric families of regular contact saucers $(B_k,\zeta^{u}_k)$
nodes.label: lm:finite-contact

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.5
nodes.statement: By the contactomorphism $g_k^{-1}$ we know $\zeta^{s}_k$ is equivalent to a saucer whose boundary contact germ is defined by the two graphs over $Q$: $$ \mbox{$\{y_n = (\Phi^{s}_{k-1} \circ g_k)|_Q\}$ and $\{y_n = (\Phi^{u}_{k} \circ g_k)|_Q\}$.} $$ However $\Phi^{s}_k|_Q \circ g_k = \mu+\sum\limits_1^k(\phi^s\circ (g_j^{-1}g_k))|_Q$ and the number of different sums of this type is bounded above the number $L=2^{m }$ of finite subsets of the set $S(Q)$.
nodes.statement_short: Translate by $g_k^{-1}$: each saucer is determined by a subset of the finite set $S(Q)$.

nodes.name: Rescaled translates phi_{g,N}
nodes.statement: Given a positive $N$ and an element $g\in \Theta_N$ we denote $\phi_{g,N}:=\frac1N\phi\circ C_N\circ g^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Rescaling of the saucers by C_N
nodes.statement: Notice that by the contactomorphism $C_N^{-1}$ the regular semi-contact saucer which is defined over the domain $Q$ by the functions $\Phi^s_{k-1}$ and $\Phi^s_{k}$ is equivalent to the saucer over the domain $ C_N^{-1}(Q)$ defined by the functions $\Phi^s_{k-1,N}:=\frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{j=1}^{k-1}\phi^u_{g_j,N}$ and $\Phi^s_{k,N}:=\frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{j=1}^{k}\phi^s_{g_j,N}$, where $\phi^s_{g,N}:=\frac1N\phi^s\circ C_N\circ g^{-1}$.

nodes.name: phi^_{g,N} depends only on the class in Theta^_N
nodes.statement: Consider the function $\widehat{\phi_{g,N}}: \widetilde\Pi \to {\mathbb{R}}$ We note that $\widehat{\phi_{g,N}}=\widehat{\phi_{g',N}}$ if $g,g'$ are in the same conjugacy class from $\widehat\Theta_N=\Theta_N/\Upsilon$, so that in the notation for $\widehat{\phi_{g,N}}$ we can use $g\in\widehat \Theta_N$.

nodes.name: Positive decomposition by equivariant translates
nodes.statement: With the above choices of $Q,Q',\phi_+,\phi_-$, for any bounded open domains $U^\prime$ and $U\Supset U^\prime$ in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ and any $C^\infty$-function $K\colon U\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which is positive on $(U\setminus\overline U^\prime)$, there exist $N>0$ and a finite subset $\Lambda \subset\widehat\Theta_N$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $ U^\prime \times S^1 \Subset \bigcup \limits_{g\in \Lambda} g({\rm Int\,} \pi(Q'_N))\subset \bigcup \limits_{g\in \Lambda} g({\rm Int\,} \pi(Q_N)) \Subset U \times S^1;$ \item $ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\widehat{\phi_{ g,N}} < \; \begin{cases} -\frac{2\mu} N& \hbox{on}\; U'\times S^1;\cr K - \frac\mu N& \hbox{on}\; (U\setminus U')\times S^1. \end{cases} $ \end{itemize}
nodes.label: lm:positive-decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.6
nodes.statement: Suppose $K\colon U \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is given. Since $K$ is positive on $U \setminus U'$, we may fix some $\varepsilon > 0$ with the property that the set $P := \{(x,y,z) \in U \setminus U': K(x,y,z) > \varepsilon\}$ disconnects $U'$ from $\partial U$. Notice that the conclusion of the lemma only becomes stronger if we enlarge the set $U' \Subset U$. With this in mind we redefine $U'$ to be the interior of the union of all components of $U \setminus P$ which are disjoint from $\partial U$. Set $\widehat Q_N:= \pi(Q_N),\;\widehat Q'_N:= \pi(Q'_N)$. For a sufficiently large $N$ there exists a finite set $ \Lambda\subset\widehat\Theta$ such that $(U' \cup P) \times S^1\Supset \bigcup \limits_{g\in \Lambda}g(\widehat Q_N) \supset \bigcup \limits_{g\in \Lambda}g(\widehat Q^\prime_N) \Supset U' \times S^1$. Furthermore, suppose that \begin{equation} N> (m+1)\mu\varepsilon^{-1} . \end{equation} Then, using \eqref{eq:largeN} we get on $P \times S^1$ $$ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{g,N} < \frac{m \mu}N = \frac{(m+1) \mu}N -\frac\mu N < \varepsilon-\frac\mu N <K-\frac\mu N.$$ On the other hand, on $U'\times S^1$ we have $$ \sum\limits_{g\in\Lambda}\phi_{g,N} <-\frac{(m+1)\mu}N + \frac{(m-1)\mu}N < - \frac{2\mu} N. $$ Indeed this holds, for given $(x,y,z) \in g(Q'_N)$ because according to inequality (ii) a single negative term $\widehat{\phi_{g,N}}(x,y,z)$ is larger in absolute value by at least $\frac{2\mu}N$ than the sum of all positive terms (the denominator $N$ appears because of the scaling factor of the function in the definition of $\phi_{g,N}$).
nodes.statement_short: Cover $U'$ by translates of $Q'_N$ for large $N$; the very negative term of $\phi$ dominates the at most $m$ positive overlapping terms.

nodes.name: Choice of N (43)
nodes.statement: N> (m+1)\mu\varepsilon^{-1} .
nodes.label: eq:largeN

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8.1
nodes.statement: Let $U={\rm Int\,} \Delta$ and $U'\Subset U$ be a star-shaped subset such that $K|_{U\setminus U'}>0$. Apply Lemma \ref{lm:positive-decomposition}, providing an integer $N>0$, and a finite set $\Lambda\subset\widehat\Theta_N$. Then the corresponding function $$\Phi=\Phi^{S^1,N}=\frac\mu N+\sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{g,N} :\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}}$$ satisfies $\Phi (w,t)< K(v)$ for $w\in \Delta\setminus U'$ and $\Phi|_{U'\times S^1}<-\frac\mu N$. According to Proposition \ref{prop:shallow} there exists a contact Hamiltonian $\widetilde K$ so that $\eta_{\widetilde K}$ is dominated by $\eta_K$, where $\widetilde K|_{\Delta\setminus U'}=K|_{\Delta\setminus U'}$ and $\widetilde K|_{U'}>-\frac\mu N$. Therefore $\Phi(w,t)<\widetilde K(w)$ for all $(w,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$. The function $\Phi$ is equal $\frac\mu N>0$ near $\partial \Delta\times S^1$ and hence defines a circular shell model $\eta_{\Phi}$ which is dominated by $\eta_{\widetilde K}$. Hence it sufficient to prove the required extension result for $\eta_{\Phi}$. We order $\Lambda$ using the chosen ordering of $\widehat\Theta$ and define functions $$\Phi_k= \frac\mu N+\sum\limits_{j=1}^k \phi_{g_j,N}:\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}},\; k=0,\dots,|\Lambda|,$$ where $|\Lambda|$ is the cardinality of $\Lambda$. We have $\Phi_0=\frac\mu N$ and $\Phi_{|\Lambda|}=\Phi$. The shells $\eta_{\Phi_k}$ and $\eta_{\Phi_{k-1}}$ differ by one of the regular saucers $(B_p,\zeta_p)$, from the finite list provided by Lemma \ref{lm:finite-contact}, while the shell $\eta_{\Phi_0}$ is solid, since $\Phi_0>0$ everywhere.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 8.6 and Proposition 4.9 reduce to the shell of a sum of translates $\Phi$, and peel off one translate at a time, each step a saucer from Lemma 8.5.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:to saucers} allows us to assume that $\xi$ is contact outside of a finite collection of disjoint saucers $\{B_i\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$, so that the restriction $\xi|_{B_i}$ for each $i=1,\dots, N$, is a regular semi-contact saucer. Using Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle} we replace saucers by circular model shells defined by time-independent contact Hamiltonians. Applying Proposition \ref{prop:circular-to-universal-saucers} we can further reduce to the case of a contact structure in the complement of saucers from the finite list $(B_p,\zeta_p)$, $p=1,\dots, L$. Using again Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle} we replace saucers by circular model shells $\left(B_{K_p},\eta_{K_p}\right)$ defined by time-independent contact Hamiltonians. We may then choose any special Hamiltonian $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ satisfying $K_{\mathrm{univ}}(x) < {\rm min}_p K_p(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to regular saucers (Prop 6.2), then to circle models (Prop 6.12), then to finitely many universal saucers (Prop 8.1), and take $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ below all resulting Hamiltonians.

nodes.name: Universal Hamiltonian for the parametric case
nodes.statement: There exist a special Hamiltonian $K_{\mathrm{univ}}:\Delta_{\rm cyl}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ and a non-increasing function $\theta:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\theta(0)=0$ and $\theta(1)=1$, which depend only on the choice of $Q,Q',\phi_+,\phi_- $, and such that for each $p=1\dots, 2^m$ there exists a family of subordination maps $$\eta_{K^{(\theta(s))}_{\mathrm{univ}}}\to\eta^{s}_p:=(B_p,\zeta^{s}_p), \; s\in[0,1], $$ which are solid for $s=0$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.label: lm:universal-eps

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.7
nodes.statement: We note that there exists $\delta>0$ such that the regular saucer $(B_p,\zeta^{s}_p)$ is solid for $s\in[0,\delta]$, i.e.\ the contact structure on its boundary is extended inside as a genuine contact structure. Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle-param} implies that the family of saucers $(B_p,\zeta^{s}_p)$ dominates a family of circular models $\eta_{\widetilde K^{s}_p}$, where $\widetilde K^{s}_p>0$ for $s\in[0,\delta']$, $p=1,\dots, 2^m$, for some $\delta'<\delta$. We also note that Lemma \ref{lm:changing-B} allows us to assume that the domain $\Delta$ in the definition of the Hamiltonians $\widetilde K_p^{s}$ coincides with $\Delta_{\rm cyl}$. Choose as $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ any special contact Hamiltonian which satisfies $$K_{\mathrm{univ}}<\mathop{{\rm min}}\limits_{s\in[0,1],p=1,\dots, L=2^m}\widetilde K^s_p.$$ (See Example \ref{ex:special}.) There exists $\delta''\in(0,\delta')$ such that $\widetilde K^s_p>K^{(0)}_{\mathrm{univ}}$ for all $s\in[0,1],\; p=1,\dots, 2^m$. Choose a non-decreasing function $\theta:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such that $\theta(s)=0$ for $s\in[0,\tfrac{\delta'}2]$ and $\theta(s)=1$ for $s\in[\delta'',1]$. Then $K_{\mathrm{univ}}^{(\theta(s))}<\widetilde K^s_p$ for all $s\in[0,1], p=1,\dots, 2^n$. Hence, by Lemma \ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} one can arrange the inclusion maps $\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}^{(\theta(s))}}\to \eta^s_p$ be subordinations.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Dominate each saucer family by circle models (Prop 6.13) on $\Delta_{\rm cyl}$ (Lemma 4.6), choose $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ below them and a reparametrization $\theta$, and apply Lemma 4.1.

nodes.name: Compatibility of the two universal Hamiltonians
nodes.statement: {\rm It is not clear that any Hamiltonian $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ satisfying Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model} also satisfies Lemma \ref{lm:universal-eps}, or conversely. But once we know that there are two Hamiltonians separately satisfying Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model} and Lemma \ref{lm:universal-eps} we can simply choose $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ to be less than both of them, and this Hamiltonian will suffice for both.}
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case

nodes.name: Cut-off function theta
nodes.statement: Choose any decreasing $C^\infty$-function $\theta:[0,1]\to [0,1]$ which is equal to $1$ on $[0,\frac13]$ and to $0$ on $[\frac23,1]$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case

nodes.name: Parametric reduction to universal saucer families
nodes.statement: There is a universal finite list of families saucers $(B^{s}_p,\zeta^s_p)$, $p=1,\dots, L$, $s\in[0,1]$, where $L$ depends only on dimension $n$, with the following property. Let $K^\tau:\Delta\to{\mathbb{R}}$, $\tau\in T$, be a family of time-independent contact Hamiltonians parameterized by the unit disc $T=D^q\subset{\mathbb{R}}^q$, and such that $K^\tau(x)>0$ for $(\tau,x)\in \partial(T\times\Delta)$. Let $({}^TB=T\times B,{}^T\eta)$ be the fibered circular shell defined by this family. Denote by ${}^T\eta_p$ the shell corresponding to the family of saucers $\eta^{(\theta(||\tau||))}_p$. Then there exist finitely many balls $B_i\subset B $, $i=1,\dots, N$, with piecewise smooth boundary, so that the fibered contact shell ${}^T\eta $ (viewed as a fibered almost contact structure on ${}^TB $) is homotopic rel.\ ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial (T\times B) $ to a fibered almost contact structure ${}^T\xi$ which is genuinely contact on $T\times(B \setminus \bigcup B_i)$, and such that each fibered contact shell ${}^T\xi|_{B_i}$ is equivalent to one of the fibered saucer shells ${}^T\eta_p$, $p=1,\dots, L$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.label: prop:circular-to-universal-param

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8.9
nodes.statement: First, we can choose $\overline K^s: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$, $s \in [0,1]$, so that $\overline K^{||\tau||} \leq K^{ \tau }$ everywhere, $\overline K^1 > 0$ and $\overline K^s|_{\partial \Delta} >0$ for all $s\in[0,1]$. It, therefore, suffices to prove the proposition for the family $\overline K^{||\tau||}$. We can also assume that $\overline K^0(x) \leq \overline K^s(x)$ for any $x \in \Delta$, $s \in [0,1]$. Let $U={\rm Int\,} \Delta$ and $U'\Subset U$ be a star-shaped subset such that $\overline K^{||\tau||}|_{U\setminus U'}>0$ for all $\tau\in T$. We also choose $\delta>0$ so that $\overline K^s > 0$ for all $s \in [1-\delta, 1]$. Apply Lemma \ref{lm:positive-decomposition} to $\overline K^0$, providing an integer $N>0$, and a finite set $\Lambda=\{g_1,\dots, g_k\}\subset\widehat \Theta_N$, so that the function $$\Phi=\Phi^{S^1,N}=\frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{g,N} :\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}}$$ satisfies $\Phi (w,t)< \overline K^s(w)$ for $w\in \Delta\setminus U'$ and $\Phi|_{U'\times S^1}<-\frac\mu N$. Choosing $N$ large enough we can also arrange that $\mathop{{\rm min}}\limits_{||\tau||\geq1-\delta} \overline K^\tau> \Psi =\Psi^{S^1,N}=\frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{+,g,N}=\frac\mu N+ \frac1N\sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\left(\phi_{+}\circ C_N\circ g^{-1}\right)$. According to Proposition \ref{prop:shallow-param} there exists a family of functions $\widetilde K^s $, $s\in[0,1]$, such that \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde K^s=\overline K^s$ on $\Delta \setminus U'$, $\widetilde{K}^s > -\frac\mu N$, $s\in[0,1]$; \item $\widetilde K^s= \overline K^s$ for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$; \item there exists a family of subordination maps $h^s: \eta_{\overline K^s}\to \eta_{\widetilde{K^s}}$ which are identity maps for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$. \end{itemize} In particular, $\Phi(w,t)<\widetilde K^s(w)$ for all $w\in \Delta, t\in S^1, s\in[0,1]$. Recall the notation $\phi^s= \phi_+-s\phi_-,\; \phi^s_{g_j,N}=\frac1N\phi^s\circ C_N\circ g_i^{-1} $ from Section \ref{sec:equi-cov}. Choose a diffeomorphism $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such $f(1-\frac\delta2)=\frac23, f(1-\delta)=\frac13$. Then the function $\widetilde\theta:=\theta\circ f$ satisfies $\widetilde\theta|_{[0,1-\delta]} = 1$ and $\widetilde\theta|_{[1-\frac\delta2,1]} = 0$. We define the families of functions $\Phi^s_i:= \frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{j=1}^i \left( \phi^{\widetilde{\theta}(s)}_{g_j,N}\right):\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}}$, so we have $\Phi^s_0=\frac1N$, $\Phi^s_{|\Lambda|}=\Phi$ for $s\leq 1-\delta$, and $\Phi^1_{|\Lambda|}=\Psi$. Here ${|\Lambda|}$ is the cardinality of $\Lambda$. The function $\Phi^s:=\Phi^s_k$ for each $s\in[0,1]$ is equal $\frac1N>0$ near $ \partial \Delta\times S^1$, and it satisfies the inequality $\Phi^s<\widetilde K^s$. Indeed, for $s\in[0,1-\delta]$ we have $\Phi^s=\Phi<\widetilde K^s$, and for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$ we have $\Phi^s<\Psi<\overline K^u=\widetilde K^s$. Therefore, the family of circular shell models $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}}$ is dominated by $\eta_{\widetilde K^{||\tau||}}$, and hence it is sufficient to prove the required extension result for the family $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}}$. The family of model shells $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}_i}$ and $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}_{i-1}}, \tau\in T$, differ by one of the regular saucer families $(B_p,\zeta^{\widetilde\theta(||\tau||)}_p)$, $p=1,\dots, L=2^m$, from the finite list provided by Lemma \ref{lm:finite-contact}. The shell $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}_0}$ is solid for all $\tau\in T$, since $\Phi^{||\tau||}_0>0$ everywhere. Similarly the saucers $(B_p,\zeta^{||\tau||}_p)$ for $\tau\in{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T$ are solid for $\tau\in{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T$, because we have $\Phi^{||\tau||}_j\geq\Phi^{||\tau||}_{j-1}$ for all $j=1,\dots, |\Lambda|$. But the fibered saucer corresponding to the family $(B_p,\zeta^{\widetilde\theta(||\tau||)}_p)$ is equivalent to ${}^T\eta_p$, $p=1,\dots, L$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Parametric version of the proof of Proposition 8.1 using Lemma 8.6, Proposition 4.10 and interpolated sums $\Phi^s_i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.10
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:to-saucers-param} allows us to assume that ${}^T\xi_0$ is fibered contact outside of a finite collection of disjoint $\{B_i\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$, so that the restriction for each $i=1,\dots, N$, $\xi_0|_{B_i}$ is a fibered regular semi-contact saucer. Applying Proposition \ref{prop:circular-to-universal-param} we further reduce the holes to a finite list of fibered saucers ${}^T\eta_p, p=1,\dots, L=2^m$. Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle-param} allows us to replace each saucer ${}^T\eta_p$, $p=1,\dots, L,$ by a fibered circular model shell ${}^T\eta_{K_p}$ defined by a family of time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K_p^\tau, \tau\in T$. But then, using Lemma \ref{lm:universal-eps} we conclude that each circular model shell ${}^T\eta_{K_p}$ dominates the fibered circular model ${}^T\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}:=\{\eta_{K^{ (\theta(||\tau||)}_{\mathrm{univ}}})\}_{\tau\in T}$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Chain Propositions 7.6, 8.9, 6.13 and Lemma 8.7.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.5
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:existence-fol} follows from Theorem \ref{thm:classif-fol} because any leafwise almost contact structure is homotopic to a structure from $\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_n))$ for an appropriate choice of embeddings $h_1,\dots, h_N$. Hence, it is sufficient to prove Theorem \ref{thm:classif-fol}.
nodes.statement_short: Homotope any leafwise almost contact structure into the space with an overtwisted basis and apply Theorem 1.6.

nodes.name: Choosing parametric paths
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be a connected manifold of dimension $m>1$, $T $ a compact contractible set, $T_1,\dots, T_k\subset T$ its compact subsets such that \begin{description} \item{$(\star)$} any intersection $T_{i_{1}}\cap \dots \cap T_{i_{p}}$ for $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_p\leq k$ is either empty or contractible. \end{description} Let $B$ be a closed $m$-dimensional ball with a given point $p \in \partial B$, $S_j:T_j\times B\to T_j\times U$, $S_j(\tau,x)=(\tau,s_j(\tau,x))$, and $S_\pm:T\times B\to T\times U$, $S_\pm(\tau,x)=(\tau,s_\pm(\tau,x))$, be pairwise disjoint fiberwise smooth embeddings. Then there exists a fiberwise embedding $S:T\times[-1,1]\to T\times U$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $S(\tau,\pm 1)=S_\pm(\tau,p)$, $\tau\in T$; \item $S (T\times[-1,1])\cap\bigcup\limits_1^kS_j(T_j\times B)=\varnothing$; \item $S (T\times(-1,1))\cap\left(S_-(T\times B)\cup S_+(T\times B)\right)=\varnothing$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lm:choosing-paths

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.1
nodes.statement: We will prove the statement by induction in $k$. When $k=0$ the statement follows from the fact that the space of maps of the contractible set $T$ into the space of pairs of disjoint embeddings of $B$ into $U$ is connected, and hence by a fiberwise isotopy we can assume that the embeddings $s_\pm(\tau,\cdot):B\to U$ are independent of $\tau$, i.e. $s_\pm(\tau,x)=\widetilde s_\pm(x)$ for all $(\tau,x)\in T\times B$. Then to construct the required embedding it is sufficient to connect the points $\widetilde s_\pm(p)$ by an embedded arc in $U$ which does not intersect the ball $\widetilde s_\pm(B)$ in its interior points. Suppose that the statement is already proven for $k=j$ (and any $U$). Suppose first that one of the $k=j+1$ sets $T_1,\dots, T_k$, say $T_k$, coincides with $T$. By a fiberwise isotopy we can make the embedding $s_k(\tau,\cdot):B\to U$ independent of $\tau$, i.e. $s_k(\tau,x)=\widetilde s_k(x)$ for all $(\tau,x)\in T\times B$. Therefore, the statement reduces to the case of $k-1=j$ sets $T_1,\dots, T_j$ and their embeddings into $\widetilde U=U\setminus\widetilde s_k(B)$, which is connected as well. Consider now the general case. By an argument as above, we can assume that the embeddings $s_+(\tau, \cdot)$ are independent of $\tau$, i.e. $s_+(\tau,x)=\widehat s_+(x)$ for all $(\tau,x)\in T\times B$. Denote $\widehat U:= U\setminus \widehat s_+(B)$. Suppose that $T_k$ is a proper subset of $T$. Set $\widehat T:= T_k$, $\widehat T_i:= T_i\cap T_k$, $\widehat S_i:= S_i|_{\widetilde T_i\times B}$, $i=1,\dots, k-1$, $\widehat S_-:= S_-|_{T_k\times B}$, $\widehat S_+:= S_k|_{T_k\times B}$. Note that the sets $\widehat T_i$, $i=1,\dots, k-1$, and $\widehat T$ satisfy the condition $(\star)$. Considering $\widehat S_i$ as embeddings into $\widehat T_i\times\widehat U$, and $\widehat S_\pm$ as embeddings into $\widehat T\times\widehat U$ we can apply the inductional hypothesis to construct a fiberwise embedding $\widehat S:\widehat T\times [-1,1]\to \widehat T\times\widehat U$ such that \begin{description} \item{--} $\widehat S(\tau,\pm 1)=S_\pm(\tau,\widehat p)$, $\tau\in \widehat T$, where $\widehat p\in \partial B$, is a point different from $p$; \item{--} $\widehat S (\widehat T\times[-1,1])\cap\bigcup\limits_1^{k-1}\widehat S_j(\widehat T_j\times B)=\varnothing$; \item{--} $\widehat S (\widehat T\times(-1,1))\cap\left(\widehat S_-(\widehat T\times B)\cup \widehat S_+(\widehat T\times B)\right)=\varnothing$. \end{description} Using the embedding $\widehat S$ we can make a fiberwise connected sum of the embeddings $\widehat S_\pm$ to construct a fiberwise embedding $\widetilde S_-:T\times B\to T\times \widehat U$ with the following properties: \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde S_-(T\times B)\cap \bigcup\limits_1^{k-1}S_j(T_j\times B)=\varnothing$; \item $\widetilde S_-(T\times B)\supset S_-(T\times B)\cup S_k(T_k\times B)$; \item the embeddings $\widetilde S_-$ and $S_-$ coincides near $T\times p\in T\times \partial B$. \end{itemize} Hence, by applying again the inductional hypothesis to the embeddings $\widetilde S_-, S$ and $S_j, j=1,\dots k-1$, we can construct a fiberwise embedding $S:T \times [-1,1]\to T\times U$ with the required properties.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number $k$ of sets $T_j$, using contractibility to make embeddings independent of $\tau$ and fiberwise connected sums.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.6
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be an $m$-ball. We need to prove that any map $$ (T,\partial T)\to (\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_N)), \mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_N)) $$ is homotopic rel. $\partial T$ to a map into $\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_N)$. In other words, let $\xi_\tau\in\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_n)$, $\tau\in T$, be a family of leafwise almost contact structures which are genuine leafwise contact structures for $\tau\in\partial T$. We will construct a homotopy rel. $\partial T$ to a family of genuine leafwise contact structures $\widetilde\xi_\tau, \tau\in T$. Consider a foliation $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}$ on $T\times V$ with leaves $\tau\times L$ where $\tau\in T$ and $L$ a leaf of $\mathcal{F}$. Let $\widehat h_j:T\times T_j\times B\to T\times V$ be the embeddings, given by $$\widehat h_j(\tau, \tau',x)=(\tau,h_j(\tau',x), (\tau,\tau',x)\in T\times T_j\times B, j=1,\dots, N.$$ The family $\xi_\tau,\tau\in T$, can be viewed as a leafwise almost contact structure $\Xi$ from $\mathfrak{cont}(\widehat \mathcal{F};\widehat h_1,\dots,\widehat h_N)$ which is genuine on leaves $\tau\times L$ for $ \tau\in\partial T$. Moreover, we can assume that $\Xi$ is a genuine leafwise contact structure on a neighborhood $U\supset \partial T\times V$ and neighborhoods $U_j\supset \widehat h_j(T\times T_j\times B)$, $j=1,\dots, N$. There exists a triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ of $T\times V$ with the following properties: \begin{itemize} \item there are compact {\em subcomplexes} $\widehat U , \widehat U_j$, $j=1,\dots, N$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ such that $\partial T\times V\subset\widehat U\subset U,\; \widehat h_j(T\times T_j\times B)\subset\widehat U_j\subset U_j$, $j=1,\dots, N$; \item the restriction $\mathcal{T}_0$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ to $T\times V\setminus {\rm Int\,}(\widehat U\cup\bigcup\limits_1^N\widehat U_j)$ is transverse to the foliation $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}$; \item For every top-dimensional simplex $\sigma$ of $\mathcal{T}_0$ there exists a submersion $\pi_\sigma:{\rm Int\,}\sigma\to B^{q+m}$ which is a fibration over an open $(q+m)$-ball with the ball fibers, and such that the pre-images $\pi_\sigma^{-1}(s), s\in B^{q+m},$ are intersections of the leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$ with ${\rm Int\,}\sigma$.\end{itemize} Applying Gromov's parametric $h$-principle for contact structures on open manifolds (see \cite{Gro69} and Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open}) inductively over skeleta of the triangulation we can deform $\Xi$, keeping it fixed on $\widehat U\cup\bigcup\limits_1^N\widehat U_j$ to make it leafwise genuinely contact in a neighborhood of the codimension $1$ skeleton of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}_0$. Our next goal is to further deform $\Xi$ on each top-dimensional simplex $\sigma$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}_0$, keeping it fixed on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\sigma$, to make in leafwise genuine contact structure on $\sigma$. Let us choose one of such simplices. There exists a compact subset $\overline\sigma\subset{\rm Int\,}\sigma$ such that the leafwise almost contact structure $\Xi$ is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,}\overline\sigma)$ and $\pi_\sigma|_{\overline\sigma}$ is a fibration over a closed $(m+q)$-ball $X $ with fibers diffeomorphic to a closed $(2n+1)$-ball. Hence, $\Xi|_{\overline\sigma}$ can be viewed as a fibered over $X$ almost contact structure on $\overline\sigma$, and applying Proposition \ref{prop:to-saucers-param} we can further deform $\Xi$ keeping it fixed on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\sigma$, to make it genuine away from a finite number of disjoint domains $Z_i$ fibered over $X_i\subset X$ with piecewise smooth boundary, $i=1,\dots, K$. These domains are not necessarily disjoint but could be chosen arbitrary small and in such a way that all non-empty intersections $X_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap X_{i_k}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_k\leq K$, are again balls with piecewise smooth boundaries. Let $Y$, $Y\subset\overline\sigma$, and $Y_i,\; Y_i\subset Z_i,$ be subfibrations of the fibrations $\overline\sigma\to X$ and $Z_i\to X_i , \; i=1,\dots, K$, formed by boundaries of the corresponding ball-fibers. Next, we use Lemma \ref{lm:choosing-paths} to construct for each $X_j$ a fiberwise embedding $S_j:X_j\times[0,1]\to\overline Z_j\setminus \bigcup\limits_{i\neq j}Z_i$ with $S_j(\tau,0)\in Y_j$ and $S_j(\tau,1)\in Y$. Recall that by assumption every point $(\tau,x)\in Y$ can be connected to a point on the boundary of one of the overtwisted balls $B_{i,\tau,\tau'}:=h_i(\tau\times\times\tau' B_i), \; i=1,\dots, N,\;\tau\in T,$ by an embedded path in the corresponding leaf. This path can be chosen inside an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the codimension $1$ skeleton of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}_0$. Hence, if the sets $X_j$ are chosen sufficiently small we can extend each of the embeddings $S_j$ to a leafwise embedding $\widetilde S_j:X_j\times[0,2]\to V$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $S_j(\tau,0)\in Y_j$; \item $S_j(\tau,2)\in h_i(T_i\times\partial B) $ for some $i=i(\sigma,j)$. \end{itemize} Moreover, using Proposition \ref{prop:neighb-ot} to increase the number of embeddings $h_i$ we can additionally arrange that the map $(\sigma,j)\mapsto i(\sigma,j)$ is injective. Then, successively applying Theorem \ref{thm:main-existence-T} to neighborhoods of $Z_j\cup S_j(X_j\times[0,2])\cup \bigcup\limits_{\tau\in X_j}h_{i(\sigma,j)}(S(\tau,2)\times B)$ for all top-dimensional simplices $\sigma$ of the triangulation we deform $\Xi$ to make it leafwise genuinely contact on these neighborhoods.
nodes.statement_short: Triangulate transversally to the foliation, use Gromov's h-principle near the codimension-1 skeleton, reduce each simplex to fibered saucers (Prop 7.6), connect them to overtwisted balls (Lemma 9.1) and apply Theorem 3.12.

nodes.name: Smooth overtwisted discs in dimension > 3
nodes.statement: We do not know if it is possible to characterize overtwisted structures in dimension $>3$ by existence of a {\em smooth} overtwisted disc.

nodes.name: Overtwisted (new sense) implies overtwisted (Eliashberg) in dimension 3
nodes.statement: In the $3$-dimensional case a contact structure which is overtwisted in our sense is also overtwisted in the sense of \cite{Eli89}.

nodes.name: Sketch: overtwisted in new sense implies classical
nodes.statement: This should be clear from the picture of the characteristic foliation on the disc $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$, see Figure~\ref{f:Disk}.
nodes.statement_short: Read off from the characteristic foliation of $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$.

nodes.name: Classical overtwisted implies overtwisted (new sense) in dimension 3
nodes.statement: The converse is also true.

nodes.name: Sketch: classical overtwisted implies new sense
nodes.statement: This can be seen directly by finding a copy of $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\xi_{\mathrm{ot}})$ in a neighborhood of the traditional overtwisted disc, or indirectly, from the classification theorem from \cite{Eli89}. Indeed, one can first find a contact structure on the ball with standard boundary which contains $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\xi_{\mathrm{ot}})$ and which is in the standard almost contact class. Then, implanting this ball in an overtwisted contact manifold does not change the isotopy class of this structure.
nodes.statement_short: Use Eliashberg's 3-dimensional classification: implant a ball containing $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ without changing the isotopy class.

nodes.name: All definitions satisfying Theorem 1.2 are equivalent
nodes.statement: Note, however, that {\em all definitions for which Theorem \ref{thm:main} holds are equivalent}.

nodes.name: Alternative base domain D~
nodes.statement: Suppose $\widetilde D\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-2}$ be any other star-shaped domain with a piecewise smooth boundary.

nodes.name: Domains Delta~_cyl and half-domains
nodes.statement: Denote $$\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}:= \{(x,z)\in{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-2}\times{\mathbb{R}};\; x\in\widetilde D, |z|\leq 1\},\;\; \Delta_{\rm cyl}^-:=\Delta_{\rm cyl}\cap\{z\leq 0\} $$ $$\hbox{and}\;\; \widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-:=\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}\cap\{z\leq 0\}.$$

nodes.name: Function space C_+
nodes.statement: Let $C_+ $ be the space of continuous piecewise smooth functions $\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-\to {\mathbb{R}}$ which are positive on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}\cap\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-$.

nodes.name: Regions U_{K_-,K_+} and Sigma_{K_+}
nodes.statement: Given two functions $K_\pm\in C_+ $ such that $K_-<K_+$ we denote \begin{align*} U_{K_-,K_+} &= \{(x,v,t): K_-(x,t)\leq v \leq K_+(x,t), z(x)\leq 0\} \\&\subset (\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl} ^-\times T^*S^1, \ker(\lambda_{{\rm st}} + v\,dt)) \quad \mbox{and} \\ \Sigma_{K_+} &= \{(x,v,t): 0 \leq v \leq K_+(x, t)\,,\,\, x \in \partial \Delta, z(x)\leq 0\} \\& \subset (\Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2, \ker(\lambda_{{\rm st}} + v\,dt)). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Glued germ U^_{K_-,K_+}
nodes.statement: Gluing these pieces together via the natural identification between their common parts we define $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+} :=U_{K_-,K_+} \cup \Sigma_{K_+}$.

nodes.name: Overtwisted germs over other domains
nodes.statement: For any $K_+\in C_+(\widetilde\Delta)$ there exists $K_-\in C_+(\widetilde\Delta)$, such that $K_-<K_+$ such that $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$ is overtwisted.
nodes.label: lm:base-change

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10.1
nodes.statement: Choosing a representative $\eta$ of the contact germ along $\Sigma_{K_+}$ let $U$ be a neighborhood of $\partial \widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl} $ such that $K|_{U\cap\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-}>0$ and the contact structure $\eta$ is defined on $\{(x,v,t); x\in U\cap\{z\geq 0\}, v\leq K_+(x)\}$. There is a contact embedding $\Phi: \Delta_{\rm cyl}^-:= \widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-$ such that $\Phi(\partial\Delta_{\rm cyl}\cap \Delta_{\rm cyl}^-)\subset U$ and $\Phi(\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-\cap\{z=0\})\subset \{z=0\}$. Indeed, the contact vector field $Z=L+z\frac{\partial}{\partial z}$, $L=\sum\limits_1^{n-1}\limits u_i\frac{\partial}{\partial u_i}$ is given by the contact Hamiltonian $z$ with respect to the standard contact form $\lambda_{\rm st}=dz+\sum\limits_1^{n-1}u_id\phi_i$. Consider a cut-off function $\sigma:{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}\to{\mathbb{R}}_+$ which is equal to $1$ on $\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}\setminus U$ and supported in ${\rm Int\,}\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}$, and let $\widetilde Z$ denote the contact vector field defined by the contact Hamiltonian $K:=z\sigma$. Let us observe that $\widetilde Z$ is tangent to the hyperplane $\{z=0\}$ because $K$ vanishes on this hyperplane. Let $Z^t$ and $\widetilde Z^t$ be the contact flows generated by $Z$ and $\widetilde Z$. Then the formula $\Phi:= \widetilde Z^{\widetilde C}\circ Z^{-C}$ is the required contact embedding for appropriately chosen positive constants $C,\widetilde C$. For an appropriate choice of a special Hamiltonian $K<K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ we have $\Phi_*K< K_+$. On the other hand, there exists $K_-\in C_+$ such that $\Phi_*K>K_-$. Hence, the overtwisted disc $D_{\mathrm{ot}}=D_K$ embeds into an arbitrarily small neighborhood of $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$, i.e. $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$ is overtwisted.
nodes.statement_short: Embed $\Delta^-_{\rm cyl}$ into $\widetilde\Delta^-_{\rm cyl}$ by contact flows so that a pushed special Hamiltonian lies between $K_-$ and $K_+$.

nodes.name: Standard wrinkle
nodes.statement: Let $B$ denote the unit ball in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ and $w:B\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ be the {\it standard wrinkle} (see \cite{EliMi97}), i.e.\ a map given by the formula $$(v, y_n,)\mapsto(v, y_n^3-3\alpha(r)y_n),\; v\in{\mathbb{R}}^{2n},$$ where $r:=||v||^2$, and $\alpha:[0,1]\to{\mathbb{R}}$ is a $C^{\infty}$-function which is positive on $(\frac14,\frac34)$, negative on $(\frac34, 1]$, constant near $0$, has a negative derivative at $\frac34$, and satisfies the inequality $\alpha(r)\leq 1-r^2$.

nodes.name: Wrinkle region W
nodes.statement: Denote $W:\{y_n^2\leq\alpha(r)\}$.

nodes.name: Wrinkle complement embeds in overtwisted manifolds
nodes.statement: Note that Corollary \ref{cor:isocontact} allows us to construct a contact embedding of $(U\setminus W,(w^*\zeta)|_{U\setminus W})$ into any overtwisted contact manifold of the same dimension.

nodes.name: Wrinkle complement contains an overtwisted disc
nodes.statement: One can also show, though we do not know a simple proof of this fact, that $(U\setminus W,(w^*\zeta)|_{U\setminus W})$ contains an overtwisted disc.

nodes.name: Wrinkle characterization of overtwisting
nodes.statement: Hence, {\em a contact structure $\xi$ on a manifold $M$ is overtwisted if and only if there exists a neighborhood $U\supset W$ in $B$, and a contact embedding $(U\setminus W,(w^*\zeta)|_{U\setminus W})\to (M,\xi)$. }

nodes.name: k-stabilization
nodes.statement: Given a contact manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with a fixed contact form $\lambda$ its {\em $k$-stabilization} is the contact manifold $Y_k^{\mathrm{stab}}:=Y\times{\mathbb{R}}^{2k}$ endowed with the contact structure $ \xi_k^{\mathrm{stab}}:=\{\lambda+\sum\limits_1^k v_id\phi_i=0\}$.

nodes.name: Stabilization is independent of the contact form
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to check that up to a canonical contactomorphism the contact manifold $(Y_k^{\mathrm{stab}},\xi_k^{\mathrm{stab}})$ is independent of the choice of the contact form $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Stabilization preserves overtwisting
nodes.statement: The $k$-stabilization $(Y_k^{\mathrm{stab}},\xi_k^{\mathrm{stab}})$ of any overtwisted contact manifold $(Y,\xi)$ is overtwisted for any $k\geq 0$.
nodes.label: thm:stab

nodes.name: Overtwisting via stabilized 3-dimensional discs
nodes.statement: In particular, this implies that an overtwisted contact manifold of dimension $2n+1$ can be equivalently defined as a contact manifold containing the $(2n-2)$-stabilization of a neighborhood of the standard $3$-dimensional overtwisted disc.

nodes.name: Overtwisting of M x T^*S^1
nodes.statement: For any overtwisted contact manifold $(M,\xi=\{\lambda=0\})$ the contact manifold $(M\times T^*S^1, \{\lambda+vdt=0\}$ is overtwisted. Moreover, $M\times T_+^*S^1:=(M\times T^*S^1)\cap\{v>0\}$ is overtwisted as well.
nodes.label: cor:stab2

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 10.3
nodes.statement: $(M\times T_+^*S^1, \lambda+vdt)$ is contactomorphic to $(M\times {\mathbb{R}}^2\setminus 0, \lambda+xdy-ydx$. On the other hand, there exists a contact embedding $(M\times D^2_R,\lambda +xdy-ydx)\to (M\times {\mathbb{R}}^2\setminus 0, \lambda+xdy-ydx)$. It can be defined, for instance, by the formula $(w,x,y)\mapsto (\frak{R}^{-2Ry}(w), x+2R,y)$, where $\frak{R}^t$ is the Reeb flow of the contact form $\lambda$. But according to Theorem \ref{thm:stab} the product $(M\times D^2_R, \{\lambda+xdy-ydx=0\})$ is overtwisted if the radius of the $2$-disc $D^2_R$ is sufficiently large, and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Embed $M\times D^2_R$ into $M\times(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus0)$ via the Reeb flow and apply Theorem 10.2.

nodes.name: Eliashberg-Polterovich relation on Cont~
nodes.statement: In \cite{EliPolt00} there was introduced a relation $\leq$ on the universal cover $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Cont}}(Y,\xi)$ of the identity component of the group of contactomorphisms of $(Y,\xi)$. Namely, $f\leq g$ for $f,g\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{Cont}}(Y,\xi)$ if there is a path in $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Cont}}(Y,\xi)$ connecting $f$ to $g$ which is generated by a non-negative contact Hamiltonian.

nodes.name: Non-orderable contact manifold
nodes.statement: This relation is either trivial (e.g. in the case of the standard contact sphere of dimension $>1$, see \cite{EKP06}, and in this case the contact manifold $(Y,\xi)$ is called {\em non-orderable}, or it is a genuine partial order, e.g. in the case of ${\mathbb{R}} P^{2n-1}$ (see \cite{Giv}) or the unit cotangent bundle $UT^*(M)$ of a closed manifold $M$, see \cite{EKP06, ChNem10}.
nodes.origin_citation: Eliashberg, Kim, Polterovich 2006; Givental 1990; Chernov & Nemirovski 2010

nodes.name: Orderability of closed overtwisted 3-manifolds
nodes.statement: It is an open longstanding question whether a $3$-dimensional closed overtwisted contact manifold is orderable or not (see \cite{{CaPrSa10}, CaPr14} for partial results in this direction).
nodes.origin_citation: longstanding question (cf. Casals, Presas, Sandon 2010; Casals & Presas 2014)

nodes.name: Contact manifold Y x T^*S^1
nodes.statement: Given a contact manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with a fixed contact for $\lambda$ consider the contact manifold $(Y\times T^*S^1, \{\lambda+vdt=0\})$, where $S^1={\mathbb{R}}/{\mathbb{Z}}$.

nodes.name: Generating Hamiltonian K_t
nodes.statement: Let $f\in\widetilde{\mathfrak{Cont}}(Y,\xi)$ be generated by a time dependent contact Hamiltonian $K_t:Y\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which can be assumed $1$-periodic in $t$.

nodes.name: Domain V^+(f)
nodes.statement: We consider the domain $V^+(f)=\{v+K_t(x)\geq 0, x\in Y\}\subset Y\times T^*S^1.$

nodes.name: Eliashberg-Polterovich domain property of the order
nodes.statement: If $f\leq g$ then there exists a contact diffeotopy \begin{equation} h_t:Y\times T^*S^1\to Y\times T^*S^1,\quad \hbox{such that} \quad h_0=\mathrm {Id} \quad\hbox{ and}\quad h_1(V^+(f))\subset V^+(g). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Domain criterion for the order (44)
nodes.statement: h_t:Y\times T^*S^1\to Y\times T^*S^1,\quad \hbox{such that} \quad h_0=\mathrm {Id} \quad\hbox{ and}\quad h_1(V^+(f))\subset V^+(g).
nodes.label: eq:order2

nodes.name: Converse of the Eliashberg-Polterovich domain property
nodes.statement: However it is not known whether the converse is true.

nodes.name: Weak order relation
nodes.statement: Thus, it seems natural to introduce a weaker relation: {\em we say that $f\lessapprox g$ if there exists an isotopy $h_t$ as in \eqref{eq:order2}. }

nodes.name: Equivalence of the order and the weak order
nodes.statement: If $f\leq g$ then $f\lessapprox g$ but we do not know whether these relations are equivalent or not.

nodes.name: Known orderable manifolds are weakly orderable
nodes.statement: However, as we already stated above, in all known to us cases of contact orderability in the sense of $\leq $ one can also prove {\em weak orderability} in the sense of $\lessapprox $.

nodes.name: Overtwisted manifolds are not weakly orderable
nodes.statement: Any closed overtwisted contact manifold is not weakly orderable.
assumptions: Any closed overtwisted contact manifold
conclusions: is not weakly orderable
nodes.label: thm:non-orderability

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10.4
nodes.statement: According to Corollary \ref{cor:stab2} for a sufficiently large contact Hamiltonian $K>0$ the domain $V^+(K)$ is overtwisted. Hence, Corollary \ref{cor:isocontact} from allows us to construct an isotopy of $V^+({2K})$ into $V^+(K)$ inside $Y\times T^*S^1$. This isotopy extends to a global diffeotopy, and hence $g_{2K}\lessapprox g_K$, where $g_H$ denotes a time 1 map of the contact Hamiltonian $H$. On the other hand, we clearly have $g_{K}\lessapprox g_{2K}$, i.e. the order $\lessapprox $ is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 10.3 makes $V^+(K)$ overtwisted, so Corollary 1.4 isotopes $V^+(2K)$ into $V^+(K)$, showing the weak order is trivial.

nodes.name: Almost contact structures on spheres
nodes.statement: Almost contact structures on the sphere $S^{2n+1}$ are classified by the homotopy group $\pi_{2n+1}(SO(2n+2)/U(n+1))$.
nodes.section: Classification of overtwisted contact structures on spheres

nodes.name: Harris' computation of pi_{2n+1}(SO(2n+2)/U(n+1))
nodes.statement: $$\pi_{2n+1}( SO(2n+2)/U(n+1))=\begin{cases} {\mathbb{Z}}/n!{\mathbb{Z}},& n=4k;\cr {\mathbb{Z}},& n=4k+1;\cr {\mathbb{Z}}/\frac{n!}2{\mathbb{Z}},& n=4k+2.\cr {\mathbb{Z}}\oplus{\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}, & n=4k+3;\cr \end{cases} $$
nodes.section: Classification of overtwisted contact structures on spheres
nodes.label: lm:comput-sphere

nodes.name: Classification of overtwisted contact structures on spheres
nodes.statement: Thus, Corollary \ref{cor:main} implies that on spheres $S^{8k+1}$, $k>0$, there are exactly $(4k)!$ different overtwisted contact structures, on spheres $S^{8k+5}$, $k\geq 0$, there are $\frac{(4k+2)!}2$ different overtwisted contact structures, while on all other spheres there are infinitely many. In particular, there is a unique overtwisted contact structure on $S^5$.
nodes.section: Classification of overtwisted contact structures on spheres
nodes.statement_short: Counts overtwisted contact structures on $S^{2n+1}$: $(4k)!$ on $S^{8k+1}$, $(4k+2)!/2$ on $S^{8k+5}$, infinitely many otherwise; unique on $S^5$.

nodes.name: Infinitely many tight contact structures on S^5
nodes.statement: It is interesting to note that $S^5$ has infinitely many {\it tight}, i.e.\ non-overtwisted contact structures. Besides the standard contact structure, these are examples given by Brieskorn spheres (see \cite{Ust}).
nodes.section: Classification of overtwisted contact structures on spheres
