nodes.name: Classification of tight contact structures in dimension > 3
nodes.statement: The full classification of tight contact structures on any manifold of dimension $>3$ is an open problem.
nodes.section: Classification of overtwisted contact structures on spheres

nodes.name: Verify the contact condition where $\partial_v\rho>0$
nodes.statement: One checks $\alpha_\rho$ satisfies the contact condition \begin{equation} \mbox{$\alpha_\rho \wedge (d\alpha_\rho)^n > 0$ whenever $\partial_v \rho > 0$} \end{equation} and hence $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho})$ is a contact shell by conditions (ii) and (iii).
nodes.statement_short: Verify the contact condition where $\partial_v\rho>0$

nodes.name: Same $C$: compare $\rho_0,\rho_1$ by fiberwise diffeomorphisms and a straight-li
nodes.statement: Consider the special case of two choices $\rho_0$ and $\rho_1$ as in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoS1} for the same $C$. We can pick a family of diffeomorphisms $\phi_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that $$ \phi_{(x,t)}(v) = (\rho_1^{-1}\circ\rho_0)_{(x,t)}(v) \mbox{ on } {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{v = K(x,t) + C\} \cup {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta $$ and this family induces a diffeomorphism $\Phi: B_{K,C} \to B_{K,C}$ such that $\Phi^*\alpha_{\rho_1} = \alpha_{\rho_1 \circ \phi}$ and $\alpha_{\rho_1 \circ \phi} = \alpha_{\rho_0}$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B_{K,C}$. It follows that $\Phi$ is an equivalence between $\eta_{K, \rho_0}$ and $\eta_{K, \rho_1}$ since we have the straight line homotopy from $\alpha_{\rho_1 \circ \phi}$ to $\alpha_{\rho_0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Same $C$: compare $\rho_0,\rho_1$ by fiberwise diffeomorphisms and a straight-line homotopy

nodes.name: General case: shift $v$ by $C_1-C_0$ and reduce to the special case
nodes.statement: Given two choices $(C_0, \rho_0)$ and $(C_1, \rho_1)$, we can pick a family of diffeomorphisms $\psi_{(x,t)}: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that $$ \psi_{(x,t)}(v) = v + (C_1 - C_0) \quad \mbox{ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \{v = C_0+K(x,t)\}$}. $$ Now to see $(B_{K, C_0}, \eta_{K, \rho_0})$ and $(B_{K, C_1}, \eta_{K, \rho_1})$ are equivalent, just note that $(B_{K, C_0}, \eta_{K, \rho_0})$ and $(B_{K, C_0}, \eta_{K, \rho_1 \circ \psi})$ are equivalent via the previous special case and $\psi$ induces an isomorphism $\Psi: (B_{K, C_0}, \alpha_{\rho_1\circ\psi}) \to (B_{K, C_1}, \alpha_{\rho_1})$.
nodes.statement_short: General case: shift $v$ by $C_1-C_0$ and reduce to the special case

nodes.name: Pick a ball $B$ near $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ with $D_{\mathrm{ot}}\subset\partial B$
nodes.statement: By assumption there is a piecewise smooth disc $D_{\mathrm{ot}}\subset M\setminus A$ such that all almost contact structures $\xi^\tau$ for $\tau\in T$ are genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ and restrict to $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ as $\eta_{\mathrm{ot}}$. Since $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}})$ determines the germ of the contact structure we may pick a ball $B \subset {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ with $D_{\mathrm{ot}} \subset \partial B$ and assume $({}^{T} B, {}^T \xi) = T \times (B, \xi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a ball $B$ near $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ with $D_{\mathrm{ot}}\subset\partial B$

nodes.name: Standardize the holes by Proposition 3.10
nodes.statement: By applying Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model-param} we may assume there is a collection of disjoint fibered balls ${}^{T_i}B_i \subset M \setminus (A \cup B)$ over a collection of discs $T_i \subset T$ for $i = 1, \dots, L$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item ${}^T\xi$ is genuine away from $\bigcup_{i=1}^L {\rm Int\,}({}^{T_i}B_i)$ and \item the fibered shells $({}^{T_i}B_i, {}^{T_i}\xi)$ and $({}^{T_i}B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ are equivalent.
nodes.statement_short: Standardize the holes by Proposition 3.10

nodes.name: Genuine away from the fibered holes
nodes.statement: ${}^T\xi$ is genuine away from $\bigcup_{i=1}^L {\rm Int\,}({}^{T_i}B_i)$ and
nodes.statement_short: Genuine away from the fibered holes

nodes.name: Holes are universal fibered circle models
nodes.statement: the fibered shells $({}^{T_i}B_i, {}^{T_i}\xi)$ and $({}^{T_i}B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ are equivalent.
nodes.statement_short: Holes are universal fibered circle models

nodes.name: Get disjoint overtwisted balls inside $B$ by Proposition 3.8
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:neighb-ot} to get $L$ disjoint balls $B_i' \subset {\rm Int\,}(B\setminus (D_{\mathrm{ot}}\cup A))$ with an overtwisted disc $(D^i_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (\partial B_i', \xi)$ in each of them.
nodes.statement_short: Get disjoint overtwisted balls inside $B$ by Proposition 3.8

nodes.name: Connect holes to overtwisted balls by transverse parametric paths (Lemma 9.1)
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma \ref{lm:choosing-paths}, proven in Section \ref{sec:foliations-proofs} below, that for each $j$ we can find a parametric family of embedded paths $^{T_j}\gamma_j$ connecting $^{T_j}B_j$ to $^{T_j}B'_j$ in $T\times(M\setminus A\cup D_{\mathrm{ot}})$. Moreover, using Gromov's parametric $h$-principle for transverse paths, see \cite{Gr-PDR}, we can assume the constructed paths are transverse.
nodes.statement_short: Connect holes to overtwisted balls by transverse parametric paths (Lemma 9.1)

nodes.name: Form parametric ambient boundary connected sums
nodes.statement: As we explain in Section~\ref{sec:BCS}, with these parametric paths we can form disjoint parametric ambient boundary connected sums ${}^{T_j}C_j \subset {}^{T_j}(M \setminus (A \cup D_{\mathrm{ot}}))$ for each $j=1, \dots, L$, between the fibered shells $^{T_j}B_j$ and $^{T_j}B'_j$. Furthermore, by Section~\ref{sec:BCS} and property (ii) above we have isomorphisms of fibered almost contact structures $$ ({}^{T_i}C_i, {}^{T_i}\xi) \cong ({}^{T_i}B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}} \# {}^{T_i}B_i',\, {}^{T_i}\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}} \# {}^{T_i}\xi). $$
nodes.statement_short: Form parametric ambient boundary connected sums

nodes.name: Fill each connected sum by Proposition 3.11
nodes.statement: Applying Proposition~\ref{p:ConnectSumDisc-param} inductively for $j=1,\dots, L$ we deform ${}^T\xi$ on these connected sums relative to their boundary to get a fibered genuine contact structure on ${}^{T}M$.
nodes.statement_short: Fill each connected sum by Proposition 3.11

nodes.name: Arrange $M\setminus f(N)$ overtwisted and $M$ open, overtwisted at infinity
nodes.statement: By an isotopy of $f$ we can arrange that the complement $M\setminus f(N)$ is overtwisted and the closure $f(N)$ is compact. Then, slightly reducing if necessary the manifold $M$, we can assume it non-compact and overtwisted at infinity.
nodes.statement_short: Arrange $M\setminus f(N)$ overtwisted and $M$ open, overtwisted at infinity

nodes.name: Exhaust $N$ by compact sets $C_j$
nodes.statement: Let us exhaust $N$ by compact subsets: $N=\bigcup\limits_1^\infty C_j$, such that $C_j\Subset{\rm Int\,} C_{j+1}$ and $V\setminus C_j$ is connected, $ j=1,\dots $. Set $C_0:=\varnothing$.
nodes.statement_short: Exhaust $N$ by compact sets $C_j$

nodes.name: Inductive claim: extend the contact region from $C_{j-1}$ to $C_j$
nodes.statement: The result follows by induction from the following claim: {\em Suppose we are given an embedding $f^{j-1}:N\to M$ which is contact on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, C_{j-1}$ and a homotopy of bundle isomorphisms $\Phi^{j-1}_{t} :TN\to TM$ covering $f^{j-1}$ such that the following property ${\rm P}^{j-1}$ is satisfied: \begin{description} \item{${\rm P}^{j-1}:$} The homotopy $\Phi^{j-1}_t$ is contact on $T(N)|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, C_{j-1}}$ for all $t\in[0,1]$, $\Phi^{j-1}_0$ is contact everywhere, and $\Phi^{j-1}_1=df^{j-1}$. \end{description} Then there exists a pair $(f^j,\Phi_t^j)$ which satisfies ${\rm P}^{j}$ and such that $f^{j-1}$ and $f^j$ are isotopic via an isotopy fixed on $C_{j-1}$.}
nodes.statement_short: Inductive claim: extend the contact region from $C_{j-1}$ to $C_j$

nodes.name: Inductive hypothesis on $(f^{j-1},\Phi^{j-1}_t)$
nodes.statement: {\em Suppose we are given an embedding $f^{j-1}:N\to M$ which is contact on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, C_{j-1}$ and a homotopy of bundle isomorphisms $\Phi^{j-1}_{t} :TN\to TM$ covering $f^{j-1}$ such that the following property ${\rm P}^{j-1}$ is satisfied:
nodes.statement_short: Inductive hypothesis on $(f^{j-1},\Phi^{j-1}_t)$

nodes.name: Property $P^{j-1}$
nodes.statement: {${\rm P}^{j-1}:$} The homotopy $\Phi^{j-1}_t$ is contact on $T(N)|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, C_{j-1}}$ for all $t\in[0,1]$, $\Phi^{j-1}_0$ is contact everywhere, and $\Phi^{j-1}_1=df^{j-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Property $P^{j-1}$

nodes.name: Inductive conclusion
nodes.statement: Then there exists a pair $(f^j,\Phi_t^j)$ which satisfies ${\rm P}^{j}$ and such that $f^{j-1}$ and $f^j$ are isotopic via an isotopy fixed on $C_{j-1}$.}
nodes.statement_short: Inductive conclusion

nodes.name: Introduce the family $\xi_t$ of almost contact structures
nodes.statement: Let $\xi_t$ be a family of almost contact structures on $M$ such that $\xi_t=(\Phi^{j-1}_t)_*\zeta$ on $f^{j-1}(C_j)$ and $\xi_t=\xi$ outside $f^{j-1}(C_{j+1})$. We note that $\xi_0=\xi$ on $f^{j-1}(C_j)$, and $\xi_t=\xi$ on $f^{j-1}(C_{j-1})$ for all $t\in[0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the family $\xi_t$ of almost contact structures

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2 gives a homotopy of genuine contact structures $\widetilde\xi_t$
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:main} allows us to construct a compactly supported homotopy $\widetilde \xi_{t}$ of {\em genuine} contact structures on $M$, $t\in[0,1]$, connecting $\widetilde \xi_0=\xi$ and a contact structure $\widetilde\xi_1$ which coincides with $\xi_1$ on $f^{j-1}(C_j)$. Moreover, this can be done to ensure existence of a homotopy $\Psi_t:TM\to TM$ of bundle isomorphisms such that $\Psi_0=\mathrm {Id}$, $\Psi_t^*\widetilde\xi_t=\xi_t$, and $\Psi_t|_{f^{j-1}(C_{j-1})}=\mathrm {Id}$, $t\in[0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.2 gives a homotopy of genuine contact structures $\widetilde\xi_t$

nodes.name: Gray's theorem gives a diffeotopy $\phi_t$
nodes.statement: Then Gray's theorem \cite{Gray59} provides us with a compactly supported diffeotopy $\phi_t:M\to M$, $t\in[0,1]$, such that $\phi_0=\mathrm {Id}$, $\phi_t^*\xi =\widetilde \xi_{t}$ and $\phi_t|_{f^{j-1}(C_{j-1})}=\mathrm {Id}$.
nodes.statement_short: Gray's theorem gives a diffeotopy $\phi_t$

nodes.name: Define $f^j$, $\Phi^j_t$ and verify $\Phi^j_t$ is contact on $C_j$
nodes.statement: Set $f^j:=\phi_1\circ f^{j-1}$ and $\Phi^j_{t}:= d\phi_t\circ \Psi_t^*\circ\Phi^{j-1}$, $t\in[0,1]$. Then $\Phi^j_1=df^j$, $(\Phi^j_t)^*\xi= (\Phi^{j-1}_t)^*\circ(\Psi_{t}) \circ (d\phi_t)^*\xi= (\Phi^{j-1}_t)^*\circ\Psi_t^*\widetilde\xi_{t}= (\Phi^{j-1}_t)^*\xi_t$. Hence, $(\Phi^j_t)^*\xi|_{C_j}=\zeta$ for all $t\in[0,1]$. We also have $(\Psi^j_0)^*\xi=\zeta$ everywhere.
nodes.statement_short: Define $f^j$, $\Phi^j_t$ and verify $\Phi^j_t$ is contact on $C_j$

nodes.name: Property $P^j$ holds; induction completes
nodes.statement: Thus, the pair $(f^j,\Phi^j_t)$ satisfies ${\rm P}^{j}$, and the claim follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: Property $P^j$ holds; induction completes

nodes.name: Goal: build an isomorphic model for $\Phi_*K$
nodes.statement: For a given model $(B_{K,C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$ we will build a model $(B_{\Phi_*K,\tilde{C}}, \eta_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{\rho}})$ such that the two models are isomorphic as almost contact structures.
nodes.statement_short: Goal: build an isomorphic model for $\Phi_*K$

nodes.name: Define fiberwise diffeomorphisms $\phi_{(x,t)}$ and $\tilde\rho$
nodes.statement: For $\tilde{C} + {\rm min}(\Phi_*K) > 0$, pick a family of diffeomorphisms for $(x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$ $$ \phi_{(x,t)}: [0, K(x,t)+C] \to [0, c_{\Phi}(x)K(x,t) + \tilde{C}] $$ and define a smooth family of functions for $(x, t) \in \Delta \times S^1$ $$ \tilde{\rho}_{(\Phi(x), t)}: [0, c_{\Phi}(x)K(x,t) + \tilde{C}] \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad \mbox{by}\quad \tilde{\rho}_{(\Phi(x), t)}(v) = c_\Phi(x) \rho_{(x,t)}(\phi_{(x,t)}^{-1}(v)). $$
nodes.statement_short: Define fiberwise diffeomorphisms $\phi_{(x,t)}$ and $\tilde\rho$

nodes.name: $\tilde\rho$ is admissible given the boundary normalization
nodes.statement: One see one $\tilde{\rho}$ satisfies the conditions in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoS1} to define $(B_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{C}}, \eta_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{\rho}})$ provided $$ \mbox{$\phi_{(x,t)}(v) = c_{\Phi}(x)(v - C)+ \tilde{C}$ \quad for \quad $(x,t,v) \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{v = K(x,t) +C\}$.} $$
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde\rho$ is admissible given the boundary normalization

nodes.name: $\widehat\Phi$ is an isomorphism of almost contact structures
nodes.statement: It follows by construction that the diffeomorphism $$ \widehat\Phi: (B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}) \to (B_{\Phi_*K, \tilde{C}}, \eta_{\Phi_*K,\tilde{\rho}}) \quad\mbox{defined by}\quad \widehat\Phi(x,v,t) = (\Phi(x), \phi_{(x,t)}(v), t) $$ is an isomorphism of almost contact structures.
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat\Phi$ is an isomorphism of almost contact structures

nodes.name: Conditions (i)-(iv) hold for $\tilde K_\delta$
nodes.statement: Provided $\delta$ is sufficiently close to $1$, it is clear that $$ \tilde{K}_\delta := (C_\delta)_* K_{\delta} = \frac{K \circ C_\delta^{-1}}{\delta} + \frac{\delta -1}{\delta} $$ satisfies items (i)-(iv) in Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam} with $\tilde{z}_D = z_D / \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Conditions (i)-(iv) hold for $\tilde K_\delta$

nodes.name: Rescaled $\tilde k_\delta$ satisfies the subscaling inequality
nodes.statement: If $k: {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is the special function for $K$, then let $\tilde{k}_\delta(u) := \tfrac{k(\delta u)}{\delta} + \tfrac{\delta-1}{\delta}$. Using that $k$ is special, computing for $a > 1$ and recalling $\delta < 1$, we see $$ a\,\tilde{k}_\delta(u/a) -\tilde{k}_{\delta}(u) < (a-1)\tfrac{\delta - 1}{\delta} < 0 $$ so therefore $\tilde{k}_\delta$ is special provided $\delta$ is close enough to $1$ so that $\tilde{k}_\delta(1) > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescaled $\tilde k_\delta$ satisfies the subscaling inequality

nodes.name: Condition (v) holds with $\tilde k_\delta$
nodes.statement: Therefore item (v) in Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam} holds for $\tilde{K}_\delta$ with respect to $\tilde{k}_\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (v) holds with $\tilde k_\delta$

nodes.name: Introduce the family $K_\delta=K+(\delta-1)$
nodes.statement: Consider an overtwisted disc $(D_{K}, \eta_{K})$ defined by a special contact Hamiltonian $K: \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$. For $\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]$, let $\Delta_\delta = \{\abs{z} \leq \delta,\, u \leq \delta\}$ and consider the family of contact Hamiltonians $$ K_{\delta}: \Delta_\delta \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{where}\quad K_{\delta}:= K + (\delta - 1). $$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the family $K_\delta=K+(\delta-1)$

nodes.name: The spheres $\partial B_{K_\delta}$ foliate a neighborhood
nodes.statement: Observe any neighborhood of $(\partial B_{K}, \eta_{K})$ contains a foliation $\{(\partial B_{K_{\delta}}, \eta_{K_{\delta}})\}_{\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]}$ provided $\varepsilon > 0$ is small enough.
nodes.statement_short: The spheres $\partial B_{K_\delta}$ foliate a neighborhood

nodes.name: Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3 identify them with special models
nodes.statement: Furthermore, when $\varepsilon > 0$ is sufficiently small, Lemmas~\ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} and \ref{lem:Scale} give us a family of special contact Hamiltonians $\{\tilde{K}_\delta: \Delta_{{\rm cyl}} \to {\mathbb{R}}\}_{\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]}$ such that $\tilde{K}_\delta < K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ together with contactomorphisms $$ (\partial B_{K_{\delta}}, \eta_{K_{\delta}}) \cong (\partial B_{\tilde{K}_{\delta}}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_{\delta}})\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3 identify them with special models

nodes.name: Conclude a foliation by overtwisted discs
nodes.statement: Therefore every neighborhood of $(D_{K}, \eta_{K})$ contains a foliation $\{(D_{K_{\delta}}, \eta_{K_{\delta}})\}_{\delta \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]}$ of overtwisted discs.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude a foliation by overtwisted discs

nodes.name: WLOG $\Delta\subset{\rm Int}\,\Delta'$ via Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Since $\Delta'$ is star-shaped, there is a contactomorphism $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1})$ such that $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Phi(\Delta')$ and therefore by Lemma~\ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} without loss of generality we may assume $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta'$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $\Delta\subset{\rm Int}\,\Delta'$ via Lemma 4.2

nodes.name: Choose $C'$ and $\rho'$ with (14) and (15)
nodes.statement: Given the contact shell structure $(B_{K, C}, \eta_{K, \rho})$, pick any contact shell $(B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!,\rho'})$ subject to the additional conditions that \begin{equation} K'(x,t) + C' > K(x,t) + C \mbox{ for all $(x,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$} \end{equation} and the smooth family of functions $\rho'_{(x,t)} : {\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ for $(x,t) \in \Delta' \times S^1$ satisfy \begin{equation} \rho' = \rho \quad\mbox{on\quad ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, B_{K,C} \subset B_{K',C'}$}, \end{equation} where the latter is always possible since $\Delta \subset {\rm Int\,}(\Delta')$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $C'$ and $\rho'$ with (14) and (15)

nodes.name: Get the inclusion as an embedding of almost contact structures
nodes.statement: By \eqref{e:containCon} we have an inclusion \begin{equation} (B_{K,C}, \eta_{K,\rho}) \subset (B_{K'\!,C'}, \eta_{K'\!,\rho'}) \end{equation} and by \eqref{e:embed} it is an embedding of almost contact structures.
nodes.statement_short: Get the inclusion as an embedding of almost contact structures

nodes.name: Claim: $\Delta'$ can be squeezed into any collar of $\partial\Delta$
nodes.statement: For any neighborhood $U\supset \partial \Delta$ there is a contactomorphism $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1})$ such that $\Phi(\Delta') \subset \Delta$ and $\Phi(\partial \Delta')\subset U$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\Delta'$ can be squeezed into any collar of $\partial\Delta$

nodes.name: WLOG $\Delta'\subset\Delta$ by the flow of $Z$
nodes.statement: To see this first note without loss of generality we may assume $\Delta' \subset \Delta$ by replacing $\Delta'$ with $Z^{-N}(\Delta')$ for $N$ sufficiently large.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $\Delta'\subset\Delta$ by the flow of $Z$

nodes.name: Use the flow of a cut-off contact vector field $\tilde Z$
nodes.statement: After this reduction, the required contactomorphism is given by $\tilde{Z}^T$ for $T$ sufficiently large, where $\tilde{Z}$ is a contact vector field with ${\rm supp}(\tilde{Z}) \subset {\rm Int\,} \Delta$ and $\tilde{Z} = Z$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, Z^{-\varepsilon}(\Delta)$ where $\Delta \setminus Z^{-\varepsilon}(\Delta) \subset U$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
nodes.statement_short: Use the flow of a cut-off contact vector field $\tilde Z$

nodes.name: Define $K'=\Phi^{-1}_*(K|_{\Phi(\Delta')})$
nodes.statement: Now pick $U \supset \partial \Delta$ to be such that $K|_{U \times S^1} > 0$, take the constructed contactomorphism $\Phi$ above, and consider the contact Hamiltonian $K' = \Phi^{-1}_*(K|_{\Phi(\Delta')})$ on $\Delta'$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
nodes.statement_short: Define $K'=\Phi^{-1}_*(K|_{\Phi(\Delta')})$

nodes.name: Conclude domination by Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemmas~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} and \ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} that $(B_K, \eta_K)$ dominates $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$.
nodes.section: 4.2.3 Changing the contactomorphism type of the domain
nodes.statement_short: Conclude domination by Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2

nodes.name: WLOG $K(0)<0$; fix $\delta$, $a$, $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality assume $K(0) < 0$ and pick a $\delta > 0$ such that \begin{align*} K(z) &< -\delta \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [0,a]$ for some $a \in (0,1)$, and}\\ \tilde{K}(z) &> \delta \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [1-\varepsilon, 1]$ for some $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$.} \end{align*}
nodes.section: 4.3.1 Minimal elements up to conjugation in the $3$-dimensional case
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $K(0)<0$; fix $\delta$, $a$, $\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Pick a piecewise-linear stretching diffeomorphism $\Phi$
nodes.statement: For $0 < \sigma \ll 1$, pick a diffeomorphism $\Phi: [-1,1] \to [-1, 1]$ such that linearly $$ \mbox{$[-\sigma,\sigma]$ maps onto $[-1+2\sigma,1-2\sigma]$\quad and\quad $\pm [2\sigma, 1]$ maps onto $\pm [1-\sigma, 1]$.} $$
nodes.section: 4.3.1 Minimal elements up to conjugation in the $3$-dimensional case
nodes.statement_short: Pick a piecewise-linear stretching diffeomorphism $\Phi$

nodes.name: Estimate $\Phi_*K<\tilde K$ on three regions
nodes.statement: Since $(\Phi_*K)(\Phi(z)) = \Phi'(z) K(z)$ we can pick $\sigma$ sufficiently small so that \begin{align*} (\Phi_*K)(z) &< -\tfrac{1-2\sigma}{\sigma}\, \delta < \tilde{K}(z) & \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [0, 1-2\sigma]$}\\ (\Phi_*K)(z) &< 0 < \tilde{K}(z) & \mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [1-2\sigma, 1-\sigma]$}\\ (\Phi_*K)(z) &\leq \tfrac{\sigma}{1-2\sigma}\, {\rm max}(K) < \delta < \tilde{K}(z) &\mbox{ if $\abs{z} \in [1-\sigma, 1]$} \end{align*} and hence get that $\Phi_*K < \tilde{K}$.
nodes.section: 4.3.1 Minimal elements up to conjugation in the $3$-dimensional case
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $\Phi_*K<\tilde K$ on three regions

nodes.name: WLOG radial star-shapedness and $K(0)>0$
nodes.statement: Without loss of generalize assume $\Delta$ is star-shaped with respect to the radial vector field $Z$ and that $K(0) > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG radial star-shapedness and $K(0)>0$

nodes.name: Choose $U$, $T$ and a cut-off contact vector field $\tilde Z$
nodes.statement: Pick a sufficiently small neighborhood $U \ni 0$ so that for some $T >0$: $$ \mbox{$\inf_U(K) > 0$\,, \quad ${\rm supp}(H) \subset Z^T(U)\subset{\rm Int\,} \Delta$\,, \quad and \quad $e^T \inf_U(K) > {\rm max}(H)$} $$ where $Z^t:{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ is the flow of $Z$ and satisfies $(Z^t)^*\lambda_{{\rm st}} = e^t \lambda_{{\rm st}}$. Let $\tilde{Z}$ be another contact vector field supported in ${\rm Int\,}(\Delta)$ and equal to $Z$ on $Z^T(U)$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $U$, $T$ and a cut-off contact vector field $\tilde Z$

nodes.name: The conformal factor $e^T$ gives $\Phi_*K\geq H$
nodes.statement: It follows the contactomorphism $\Phi := \tilde{Z}^T \in {\frak D}_0(\Delta)$ satisfies $\Phi_* K \geq H$ since $$ (\Phi_*K)(x) = (c_\Phi \cdot K)(\Phi^{-1}(x)) \geq e^T \inf_U(K) \geq H(x) \quad\mbox{if $x \in {\rm supp}(H)$} $$ and $\Phi_*K \geq 0$ otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: The conformal factor $e^T$ gives $\Phi_*K\geq H$

nodes.name: Choose modified Hamiltonians $\tilde K_0,\tilde K_1$
nodes.statement: The assumptions ensure we can pick contact Hamiltonians $\tilde{K}_i: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$ defining contact shells $(B_{\tilde{K}_i}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_i})$ so that \begin{enumerate} \item $K_0 \leq \tilde{K}_0$ and $\tilde{K}_1 \leq K_1$, \item $\tilde{K}_0 \leq \tilde{K}_1$ on $\Delta \setminus \tilde{\Delta}$, and \item $-\tilde{K}_i|_{\tilde{\Delta}} \in F_+(\tilde{\Delta})$ for $i=1,2$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose modified Hamiltonians $\tilde K_0,\tilde K_1$

nodes.name: Reduce to the modified Hamiltonians
nodes.statement: By item (i) and Lemma~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} it suffices to show $(B_{\tilde{K}_0}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_0})$ is dominated by $(B_{\tilde{K}_1}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the modified Hamiltonians

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 4.8 on $\tilde\Delta$
nodes.statement: Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:disorder} to item (iii) gives a $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\rm Int\,} \tilde{\Delta})$ such that $$ \Phi_*(\tilde{K}_0|_{\tilde{\Delta}}) \leq \tilde{K}_1|_{\tilde{\Delta}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 4.8 on $\tilde\Delta$

nodes.name: Conclude domination by Lemmas 4.2 and 4.1
nodes.statement: Together with item (ii) this means $\Phi_*\tilde{K}_0 \leq \tilde{K_1}$ where we think of $\Phi \in \mathrm{Cont}_0^c({\rm Int\,} \Delta)$ and therefore $(B_{\tilde{K}_0}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_0})$ is dominated by $(B_{\tilde{K}_1}, \eta_{\tilde{K}_1})$ by Lemmas~\ref{l:PhiToTildePhi} and \ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude domination by Lemmas 4.2 and 4.1

nodes.name: Extend gluing discs to Darboux embeddings
nodes.statement: The gluing discs $\iota_\pm:D \to\partial W_\pm$ extend to Darboux embeddings \begin{equation*} \Phi_\pm: D \times (\mp\ell-\varepsilon, \mp\ell+\varepsilon) \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \iota_\pm (D) \quad\mbox{with } \;\Phi_\pm^* \alpha = dz + \theta \mbox{ and } \Phi_\pm|_{D \times \mp \ell} = \iota_\pm \end{equation*} and moreover one can ensure $\Phi_+^{-1} (\Gamma)=0 \times [-\ell,-\ell+\varepsilon )$ and $\Phi_-^{-1}(\Gamma)=0 \times (\ell-\varepsilon,\ell]$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend gluing discs to Darboux embeddings

nodes.name: Extend over the transverse arc $\Gamma$ by the neighborhood theorem
nodes.statement: By the neighborhood theorem for transverse curves in a contact manifold, for $N > 0$ sufficiently large the embeddings $\Phi_\pm$ can be extended (after possibly decreasing $\varepsilon$) to a contact embedding $$ \Phi: \Big(D \times (-\ell-\varepsilon, \ell+\varepsilon)\Big)\cup \Big(L^{-N}(D) \times [-\ell,\ell] \Big)\cup \Big(D \times (\ell-\varepsilon, \ell+\varepsilon)\Big) \to {\rm Int\,} W, $$ whose image is contained in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\iota_+(D) \cup \Gamma \cup \iota_-(D))$ and such that $\Phi(0 \times [-\ell,\ell])=\Gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend over the transverse arc $\Gamma$ by the neighborhood theorem

nodes.name: Embed the tube and the abstract connected sum
nodes.statement: Picking $\beta:[-\ell,\ell]\to{\mathbb{R}}_{\geq 0}$ such that the tube $$T= \{(p,z) \in [-\ell, \ell] \times {\mathbb{R}}^{2n} : p \in L^{-\beta(z)}D \} $$ is contained in the domain of $\Phi$, we can now use $\Phi$ to define the required contact embedding $(W_+ \#_{T} W_-, \xi \#_{T} \xi) \to (W,\xi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Embed the tube and the abstract connected sum

nodes.name: Reduce to the model $B_K\#{\bf B}$ by domination
nodes.statement: It suffices to prove $(B_K \# {\bf B}, \eta_K \# \xi_{\bf B})$ is equivalent to a genuine contact structure, since it is dominated by $(B_{K_0} \# B, \eta_{K_0} \# \xi)$ if we pick $\varepsilon' > 0$ sufficiently small in the definition of $({\bf B}, \xi_{\bf B})$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the model $B_K\#{\bf B}$ by domination

nodes.name: Get shell embeddings $\widehat\Theta_\sigma$ with $\widehat\Theta_1$ a subordina
nodes.statement: By Lemmas~\ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus}, \ref{l:PhiToTildePhi}, and \ref{lem:contain} we can pick a family of contact shell structures on $(B_{K} \# B_{K}, \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho^{\sigma}})$ such that there is a family of contact shell embeddings \begin{equation} \widehat\Theta_\sigma: (B_{K'}, \eta_{K'}) \to (B_{K} \# B_{K}, \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}}) \end{equation} with $\widehat\Theta_1$ a subordination map. We can arrange that $\eta_{K\#K, \hat\rho_0} = \eta_K \# \eta_K$ and for all $\sigma \in [0,1]$ to have $$ \mbox{$\eta_{K\#K, \hat\rho_{\sigma}} = \eta_{K} \# \eta_{K}$ \quad on \quad ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota\{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$} $$ where $\hat\iota: B_{K} \to B_K \# B_K$ is the inclusion into the right hand factor.
nodes.statement_short: Get shell embeddings $\widehat\Theta_\sigma$ with $\widehat\Theta_1$ a subordination

nodes.name: Choose an isotopy $\Psi_\sigma$ realizing $\widehat\Theta_\sigma$
nodes.statement: We can pick an isotopy $\{\Psi_{\sigma}\}_{\sigma \in [0,1]}$ of $B_K \# B_K$ based at the identity and supported away from the boundary such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\Psi_\sigma \circ \hat\iota = \widehat\Theta_\sigma: B_{K'} \to B_K \# B_K$\,, \item $\Psi_\sigma = \mathrm {Id}$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota\{z \in [z_D, 1]\}$\,, \mbox{ and} \item $\Psi_1(B_K \# {\bf A}) = (B_K \# B_K) \setminus {\rm Int\,} \widehat\Theta(B_{K'})$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose an isotopy $\Psi_\sigma$ realizing $\widehat\Theta_\sigma$

nodes.name: Check $\xi_\sigma=\Psi_\sigma^*\eta$ is fixed near the boundary
nodes.statement: Observe that a point in ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_K \# {\bf B})$ is one of the following regions \begin{enumerate} \item ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_K \# B_K)$ where $\Psi_\sigma = \mathrm {Id}$ and $\eta_K \# \eta_{\bf B} = \eta_K \# \eta_K = \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}}$ \item ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota(\{z = z_D\})$ where $\Psi_\sigma = \mathrm {Id}$ and $\eta_K \# \eta_{\bf B} = \eta_K \# \eta_K = \eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}}$ \item ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \hat\iota(\partial B_{K'})$ where $\eta_{K}\#\eta_{\bf B} = \hat\iota_*\eta_{K'} = \hat\iota_* \widehat\Theta_{\sigma}^*(\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho^{\sigma}}) = \Psi_{\sigma}^*(\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}})$ \end{enumerate} This shows $\xi_{\sigma} := \Psi_{\sigma}^*(\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_{\sigma}})$ is a family of equivalent contact shells on $B_K \# {\bf B}$ with $\xi_0 = \eta_K \# \eta_{\bf B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Check $\xi_\sigma=\Psi_\sigma^*\eta$ is fixed near the boundary

nodes.name: $\xi_1$ is genuine
nodes.statement: We know $\eta_{K\#K,\hat\rho_1}$ is a contact structure away from ${\rm Int\,} \widehat\Theta(B_{K'})$, since $\widehat\Theta_1$ is a subordination map, and therefore $\xi_1$ is a genuine contact structure on $B_K \# {\bf B}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\xi_1$ is genuine

nodes.name: The proof of Proposition 3.9 runs parametrically
nodes.statement: Inspecting the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:ConnectSumDisc} shows that it can be done parametrically.
nodes.statement_short: The proof of Proposition 3.9 runs parametrically

nodes.name: Families $\widehat\Theta^s_\sigma$, $\Psi^s_\sigma$ and $\hat\zeta^s_\sigma$
nodes.statement: In particular we can get a family of contact shell embeddings $$ \widehat\Theta_\sigma^s: (B_{K'}, \eta_{K'}) \to (B_{K^{(s)}}\#B_K, \eta_{K^{(s)}\#K, \hat\rho_\sigma^s}) $$ and associated isotopies $\{\Psi_\sigma^s\}_{\sigma \in [0,1]}$ of $B_{K^{(s)}} \# B_K$, which lead to contact shell structures $$ \hat\zeta_\sigma^s := (\Psi_\sigma^s)^*(\eta_{K^{(s)}\#K, \hat\rho^\sigma_s}) \mbox{ on $B_{K^{(s)}} \# {\bf B}$} $$ that define a family of fibered contact shells ${}^I \hat\zeta_\sigma$ on ${}^I B_{K}\#{}^I {\bf B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Families $\widehat\Theta^s_\sigma$, $\Psi^s_\sigma$ and $\hat\zeta^s_\sigma$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.4(ii) gives subordination near $s=0$
nodes.statement: It follows from the second part of Lemma~\ref{p:ContEmb} that \begin{equation} \Big((\Theta_\sigma)_*K', \Theta_\sigma(\Delta')\Big) < (K^{(s)}\#K, \Delta \# \Delta) \quad\mbox{if $s \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{0\}$,} \end{equation} and therefore we can arrange for $\widehat\Theta_\sigma^s$ to be a subordination map when $s \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.4(ii) gives subordination near $s=0$

nodes.name: Properties (i)-(iii) of the family $\hat\zeta^s_\sigma$
nodes.statement: With this set-up the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:ConnectSumDisc} shows we can ensure the family of fibered contact shells ${}^I \hat\zeta_\sigma$ is such that ${}^I \hat\zeta_0 = {}^I \zeta$ as well as \begin{enumerate} \item $\hat\zeta_\sigma^s = \zeta^s$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_{K^{(s)}}\# {\bf B})$ for all $s$ and $\sigma$, \item $\hat\zeta_1^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $s$, and \item $\hat\zeta_\sigma^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $(\sigma, s) \in [0,1] \times [0, 3a]$ for some $a > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Properties (i)-(iii) of the family $\hat\zeta^s_\sigma$

nodes.name: Fixed near the boundary
nodes.statement: $\hat\zeta_\sigma^s = \zeta^s$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial(B_{K^{(s)}}\# {\bf B})$ for all $s$ and $\sigma$,
nodes.statement_short: Fixed near the boundary

nodes.name: Genuine at $\sigma=1$
nodes.statement: $\hat\zeta_1^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $s$, and
nodes.statement_short: Genuine at $\sigma=1$

nodes.name: Genuine for small $s$
nodes.statement: $\hat\zeta_\sigma^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $(\sigma, s) \in [0,1] \times [0, 3a]$ for some $a > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Genuine for small $s$

nodes.name: Reparametrize by a cut-off $f(\sigma,s)$
nodes.statement: Pick any smooth function $$ f: [0,1] \times [0,1] \to [0,1] \quad\mbox{with}\quad f(\sigma, s) = \begin{cases} 0 & \mbox{ if $\sigma = 0$}\\ 0 & \mbox{ if $s \in [0, a]$}\\ 1 & \mbox{ if $s \in [2a, 1]$ and $\sigma =1$} \end{cases} $$ and define the family of contact shells $\zeta_\sigma^s := \hat\zeta_{f(\sigma, s)}^s$ on $B_{K^{(s)}}\#{\bf B}$, which represents a homotopy of fibered families of contact shells $$ \{{}^I \zeta_\sigma\}_{\sigma \in [0,1]} \quad\mbox{on}\quad {}^I B_K\# {}^I {\bf B}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Reparametrize by a cut-off $f(\sigma,s)$

nodes.name: The homotopy is relative to the required set
nodes.statement: It follows from item (i) and the fact $f(\sigma, s) = 0$ if $s \in [0,a]$, that this homotopy is relative is the appropriate set.
nodes.statement_short: The homotopy is relative to the required set

nodes.name: $\zeta^s_1$ is genuine for small and large $s$
nodes.statement: Observe that $\zeta_1^s$ is a genuine contact structure for all $s \in [0,1]$, since either $s \leq 3a$ and $\zeta_1^s := \hat\zeta_{f(1,s)}^s$ is a genuine by item (iii), or $s \geq 2a$ and $\zeta_1^s := \hat\zeta_{f(1,s)}^s = \hat\zeta_{1}^s$ is genuine by item (ii).
nodes.statement_short: $\zeta^s_1$ is genuine for small and large $s$

nodes.name: Conclude the desired homotopy
nodes.statement: Therefore we have the desired homotopy between ${}^I \zeta = {}^I \zeta_0$ and a fibered family of genuine contact structures ${}^I \zeta_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the desired homotopy

nodes.name: Recall the fibered shell and reduce to the model ball
nodes.statement: Recall that $({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ is the fibered contact shell, which at the point $\tau \in T = D^q$ is given by $$ (B_{K_{0}^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# B, \eta_{K_{0}^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# \xi) $$ where $\delta: T \to [0,1]$ is a bump function that vanishes near the boundary. It suffices to prove $({}^TB_K \# {}^T{\bf B}, {}^T\eta_{K} \# {}^T\xi_{\bf B})$ is fibered equivalent to a fibered contact structure over $T$, since it is dominated by $({}^TB_{K_0} \# {}^TB, {}^T\eta_{K_0} \# {}^T\xi)$ if we pick $\varepsilon' > 0$ sufficiently small in the definition of $({\bf B}, \xi_{\bf B})$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the fibered shell and reduce to the model ball

nodes.name: Identify fibers with $\zeta^{\delta(\tau)}$
nodes.statement: In the notation of Proposition~\ref{p:LocalConnectSumDisc-param} we have the identification $$ \zeta^{\delta(\tau)} = \eta_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# \xi_{\bf B} \quad\mbox{as contact shell structures on $B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# {\bf B}$} $$ and a fibered contact structure on $({}^TB_K \# {}^T{\bf B}, {}^T\zeta_1)$ with contact structure $$ \zeta^{\delta(\tau)}_1 \mbox{ on the fiber } B_{K^{(\delta(\tau))}} \# {\bf B}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Identify fibers with $\zeta^{\delta(\tau)}$

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 5.3 fiberwise
nodes.statement: Since $\delta(\tau) = 0$ if $\tau \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial T$, the homotopy constructed in Proposition~\ref{p:LocalConnectSumDisc-param} when used fiberwise gives a homotopy between ${}^T\eta_{K} \# {}^T\xi_{\bf B}$ and ${}^T\zeta_1$ that shows they are fibered equivalent.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 5.3 fiberwise

nodes.name: Choose the constant $C$
nodes.statement: Recall $E(u) := K(u, \pm 1) > 0$ with $K \leq E$ and pick a constant \begin{equation} 0 < C < \frac{{\rm min}(E)}{{\rm max}(E)} \leq 1. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.statement_short: Choose the constant $C$

nodes.name: Choose $h$ with small derivative on the neck
nodes.statement: Pick a diffeomorphism $h:[-\ell', \ell'] \to [-\ell, \ell]$ with $h'(z) = 1$ on $z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{\pm \ell\}$ and \begin{equation} h'(h^{-1}(z)) \leq C e^{-\beta(z)} \end{equation} which is possible provided $$ \ell' > \frac{1}{2C} \int_{-\ell}^{\ell} e^{\beta(z)}dz $$ Extend $h$ by translation to get a diffeomorphism $h: {\mathbb{R}} \to {\mathbb{R}}$ and consider the associated contactomorphism $\Phi_h: ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi) \to ({\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}, \xi)$ from \eqref{e:PushS}.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.statement_short: Choose $h$ with small derivative on the neck

nodes.name: $\Phi_h$ maps the long domain into $\Delta\#_{\beta,\ell}\Delta$
nodes.statement: This is the desired contact embedding for by \eqref{e:hprime} we have $$ \Phi_h(\Delta\#_{\ell'}\Delta) = \{u \leq h'(h^{-1}(z))\,,\,\, z \in [-2-\ell, 2+\ell]\} \subset \Delta\#_{\beta,\ell}\Delta\,. $$
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_h$ maps the long domain into $\Delta\#_{\beta,\ell}\Delta$

nodes.name: Check the order on the neck
nodes.statement: To check the order on the Hamiltonians, it suffices to check on $\Phi_h(T_{\ell'})$ where we have $$ (\Phi_h)_*E(u,z) = h'(h^{-1}(z)) E(\tfrac{u}{h'(h^{-1}(z))}) < e^{-\beta(z)} E(u) = (K\#_{\beta}K)(u,z) $$ by \eqref{e:CE} and \eqref{e:hprime}.
nodes.section: 5.3.1 Transverse scaling and simplifying the neck region
nodes.statement_short: Check the order on the neck

nodes.name: Push-forward formula with factor $\tilde h_\sigma\geq1$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{e:PushH} we have $$ (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) = \tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)\,\, K\!\left(\frac{u}{\tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)}, h^{-1}_\sigma(z)\right), $$ where recall from \eqref{e:PushTh} that $$\tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z):= h_\sigma'(h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) - \big(h_\sigma'(h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) - 1\big)u \geq 1$$ where the inequality follows from $h'_\sigma(h^{-1}_\sigma(z)) \geq 1$ and $u \leq 1$.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.statement_short: Push-forward formula with factor $\tilde h_\sigma\geq1$

nodes.name: Piecewise formula (37) for $(\Gamma_\sigma)_*K$
nodes.statement: Bringing these two together, we have \begin{equation} (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, h_\sigma([-1,\, z_D'])\\ \leq k(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in h_\sigma([z_D',\, z_D])\\ K(u,z -(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D+1+\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} \end{equation} using that $h_\sigma$ is translations on the ends, while on the middle we have \begin{align*} (\Gamma_\sigma)_*K(u,z) &= (\Gamma_\sigma)_*k(u,z) = \tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)\,\, k\!\left(\frac{u}{\tilde{h}_\sigma(u,z)}\right) \leq k(u) \end{align*} using \eqref{e:special3} and \eqref{e:subscale}.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.statement_short: Piecewise formula (37) for $(\Gamma_\sigma)_*K$

nodes.name: Part (i): reduce to monotonicity of $K$ in $z$
nodes.statement: To verify $(i)$, since $$ (E\# K)(u,z) = \begin{cases} E(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in [-2-\ell,\, \ell]\\ K(u,z-(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in [\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} $$ it follows from \eqref{e:GsK} and the inequalities \begin{equation} k(u) \leq K(u,z) \leq E(u). \end{equation} that it suffices to check $$ K(u, h_\sigma^{-1}(z)) \leq K(u, z-(1+\ell)) \quad\mbox{when}\quad z \in [\ell,\, h_\sigma(z_D')]. $$ Since $h_\sigma^{-1}(z) = z-(1-2\sigma)(1+\ell)$ here, this is equivalent to $$ K(u, z+2\sigma(1+\ell)) \leq K(u, z) \quad\mbox{when}\quad z \in [-1,\, z_D' -2\sigma(1+\ell)] $$ and this latter condition follows from Definition~\ref{def:SpecialHam}.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.statement_short: Part (i): reduce to monotonicity of $K$ in $z$

nodes.name: Part (ii): compare with $K\#K$ via (38)
nodes.statement: To verify $(ii)$, using \eqref{e:defh} we see \eqref{e:GsK} at $\sigma=1$ becomes $$ (\Gamma_1)_*K(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,z+(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [-2-\ell,\, z_D'-1-\ell]\\ \leq k(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in [z_D' -1-\ell,\, z_D + 1+\ell]\\ K(u,z-(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, [z_D+1+\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} $$ while by definition $$ (K\# K)(u,z) = \begin{cases} K(u,z+(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in [-2-\ell,\, -\ell]\\ E(u) & \mbox{ if } z \in [-\ell,\, \ell]\\ K(u,z-(1+\ell)) & \mbox{ if } z \in [\ell,\, 2+\ell] \end{cases} $$ so $(ii)$ follows from \eqref{e:INEM}.
nodes.section: 5.3.2 The twist contactomorphism and a special case of Lemma~5.4
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii): compare with $K\#K$ via (38)

nodes.name: Fix models and the keyhole domain (41)
nodes.statement: Fix a $C > -{\rm min}\, K$ and a $\rho$ as in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoI} that defines contact shell models $$ \mbox{$(B_K, \eta_{K, \rho})$, $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'\!, \rho})$, and $(B_K^{I}, \eta_{K, \rho}^{I})$.} $$ Take any $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $K|_{\Delta \times [-\varepsilon, \varepsilon]} > \varepsilon$ and consider the domain \begin{align} B_{K}^{\varepsilon} &:= B_K^I\setminus\left(\{v\leq\varepsilon\}\cup\{t\in[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\}\right) \cr&= \{(x,v,t) \in \Delta \times T^*I : \varepsilon\leq v \leq K(x,t)+C\,,\,\, \varepsilon\leq t\leq1-\varepsilon\}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Fix models and the keyhole domain (41)

nodes.name: The keyhole model is dominated by the interval model
nodes.statement: Note that $\eta^I_{K, \rho}$ restricted to $B_{K}^{\varepsilon}$ defines a contact shell $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K,\rho})$ that we will call the {\em keyhole} model, and it follows from \eqref{eq:keyhole} that $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K, \rho})$ is dominated by $(B^I_K,\eta^I_{K, \rho})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: The keyhole model is dominated by the interval model

nodes.name: Remains: keyhole dominates the circle model
nodes.statement: It remains to show for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ the shell $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K,\rho})$ dominates $(B_{K'},\eta_{K'\!,\rho})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Remains: keyhole dominates the circle model

nodes.name: The keyhole also sits inside $B_K$
nodes.statement: Note that $(B_{K}^{\varepsilon}, \eta_{K,\rho}^\varepsilon)$ can be cut out of $(B_K, \eta_{K,\rho})$ by the same inequalities \eqref{eq:keyhole} where $(v,t)$ are viewed as coordinates $v=r^2$ and $t=\frac{\phi}{2\pi}$ on ${\mathbb{R}}^2$, rather then on $T^*I$. This embedding is shown on Figure \ref{fig:keyhole} and explains the term `keyhole'. \begin{figure}\begin{center} \includegraphics[scale=.5]{keyhole.pdf} \caption{The keyhole model inside $B_K$.} \end{center}\end{figure}
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: The keyhole also sits inside $B_K$

nodes.name: Write $\alpha_\rho$ in Cartesian coordinates; genuine near $p=0$, $q\geq-2\delta
nodes.statement: For standard coordinates $(q, p) \in {\mathbb{R}}^2$ where $q = \sqrt{v}\cos(2\pi t)$ and $p = \sqrt{v}\sin(2\pi t)$, by the assumptions on $\rho$ in \eqref{e:FamilyRhoI}, the $1$-form on $\Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2$ defining $\eta_{K, \rho}$ can be written as $$ \alpha_\rho = \lambda_{\rm st} + \frac{\rho(v)}{2\pi v}(qdp-pdq) $$ and on $\Delta \times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{(q,0) \in {\mathbb{R}}^2: q \geq -2\delta\}$ is a genuine contact form for some $\delta >0$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Write $\alpha_\rho$ in Cartesian coordinates; genuine near $p=0$, $q\geq-2\delta$

nodes.name: Choose $k$, $\Gamma_k$ and an isotopy $\psi_s$
nodes.statement: Pick a smooth function $k: \Delta \to [-\delta, \infty)$ such that both $k(x) = -\delta$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial \Delta$ and $k(x) = K(x,0)$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Delta'$, and $$ \Gamma_k := \{(x, q, 0) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 : -2\delta \leq q \leq k(x)\} \subset B_K. $$ Consider a smooth isotopy $\{\psi_s\}_{s \in [0,1]}$ of $\Delta \times \{q \geq -2\delta,\, p = 0\}$ of the form $\psi_s(x,q) = (x, g_s(x,q))$, supported away from $\partial B_K$, and such that $$ \psi_1(\Gamma_k) = \{(x, q, 0) \in \Delta \times {\mathbb{R}}^2 : -2\delta \leq q \leq -\delta\} \subset B_K. $$
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Choose $k$, $\Gamma_k$ and an isotopy $\psi_s$

nodes.name: Extend $\psi_s$ to a contact isotopy by a Moser argument
nodes.statement: Since this isotopy preserves $\alpha_\rho|_{\Delta \times \{p=0\}} = \lambda_{{\rm st}}$, it follows from a Moser-method argument (c.f.\ \cite[Theorem 2.6.13]{Gei08}) that $\psi_s$ can be extended to a contact isotopy $\Psi_s$ of $B_K$ supported in $\Delta \times {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\{(q,0) \in {\mathbb{R}}^2: q \geq -2\delta\}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Extend $\psi_s$ to a contact isotopy by a Moser argument

nodes.name: $\Psi_1$ moves $B_{K'}$ into the keyhole
nodes.statement: If $\varepsilon$ is small enough, then the contactomorphism $\Psi_1$ satisfies $\Psi_1(B_{K'})\subset B_K^\varepsilon$ and hence the keyhole model shell $(B_K^\varepsilon,\eta^\varepsilon_{K, \rho})$ dominates the circular model shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K', \rho})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: $\Psi_1$ moves $B_{K'}$ into the keyhole

nodes.name: Introduce diffeotopies and a modified $\widehat h_t$
nodes.statement: Denote by $h_t$ and $g_t$ the contact diffeotopies generated by $H$ and $G$. Pick a contact diffeotopy such that $\widehat{h}_t = h_t$ on $\partial\Delta$ as $\infty$-jets and $$ \widehat{h}_t =\begin{cases} g_t &\mbox{when $t \in [0,\varepsilon]$}\\ h_t &\mbox{when $t \in [2\varepsilon,1-2\varepsilon]$}\\ g_t \circ g_1^{-1}\circ h_1 &\mbox{when $t \in [1-\varepsilon,1]$} \end{cases} $$
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Introduce diffeotopies and a modified $\widehat h_t$

nodes.name: WLOG $H=G$ near $\partial I$
nodes.statement: Observe $\widehat{H} = G$ when $t \in [0,\varepsilon] \cup [1-\varepsilon, 1]$ if $\widehat{h}_t$ is generated by $\widehat{H}: \Delta \times I \to {\mathbb{R}}$. Hence without loss of generality we may assume $H = G$ when $t \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial I$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $H=G$ near $\partial I$

nodes.name: Pick an isotopy $\psi^s$ matching $h_t$ to $g_t$ near $\partial\Delta$
nodes.statement: Since $h_t$ and $g_t$ are $C^\infty$-small on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta$, we can pick an isotopy $$ \psi^s: \Delta \times I \to \Delta \times I \quad\mbox{for $s\in [0,1]$ with $\psi^0 = \mathrm {Id}$} $$ supported in $\Delta \times {\rm Int\,} I$ and such that for $x \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta$ we have $$ \mbox{$\psi^s(\cdot, t)$ is a contactomorphism and $\psi^1(h_t(x), t) = (g_t(x), t)$.} $$
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Pick an isotopy $\psi^s$ matching $h_t$ to $g_t$ near $\partial\Delta$

nodes.name: Gray-Moser gives a contact isotopy $\tilde\psi_t$
nodes.statement: Applying the Gray--Moser argument parametrically in $t$ builds a contact isotopy $\tilde{\psi}_t$ such that $\tilde{\psi}_t = \mathrm {Id}$ when $t \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial I$ and $\tilde\psi_1(h_t(x)) = g_t(x)$ when $x \in {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \partial\Delta$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Gray-Moser gives a contact isotopy $\tilde\psi_t$

nodes.name: Its generating Hamiltonian is the required $\widetilde H$
nodes.statement: Defining $\tilde{h}_t:= \tilde\psi_t \circ h_t$ and $\widetilde{H}$ to be its generating contact Hamiltonian gives the result.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Its generating Hamiltonian is the required $\widetilde H$

nodes.name: Normalize $B$ and its boundary
nodes.statement: We can assume that $B=\{0\leq v\leq\Phi(w,t): (w,t)\in D\}$, where the function $\Phi $ is positive on ${\rm Int\,} D$ and coincides with $\phi$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D$, and hence $\partial B=D\cup\Gamma$ where $\Gamma:=\{v=\Phi(w,t): (w,t)\in D\}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Normalize $B$ and its boundary

nodes.name: Define the holonomy contactomorphism $f_\phi$
nodes.statement: Given a point $w\in\Delta$, consider a leaf $\ell_w$ through the point $(w,h_-(w)) \in D$ of the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_\phi$ on the graph $\Gamma_\phi:=\{v=\phi(w,t): (w,t)\in D\}$ and let $(w', h_+(w')) \in D$ be the other end of the leaf $\ell_w$. This rule $f_\phi(w):=w'$ defines the holonomy contactomorphism $ f_\phi:\Delta \to\Delta$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Define the holonomy contactomorphism $f_\phi$

nodes.name: Straighten $D$ by the contactomorphism $G$
nodes.statement: Consider the diffeomorphism $G:D\to \widetilde D=\Delta\times[0,1]$ defined by the formula $$G(w,t)=\left(w,\frac{t- h_-(w)}{h_+(w)-h_-(w)}\right).$$ Since $\lambda_{{\rm st}} + vdt$ restricted to $D$ and $\widetilde{D}$ is $\lambda_{{\rm st}}$ and is preserved by $G$, it follows that $G$ extends to a contactomorphism $G:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\widetilde D$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Straighten $D$ by the contactomorphism $G$

nodes.name: Transport $\phi$ near the boundary and extend to $\widetilde\phi$
nodes.statement: The diffeomorphism $G$ moves the graph of the function $\phi|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D}$ onto a graph of some function $ \widetilde \phi:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\widetilde D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ whose $\infty$-jet vanishes on $\partial\widetilde D$. Pick any smooth extension $\widetilde \phi: \widetilde{D} \to {\mathbb{R}}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Transport $\phi$ near the boundary and extend to $\widetilde\phi$

nodes.name: Holonomy of $\widetilde\phi$ is a time-one contact map
nodes.statement: The characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_{\widetilde\phi}$ on the graph $\Gamma_{\widetilde\phi} = \{v=\widetilde\phi(w,t): (w,t)\in \widetilde{D}\}$ is represented by $\tfrac{\partial}{\partial t} - X_{\widetilde\phi_t}$ where $X_{\widetilde\phi_t}$ is the contact vector field on $\Delta$ for $\widetilde\phi_t: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$ thought of as a contact Hamiltonian. It follows that the holonomy contactomorphism $f_{\widetilde\phi}:\Delta\to\Delta$, defined similarly to $f_\phi$, coincides with the time one map of the contact isotopy of $\Delta$ defined by $-\widetilde\phi:\Delta\times[0,1]\to{\mathbb{R}}$ thought of as a time-dependent contact Hamiltonian.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Holonomy of $\widetilde\phi$ is a time-one contact map

nodes.name: Lemma 6.8 matches the holonomies
nodes.statement: According to Lemma \ref{lm:boundary-behavior} we can modify $\widetilde\phi$, keeping it fixed over ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D$, to make the holonomy contactomorphism $f_{\widetilde\phi}$ equal to $f_\phi$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6.8 matches the holonomies

nodes.name: Build a contactomorphism $F$ between the graphs
nodes.statement: Since the holonomy maps $f_{\widetilde\phi}$ and $f_\phi$ are equal, it follows that there is a diffeomorphism $F:\Gamma_\phi\to \Gamma_{\widetilde\phi}$ equal to $G$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{\partial\Gamma_\phi}$, mapping the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_\phi$ to the characteristic foliation $\mathcal{F}_{\widetilde\phi}$, and with the form $$F(w,t,\phi(v,t))=(f(w,t), \widetilde\phi(f(w,t))) \quad\mbox{for $(v,t)\in D$}$$ for some diffeomorphism $f:D\to\widetilde D$. It follows that $F$ extends to a contactomorphism of neighborhoods $F: {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma_\phi \to {\mathcal O}{\it p}\, \Gamma_{\widetilde\phi}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Build a contactomorphism $F$ between the graphs

nodes.name: Define $\widetilde B$ and the boundary map $H$
nodes.statement: Let $(\widetilde B,\sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ be a contact saucer over $\widetilde D$, where $\widetilde B=\{0\leq v\leq\widetilde\Phi(w,t),\, (w,t)\in\widetilde D\}$ for some function $\widetilde\Phi:\widetilde D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ that coincides with $\widetilde\phi$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\widetilde D$ and is positive on ${\rm Int\,}\widetilde D$. Note $\partial\widetilde B=\widetilde D\cup\widetilde \Gamma$ where $\widetilde\Gamma:=\{v=\widetilde\Phi(w,t),\, (w,t)\in\widetilde D\}$. Let us define a diffeomorphism $H:\partial B\to\partial\widetilde B$ so that $$ H|_{{\mathcal O}{\it p}\, D}=G\;\;\; \hbox{and} \;\;\; H|_{\Gamma}(w,t,\Phi(v,t))=(f(w,t),\widetilde\Phi(f(v,t))).$$
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Define $\widetilde B$ and the boundary map $H$

nodes.name: Extend $H$ to an equivalence of saucers
nodes.statement: This diffeomorphism matches the traces of contact structures on the boundaries $\partial B$ and $\partial\widetilde B$ of the saucers, and hence extends to a contactomorphism between ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial B$ and ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\widetilde B$ which can be further extended to an equivalence between the saucers $(B,\sigma_\phi)$ and $(\widetilde B, \sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Extend $H$ to an equivalence of saucers

nodes.name: Put $\zeta$ in the normal form $(B,\sigma_\phi)$
nodes.statement: By the definition of regular semi-contact saucer from Section~\ref{sec:saucers}, we may assume that $\zeta = (B, \sigma_\phi)$ where $B$ is defined over a regular domain $D\subset\Pi:=\{v=0\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}$ and $\sigma_\phi$ is given by a family of contact structures $\zeta_s$ on neighborhoods of graphs $D_s:=\{y_n=s\phi(w),\; w\in D\}$ where $\phi:D\to{\mathbb{R}}$ is a $C^\infty$-function supported in $D$ which is positive on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial D\cap{\rm Int\,} D$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Put $\zeta$ in the normal form $(B,\sigma_\phi)$

nodes.name: Regularity makes $\Delta=\pi(D)$ star-shaped
nodes.statement: By the regularity assumption of $D$ the projection $\pi:D\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$ is equivalent to the linear projection of the round ball and the image $\Delta=\pi(D)$ is contactomorphic to a star-shaped domain in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Regularity makes $\Delta=\pi(D)$ star-shaped

nodes.name: Choose $\Delta'$, $D'$ and functions $h_\pm$
nodes.statement: Choose a slightly smaller star shaped ball $\Delta'\subset{\rm Int\,} \Delta$ such that $\phi|_{{\rm Int\,} D \setminus {\rm Int\,} D'}>0$ where $D':=\pi^{-1}(\Delta')\cap D$. Note that the characteristic foliation on $D'$ is \emph{not} a regular foliation, rather it is diffeomorphic to the product foliation of the $2n-1$ disc and the interval. There exist functions $h_\pm:\Delta'\to{\mathbb{R}}$, $h_-<h_+$, such that $D'= \{(w,t);\; h_-(w)\leq t\leq h_+(w), \; w\in\Delta'\}\subset\Pi$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\Delta'$, $D'$ and functions $h_\pm$

nodes.name: A smaller saucer $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$ is dominated
nodes.statement: Choose a function $\phi':D'\to{\mathbb{R}}$ that defines an immersion type semi-contact saucer $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$ over $D'$ such that $\phi'\leq\phi|_{D'}$ and hence $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$ is dominated by $(B, \sigma_\phi)$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: A smaller saucer $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$ is dominated

nodes.name: Lemma 6.9 straightens it to a saucer over $\Delta'\times[0,1]$
nodes.statement: Hence, we can apply Lemma \ref{lm:two-saucers} and find a function $\widetilde\phi:\widetilde D:=\Delta'\times[0,1]\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which is positive near $\partial \widetilde D$ and such that the corresponding saucer $(\widetilde B, \sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ over $\widetilde D$ is equivalent to $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6.9 straightens it to a saucer over $\Delta'\times[0,1]$

nodes.name: Rescale by an affine contactomorphism
nodes.statement: Let us rescale the saucer $(\widetilde B,\sigma_{\widetilde\phi})$ by an affine contactomorphism of ${\mathbb{R}}^{2n+1}_{\rm st}$ $$(z,u,\varphi, t,v)\mapsto \left((1+\delta)^2z, (1+\delta)^2u, \varphi, (1+\delta) t-\frac\delta2, (1+\delta)v\right)$$ for $\delta > 0$, to an equivalent saucer $(\widehat B, \sigma_{\widehat\phi})$ over the domain $\widehat D:=\widehat \Delta\times[-\frac\delta2,1+\frac\delta2]$. The notation $\varphi$ stands for the tuple $(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_{n-1})$ of angular coordinates. Note that $\Delta'\subset{\rm Int\,}\widehat \Delta$ and we may choose $\delta$ sufficiently small so that $\widehat\phi|_{{\rm Int\,}\widehat D\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widetilde D}>0$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Rescale by an affine contactomorphism

nodes.name: Read off an interval model dominated by $\zeta$
nodes.statement: Then the restriction $K:=\widehat\phi|_{\widetilde D} $ of the function $\widehat \phi$ to the domain $\widetilde D=\Delta'\times[0,1]$ defines an interval model shell $(B^I_K,\eta^I_K)$. It is dominated by the saucer $(\widehat B, \sigma_{\widehat\phi})$, which is equivalent to $(B',\sigma_{\phi'})$, which is in turn dominated by $(B,\sigma_{\phi})$ .
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Read off an interval model dominated by $\zeta$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.7: an interval model below $\zeta$
nodes.statement: We first use Proposition \ref{lm: saucer dom interval} to find a dominated by $\zeta$ interval model $\eta^I_{\widetilde K}$ for some ${\widetilde K}:D\times I \to {\mathbb{R}}$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 6.7: an interval model below $\zeta$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.5: a circle model below it
nodes.statement: Then, we apply Proposition \ref{l:equiv12} to get a circular model contact shell $(B_{K'}, \eta_{K'})$ dominated by $\left(B^I_{\widetilde K}, \eta^I_{\widetilde K}\right))$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 6.5: a circle model below it

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 with a time-independent $K<K'$
nodes.statement: Finally, choosing a time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K<K'$ and applying Lemma \ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} we get the required circle model contact shell $\left(B_K, \eta_K\right)$ dominated by $ (B, \xi)$.
nodes.section: 6.6 Relations between the model contact shells
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.1 with a time-independent $K<K'$

nodes.name: Gromov's h-principle: genuine off an annulus $C$
nodes.statement: Choose an embedded annulus $C=S^{2n}\times[0,1]\subset M\setminus A$ and first use the existence part of Gromov's $h$-principle \ref{thm:Gromov-open}, to deform $\xi_0$ relative to $A$ to an almost contact structure which is genuine on $M\setminus C$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Gromov's h-principle: genuine off an annulus $C$

nodes.name: Parametric h-principle: semi-contact on $C$
nodes.statement: Next with use the $1$-parametric part of Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open}, applied to the family of neighborhoods of spheres $S^{2n}\times t$ for $t\in[0,1]$ to make the almost contact structure semi-contact on $C$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Parametric h-principle: semi-contact on $C$

nodes.name: Conclude by Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement: Finally we use Lemma \ref{lm:annuli-to-saucers} to complete the proof.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by Lemma 7.2

nodes.name: View $\zeta_s$ on a fixed collar
nodes.statement: Choose $\varepsilon>0$ such that the contact structure $\zeta_s$ is defined on $\Sigma\times[s-\varepsilon,s+\varepsilon]$ for each $s\in[a,b]$. We will view $\zeta_s$ as a family of contact structures on $\Sigma\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: View $\zeta_s$ on a fixed collar

nodes.name: Darboux-Moser isotopy makes short pieces of immersion type
nodes.statement: For each $s_0$ and $\sigma > 0$ sufficiently small, a Darboux-Moser type argument implies there is an isotopy $\phi^{s_0}_s: \Sigma \times [-\sigma, \sigma] \to \Sigma \times [-\varepsilon, \varepsilon]$ such that $\phi^{s_0}_{s_0} = \mathrm {Id}$ and $(\phi^{s}_{s_0})^*\zeta_s = \zeta_{s_0}$ for $s \in [s_0, s_0+\sigma]$. Moreover by shrinking $\sigma$ if necessary we can ensure that the hypersurfaces $\phi_{s_0}^s(\Sigma\times 0)$ are graphical in $\Sigma\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Darboux-Moser isotopy makes short pieces of immersion type

nodes.name: Choose $N>1/\sigma$
nodes.statement: Hence for any $s_0\in[a,b]$ the restriction of $\zeta_s$ to $[s_0, s_0+\sigma]$ is of immersion type and therefore choosing $N>\frac1\sigma$ we get the required partition of $\Sigma\times[a,b]$ into the annuli of immersion type.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Choose $N>1/\sigma$

nodes.name: Reduce to immersion type by Lemma 7.3
nodes.statement: Let us endow $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ with the product metric. Using Lemma \ref{lm:partition-to-special} we may assume, by passing to a partition, that the semi-contact structure $\{\xi_s\}$ on the annulus $C$ is of immersion type.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to immersion type by Lemma 7.3

nodes.name: Introduce $\mu$, $\Psi_s$, $\psi_s$ with $\psi_1$ $C^1$-small
nodes.statement: So there is a contact structure $\mu$ on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ and a smooth family of embeddings $$\Psi_s: \widehat{C}:=\Sigma \times [-\delta, \delta] \to \Sigma\times[-R,R] \quad\mbox{for $s \in [0,1]$}$$ such that $\Psi_s(x, u) = (x, \psi_s(x)+u)$ for $u\in[-\delta,\delta]$, and $\Psi_s^*\mu$ is identified with $\zeta_s$. Furthermore, the partition argument also allows us to assume that $\psi_0=0$ and that the $C^1$-norm of $\psi_1$ is arbitrary small. We will impose the appropriate bound on its $C^1$-norm further down in the proof.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\mu$, $\Psi_s$, $\psi_s$ with $\psi_1$ $C^1$-small

nodes.name: Define the nearly tangent set $\widehat V=\widehat V_+\cup\widehat V_-$
nodes.statement: Define a subset \begin{align*} \widehat V&:=\left\{x\in\Sigma: \mbox{ the angle between } \mu_{x,0} \hbox{ and } T_{x,0}\Sigma \;\hbox {in $T_{x,0}\widehat{C}$ is at most } \tfrac\pi4\right\}.\\ \end{align*} Assuming $\mu$ and $\Sigma$ cooriented, we present $\widehat V$ as a disjoint union $\widehat V=\widehat V_+\cup \widehat V_-$ defined by whether the vector field $\frac{\partial}{\partial u}$ defines the same or opposite coorientation of $\mu|_\Sigma $ and $T\Sigma$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Define the nearly tangent set $\widehat V=\widehat V_+\cup\widehat V_-$

nodes.name: Choose a contact form with Reeb field $\pm\partial_u$ on $\widehat V_\pm$
nodes.statement: We can choose a contact form $\alpha$ for $\mu$ such that its Reeb vector field $\frak{R}$ satisfies $\frak{R}(x,u)=\pm\frac{\partial}{\partial u}$ for $x\in\widehat V_\pm$ and $u\leq\sigma$ for a sufficiently small $\sigma>0$. We will assume $\sigma>0$ small enough to also ensure that $$\abs{\mbox{angle}(\mu_{x,u},\mu_{x,0}) } \leq \tfrac{ \pi}{16}$$ for $x\in\Sigma$ and $|u|\leq\sigma$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Choose a contact form with Reeb field $\pm\partial_u$ on $\widehat V_\pm$

nodes.name: Define the Hamiltonian $H$
nodes.statement: Consider any smooth function $H:\Sigma\to[-1,1]$ equal to $\pm 1$ on $\widehat V_{\pm}$. We further extend this function to $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ as independent of the coordinate $u$ and then multiply by the cut-off function $\beta(u)$ equal to $1$ on $[-\frac R3,\frac R3]$ and equal to $0$ outside $[-\frac R2,\frac R2]$. We will keep the notation $H$ for the resulting function on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Define the Hamiltonian $H$

nodes.name: Flow for a short time $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Let $h_t:\Sigma\times[-R,R]\to\Sigma\times[-R,R]$. $t\in[0,1]$, be the contact isotopy generated by $H$ as its contact Hamiltonian. Choose $\varepsilon\in(0,\frac\sigma2)$ so small that $dh_\varepsilon$ rotates any hyperplane by an angle $<\frac\pi{16}$ and $||h_\varepsilon||_{C^0}<\sigma$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Flow for a short time $\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Properties of the pushed graph $\Gamma_\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Then $\Gamma_\varepsilon:=h_\varepsilon(\Sigma\times0)$ is graphical, $\Gamma_\varepsilon=\{u=\phi_\varepsilon(x)\}$ for a function $\phi_\varepsilon:\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which satisfies the following conditions \begin{itemize} \item $\phi_\varepsilon|_{\widehat V}=\varepsilon$; \item for every $x\in\widehat W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widehat V$ we have ${\mathrm{angle}}(T_{z}\Sigma,\mu_z)>\frac\pi8$, $z=(x,\phi_\varepsilon(x))\in\Gamma_\varepsilon$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Properties of the pushed graph $\Gamma_\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Height $\varepsilon$ on $\widehat V$
nodes.statement: $\phi_\varepsilon|_{\widehat V}=\varepsilon$;
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Height $\varepsilon$ on $\widehat V$

nodes.name: Transversality off $\widehat V$
nodes.statement: for every $x\in\widehat W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widehat V$ we have ${\mathrm{angle}}(T_{z}\Sigma,\mu_z)>\frac\pi8$, $z=(x,\phi_\varepsilon(x))\in\Gamma_\varepsilon$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Transversality off $\widehat V$

nodes.name: Properties of the pushed second graph
nodes.statement: As it was explained above, the function $\psi_1\colon\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ entering the definition of the semi-contact annulus can be chosen arbitrarily $C^1$-small. Hence, by requiring it to satisfy the conditions $|\psi_1|< \frac\varepsilon2$ and $||\psi_1||_{C^1}<\tan\frac\pi{16}$ we can conclude that $\widetilde\Gamma :=h_\varepsilon(\{u= \psi_1(x),\,x\in\Sigma\})$ is graphical, $\widetilde\Gamma =\{u= \widetilde\psi_1 (x)\}$ for a function $\widetilde\psi_1:\Sigma\to{\mathbb{R}}$ which satisfies the following conditions \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde\psi_1|_{\widehat V}\geq\frac\varepsilon2$; \item for every $x\in \widehat W=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widehat V$ and $s\in[0,1]$ we have $${\mathrm{angle}}(T_{z}\widetilde\Sigma_s,\mu_z)>\frac\pi{16},\;\;z=(x,s\widetilde\psi_1(x))\in\widetilde\Gamma_s= \{u= s\widetilde\psi_1 (x)\}.$$
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Properties of the pushed second graph

nodes.name: Positivity on $\widehat V$
nodes.statement: $\widetilde\psi_1|_{\widehat V}\geq\frac\varepsilon2$;
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Positivity on $\widehat V$

nodes.name: Transversality off $\widehat V$
nodes.statement: for every $x\in \widehat W=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} \widehat V$ and $s\in[0,1]$ we have $${\mathrm{angle}}(T_{z}\widetilde\Sigma_s,\mu_z)>\frac\pi{16},\;\;z=(x,s\widetilde\psi_1(x))\in\widetilde\Gamma_s= \{u= s\widetilde\psi_1 (x)\}.$$
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Transversality off $\widehat V$

nodes.name: Define $V$
nodes.statement: Let us denote $ V:=\{\widetilde\psi_1 \geq\frac\varepsilon4\}$, so that $\widehat V\subset{\rm Int\,} V$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Define $V$

nodes.name: The induced semi-contact structure is equivalent to $\{\xi_s\}$
nodes.statement: Note that the family of contact structures $\widetilde\zeta_s$ on $\Sigma\times s\subset\Sigma\times[0,1]$ induced by $\mu$ on the neighborhoods of graphs $\Gamma_s$ of functions $ s\widetilde\psi$ defines a semi-contact structure $\{\zeta_s\}$ which is equivalent to $\{\xi_s\}$. This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{lm:Reeb-trick}.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: The induced semi-contact structure is equivalent to $\{\xi_s\}$

nodes.name: Normal form from Lemma 7.4
nodes.statement: According to Lemma \ref{lm:Reeb-trick} we may assume that the semi-contact structure $\{\zeta_s\}$ on $\Sigma\times[0,1]$ is of immersion type with the following properties. There exist a contact structure $\mu$ on $\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ and a function $\psi:\Sigma\to [-\frac R2,\frac R2]$ such that \begin{description} \item{(i)} the germ of contact structure $\zeta_s$ is induced from $\mu$ on a neighborhood of the $\Sigma\times s$ by an embedding $(x,s)\mapsto (x, s\psi(x)+t)\in\Sigma\times[-R,R] , x\in\Sigma, t\in[-\delta,\delta]$; \item {(ii)} there are closed domains $V\subset\Sigma$ and $\widehat V\subset {\rm Int\,} V$ such that $\psi|_V >0$, and the contact structure $\mu$ is transverse to graphs of functions $s\psi $ over $\widehat W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,}\widehat V$ for all $s\in[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Normal form from Lemma 7.4

nodes.name: Germs induced from $\mu$ along graphs of $s\psi$
nodes.statement: {(i)} the germ of contact structure $\zeta_s$ is induced from $\mu$ on a neighborhood of the $\Sigma\times s$ by an embedding $(x,s)\mapsto (x, s\psi(x)+t)\in\Sigma\times[-R,R] , x\in\Sigma, t\in[-\delta,\delta]$;
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Germs induced from $\mu$ along graphs of $s\psi$

nodes.name: $\psi>0$ on $V$; transversality off $\widehat V$
nodes.statement: {(ii)} there are closed domains $V\subset\Sigma$ and $\widehat V\subset {\rm Int\,} V$ such that $\psi|_V >0$, and the contact structure $\mu$ is transverse to graphs of functions $s\psi $ over $\widehat W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,}\widehat V$ for all $s\in[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: $\psi>0$ on $V$; transversality off $\widehat V$

nodes.name: Split $\psi=\psi_+-\psi_-$
nodes.statement: We will keep the notation $\psi$ for the restriction of $\psi$ to $\widehat W$. Note that $\psi$ can be presented as the difference $\psi=\psi_+-\psi_-$ of two positive functions $\psi_\pm \in C^\infty(\widehat W)$such that the graphs of the functions $s\psi_\pm$ are transverse to $\mu$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Split $\psi=\psi_+-\psi_-$

nodes.name: Covering by balls and two partitions of unity
nodes.statement: Let $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^N$ be a finite covering of $W:=\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} V$ by interiors of balls with smooth boundaries and such that $\bigcup\limits_1^N\overline{U_i}\subset \widehat W$. Let $\{\lambda^\pm_i: \Sigma \to [0,1]\}$ be two partitions of unity on $W$ subordinate to the covering $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^N$, $ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda^\pm_i|_{W}=1$, such that $\mathrm{Support}(\lambda^i_-)\Subset\mathrm{Support}(\lambda^i_+),\, i=1,\dots, N,$ and $ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda^\pm_i|_{\widehat W}\leq 1$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Covering by balls and two partitions of unity

nodes.name: Partial sums $L_k$
nodes.statement: For $0 \leq k \leq N$ define $$L_k:=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda^+_i $$ noting $L_N|_{W}=1$ and $L_N|_{\widehat V}=0$ shows $\widehat V \subset U \subset \Sigma \setminus W$, where $U:= \{L_N < 1\}$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Partial sums $L_k$

nodes.name: Functions $\psi^\pm_i$, $\Psi_k$, graphs and the map $p$
nodes.statement: For $1 \leq i \leq N$ define the functions $$\psi^\pm_i:=\psi^\pm\lambda^\pm_i: \Sigma \to {\mathbb{R}} \quad\mbox{and}\quad \psi_i:=\psi^+_i-\psi^-_i: \Sigma \to {\mathbb{R}}$$ and for $0 \leq k \leq N$ the functions $$ \Psi_k^\pm:=\sum\limits_1^k\psi^\pm_i \quad\mbox{and}\quad \Psi_k:= \Psi_k^+-\Psi_k^-= \sum\limits_1^k\psi_i\,. $$ One can further ensure that the graphs of the functions $\Psi^\pm$ are transverse to $\mu$. Let $\Gamma(\Psi_k):=\{u=\Psi_k(x),\;x\in\Sigma\}\subset\widehat C=\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ be the graph of $\Psi_k$ and likewise $\Gamma(L_k):=\{u=L_k(x),\; x\in\Sigma\}\subset C= \Sigma\times[-1,1]$ be the graph of $L_k$. Set $\Gamma_L:= \bigcup_{k=0}^N \Gamma(L_k)$ and consider the map $p: \Gamma_L \to \Sigma\times[-R,R]$ $$ p(x,u)=(x,\psi^+(x)u -\Psi^-_k(x))\; \hbox{ for}\;(x,u)\in \Gamma(L_k). $$
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Functions $\psi^\pm_i$, $\Psi_k$, graphs and the map $p$

nodes.name: The map $p$ is well defined
nodes.statement: This map is well defined because if $(x,u)\in \Gamma(L_i)\cap \Gamma(L_j)$ for $0\leq i<j\leq N$ then $\Psi^-_i(x)=\Psi^-_j(x).$ Indeed, $L_i(x)=L_j(x)$ implies that $\psi^+_l(x)=0$ for all $i<l\leq j$, and hence $\psi^-_l(x)=0$ for $i<l\leq j$ because $\mathrm{Support}(\psi^-_l)\subset\mathrm{Support}(\psi^+_l)$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: The map $p$ is well defined

nodes.name: $p$ extends to an immersion $P$
nodes.statement: Note that $p({ \Gamma_L})=\bigcup\limits_0^N \Gamma(\Psi_i)$. The map $p$ extends to an immersion $P:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\to \Sigma\times[-R,R]$. See Figure \ref{fig: stack}. \begin{figure}\begin{center} \includegraphics[scale=.5]{stack.pdf} \caption{The set $\Gamma_L$ used in the proof of the lemma. The region below a bump function is a saucer, so a partition of unity decomposes a general region into small saucers. Each saucer comes equipped with a map to $\widehat C$ making it a contact shell.} \end{center}\end{figure}
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: $p$ extends to an immersion $P$

nodes.name: The complement consists of $\Omega$ and saucers $B_i$
nodes.statement: The complement $C\setminus \Gamma_L$ is a union of the domain $\Omega:=\{(x,u);\;\Phi_N(x)\leq u\leq 1, x\in U\}$ and the interiors of saucers $B_i$ bounded by the graphs $\Gamma(L_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma(L_i)$ over the balls $\overline{U_i}$, $i=1,\dots N$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: The complement consists of $\Omega$ and saucers $B_i$

nodes.name: Extend $P$ over $\Omega$
nodes.statement: We extend the immersion $P$ to $\Omega$ as a diffeomorphism $\Omega\to\{(x,u); \Psi_N(x)\leq u\leq \psi_1(x),\;x\in U\}$ which is fiberwise linear with respect to the projection to $\Sigma$,
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Extend $P$ over $\Omega$

nodes.name: Remains to fill the saucers; Lemma 7.5
nodes.statement: It remains to extend the induced contact structure $P^*\mu$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\cup \Omega$ as a regular semi-contact structure on the saucers. The following lemma is obvious. \begin{lemma} Let $\Sigma$ be a hypersurface in a $(2n+1)$-dimensional contact manifold transversal to the contact structure, and $f:D^{2n}\to \Sigma$ a smooth embedding of the unit $2n$-ball. Then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the disc $f(D_\varepsilon^{2n}) $ is regular. \end{lemma}
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Remains to fill the saucers; Lemma 7.5

nodes.name: Lemma 7.5 and $C^1$-smallness make the boundary discs regular
nodes.statement: It follows that the covering by balls $U_i^+$ can be chosen to ensure that the discs $(\overline{U}^+_i, \zeta_0)$ are regular. If the function $ \psi$ is sufficiently $C^1$-small then for each $i=1,\dots, N$ the graphs $\Gamma^-_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma^+_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_i)$ of the functions $\Psi_{i-1}|_{\overline U_i^+}$ and $\Psi_{i}|_{\overline U_i^+}$ respectively, are regular as well.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.5 and $C^1$-smallness make the boundary discs regular

nodes.name: Normalize near $\Pi$: saucers $B_i$ are regular
nodes.statement: Hence there is a contactomorphism $g_i$ between a neighborhood $O_i\supset\Gamma_i^-$ and a neighborhood of a disc in $\Pi=\{y_n=0\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{n+1}$. Again, if $ \psi$ is sufficiently small then the neighborhood $O_i$ contains the disc $\Gamma_i^+$ and, moreover, $g_i(\Gamma^+_i)$ is transverse to the vector field $\frac\partial{\partial y_n}$, which ensures the regularity of the contact saucer $B_i$, $i=1,\dots, N$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: Normalize near $\Pi$: saucers $B_i$ are regular

nodes.name: $C^1$-smallness by partitioning
nodes.statement: Finally, it remains to observe that the required $C^1$-smallness of the function $ \psi$ can be achieved by passing to a partition. This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{lm:annuli-to-saucers}.
nodes.section: 7.1 Construction of contact structures in the complement of saucers
nodes.statement_short: $C^1$-smallness by partitioning

nodes.name: Immersion type by Lemma 7.8
