nodes.statement: Using Lemma \ref{lm:partition-to-special-param}, we can assume that the fibered semi-contact structure ${}^T\xi$ on the annulus ${}^TC=T\times C$ is of immersion type, i.e.\ there exists a fibered contact structure ${}^T \mu=\{\mu^\tau_{\tau\in T}\}$ on ${}^T\widehat C:=T\times\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ and a family of functions $\psi^\tau_s:\Sigma\to[- r,r]$, $r<R$, $s\in[0,1], \tau\in T$, such that the contact structure $\zeta^\tau_s$ on a neighborhood of $\Sigma^\tau _s$ is induced from $\mu^\tau$ by an embedding of this neighborhood onto a neighborhood of the graph of the function $\psi^\tau_s$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Immersion type by Lemma 7.8

nodes.name: Shrink the parameter space and reduce to the normal form of Lemma 7.4
nodes.statement: Let $T'\subset{\rm Int\,} T'', T''\subset {\rm Int\,} T$ be two slightly smaller compact parameter spaces such that the semi-contact structure $\mu^\tau$ is contact for $\tau\in T\setminus{\rm Int\,} T'$, i.e.\ $\psi^\tau_s(x)>\psi^\tau_{s'}(x)$ for any $x\in\Sigma, \tau\in T\setminus{\rm Int\,} T'$ and $s>s'$. Similarly to the non-parametric case (see Lemma \ref{lm:Reeb-trick}) we can reduce to the case when the following property holds: $\psi^\tau_0=0,\psi^\tau_s=s\psi^\tau$ and there exist domains $\widehat W, W \subset T\times\Sigma$, ${\rm Int\,} \widehat W\Supset W$ such that $\psi^\tau(x)>0$ for $(x,\tau)\in T'\times\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} W$, and the contact structures $\mu^\tau$ transverse to the graphs $\Gamma^\tau_s $ of the functions $s\psi^\tau$ over $V^\tau:=(\Sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,} W)\cap{\tau\times\Sigma}$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Shrink the parameter space and reduce to the normal form of Lemma 7.4

nodes.name: Split $\psi$ and choose product coverings
nodes.statement: Denote by $\psi$ the function $\psi(\tau,x,s):=\psi^\tau(x,s)$ for $(\tau,x,s)\in W$, and present $\psi$ as the difference of two positive functions, $\psi=\psi^+-\psi^-$. Let us choose a finite covering of $ W$ denoted $\{U_i\}$, such that $U_i={\rm Int\,} T_i\times {\rm Int\,}\Delta^\pm_i $, where $\Delta_i\subset\Sigma,\; T_i\subset T''$, are balls with smooth boundaries, $ i=1,\dots, N$, and $\bigcup\limits_1^N \overline{U_i}\subset \widehat W$. Here we choose the discs $T_i\subset T$ in such a way that any non-empty intersection $T_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap T_{i_k}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_k\leq L$, is again a disc with piecewise smooth boundary. More geometric constraints on the coverings will be imposed below.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Split $\psi$ and choose product coverings

nodes.name: Partitions of unity and partial sums
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda^\pm_i$ be two partitions of unity over $\widehat W$ subordinated to $U_i$ so that $\mathrm{Support}(\lambda_i^-)\Subset\mathrm{Support}(\lambda_i^+)$, $$\sum\lambda^\pm_i|_{ W}=1,\;\hbox{ and} \; \sum\lambda^\pm_i|_{\widehat W}\leq 1.$$ Let us denote $$\psi^\pm_i:=\psi^\pm\lambda^\pm_i,\; \psi_i:=\psi^+_i-\psi^-_i,\; i=1,\dots, N.$$ Set $$\Psi_k^\pm:=\sum\limits_1^k\psi^\pm_i,\;\; \Psi_k:= \Psi_k^+-\Psi_k^-=\sum\limits_1^k\psi_i,\;\Phi_k:=\sum\limits_1^k\lambda^+_i.$$ Note that $L_N|_{ W}=1$ and $L_N|_{\widehat V}=0$, so $V \subset U:= \{L_N(x) < 1\} \subset T\times\Sigma \setminus W$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Partitions of unity and partial sums

nodes.name: Graphs and the map $p$
nodes.statement: In ${}^TC=T\times\Sigma\times[0,1]$ we let $\Gamma(L_k)$ be the graph of the function $L_k$, and in ${}^T\widehat C = T\times\Sigma\times[-R,R]$ we let $\Gamma(\Psi_k)$ be the graph of the function $\Psi_k$. Set $\Gamma_L=\bigcup\limits_0^N \Gamma(L_i)\subset {}^TC$. Consider the map $p:{ \Gamma_L}\to T\times \Sigma\times[-R,R]$ given by the formula $$p(\tau,x,s)=(\tau,x, \psi^+(\tau,x)s -\Psi^-_i(\tau,x))\; \hbox{ for}\;(\tau,x,s)\in \Gamma(L_i).$$
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Graphs and the map $p$

nodes.name: $p$ is well defined
nodes.statement: This map is well defined because if $(\tau, x,s)\in \Gamma(L_i)\cap \Gamma(L_j)$ for $0\leq i<j\leq N$ then $\Psi^-_i(\tau,x)=\Psi^-_j(\tau,x).$ Indeed, $\Phi_i(\tau, x)=\Phi_j(\tau,x)$ implies that $\psi^+_l(\tau,x)=0$ for all $i<l\leq j$, and hence $\psi^-_l(\tau,x)=0$ for $i<l\leq j$ because $\mathrm{Support}(\psi^-_l)\subset\mathrm{Support}(\psi^+_l)$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: $p$ is well defined

nodes.name: $p$ extends to an immersion $P$
nodes.statement: Note that $p({ \Gamma_L})=\bigcup\limits_0^N \Gamma(\Psi_i)$. The map $p$ extends to an immersion $P:{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\to T\times \Sigma\times[-R,R]$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: $p$ extends to an immersion $P$

nodes.name: The complement consists of $\Omega$ and fibered saucers
nodes.statement: The complement ${}^TC\setminus \Gamma_L$ is a union of the domain $\Omega:=\{(x,s);\;\Phi_N(\tau,x)\leq s\leq 1, \tau\in T, x\in U\}$ and interiors of fibered saucers ${}^{T_i}B_i$ bounded by the graphs $\Gamma(L_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma(L_i)$ over the balls $\overline{U_i}$, $i=1,\dots N$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: The complement consists of $\Omega$ and fibered saucers

nodes.name: Extend $P$ over $\Omega$
nodes.statement: We extend the immersion $P$ to $\Omega$ as a fiberwise linear, with respect to the projection to $T\times \Sigma$, diffeomorphism $$\Omega\to\{(\tau, x,u); \Psi_N(\tau,x)\leq u\leq \psi(\tau, x),\;(\tau,x)\in U\}.$$
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Extend $P$ over $\Omega$

nodes.name: Remains to fill the fibered saucers
nodes.statement: It remains to extend the induced contact structure $P^*\left({}^T\mu\right)$ on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,{ \Gamma_L}\cup \Omega$ as a fibered regular semi-contact structure to the saucers.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Remains to fill the fibered saucers

nodes.name: Lemma 7.5 makes the boundary discs regular
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma \ref {lm:foliation} that the covering by balls $U_i$ can be chosen to ensure that for each $i=1,\dots, N$ and $\tau \in T^+_i$ the disc $(\tau\times\Delta^+_i, \zeta^\tau_0)$ is regular. If the functions $ \psi_1$ and $ \psi_0$ are sufficiently $C^1$-close than for each $i=1,\dots, N$ the graphs $\Gamma^-_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_{i-1})$ and $\Gamma^+_i \subset \Gamma(\Psi_i)$ of the functions $\Psi_{i-1}|_{\overline U_i^+}$ and $\Psi_{i}|_{\overline U_i^+}$, respectively, are fibered over $T_i^+$ by regular discs as well.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.5 makes the boundary discs regular

nodes.name: Normalize near $\Pi$: fibered saucers are regular
nodes.statement: Hence, there is a fibered over $T_i^+$ contactomorphism $g_i$ between a neighborhood $O_i\supset\Gamma_i^-$ and a neighborhood of a fibered disc in $T_i\times \Pi=\{y_n=0\}\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{n+1}$. Again, if $ \psi$ is sufficiently close then the neighborhood $O_i$ contains the disc $\Gamma_i^+$ and, moreover, $g_i(\Gamma^+_i)$ is transverse to the vector field $\frac\partial{\partial y_n}$, which ensures the regularity of the fibered contact saucer ${}^{T_i}B_i$, $i=1,\dots, N$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Normalize near $\Pi$: fibered saucers are regular

nodes.name: Smallness by partitioning
nodes.statement: Finally, it remains to observe that the required smallness of the function $ \psi$ can be achieved by passing to a partition.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Smallness by partitioning

nodes.name: Case $T=D^q$: parametric h-principle off an annulus
nodes.statement: First assume $T = D^q$. Choose an embedded annulus $C=S^{2n}\times[0,1]\subset M\setminus A$ and first use the $q$-parametric part of Gromov's $h$-principle \ref{thm:Gromov-open} to deform ${}^T\xi_0$ rel.\ $(T\times A)\cup(\partial T\times M)$ to a fibered almost contact structure which is genuine fibered contact structure on $T\times M\setminus C$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Case $T=D^q$: parametric h-principle off an annulus

nodes.name: Make the structure semi-contact on $T\times C$
nodes.statement: Next, with use of the $(q+1)$-parametric part of Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open} applied to the family of neighborhoods of spheres $\tau\times S^{2n}\times t, \tau\in T, t\in[0,1]$ we make the fibered almost contact structure semi-contact on ${}^TC=T\times C$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Make the structure semi-contact on $T\times C$

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7.7
nodes.statement: Finally we use Lemma \ref{lm:annuli-to-saucers-param} to complete the proof.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 7.7

nodes.name: General $T$: induct over skeleta
nodes.statement: For general $T$ we triangulate it and inductively over skeleta apply the previous proof to each simplex.
nodes.section: 7.2 Contact structures in the complement of saucers. Parametric version
nodes.statement_short: General $T$: induct over skeleta

nodes.name: Fix $\varepsilon$ and a separating set $P$
nodes.statement: Suppose $K\colon U \to {\mathbb{R}}$ is given. Since $K$ is positive on $U \setminus U'$, we may fix some $\varepsilon > 0$ with the property that the set $P := \{(x,y,z) \in U \setminus U': K(x,y,z) > \varepsilon\}$ disconnects $U'$ from $\partial U$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\varepsilon$ and a separating set $P$

nodes.name: WLOG enlarge $U'$
nodes.statement: Notice that the conclusion of the lemma only becomes stronger if we enlarge the set $U' \Subset U$. With this in mind we redefine $U'$ to be the interior of the union of all components of $U \setminus P$ which are disjoint from $\partial U$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG enlarge $U'$

nodes.name: Choose $N$ large and a finite set $\Lambda$ of translates
nodes.statement: Set $\widehat Q_N:= \pi(Q_N),\;\widehat Q'_N:= \pi(Q'_N)$. For a sufficiently large $N$ there exists a finite set $ \Lambda\subset\widehat\Theta$ such that $(U' \cup P) \times S^1\Supset \bigcup \limits_{g\in \Lambda}g(\widehat Q_N) \supset \bigcup \limits_{g\in \Lambda}g(\widehat Q^\prime_N) \Supset U' \times S^1$. Furthermore, suppose that \begin{equation} N> (m+1)\mu\varepsilon^{-1} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Choose $N$ large and a finite set $\Lambda$ of translates

nodes.name: Bound the sum on $P\times S^1$
nodes.statement: Then, using \eqref{eq:largeN} we get on $P \times S^1$ $$ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{g,N} < \frac{m \mu}N = \frac{(m+1) \mu}N -\frac\mu N < \varepsilon-\frac\mu N <K-\frac\mu N.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the sum on $P\times S^1$

nodes.name: Bound the sum on $U'\times S^1$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, on $U'\times S^1$ we have $$ \sum\limits_{g\in\Lambda}\phi_{g,N} <-\frac{(m+1)\mu}N + \frac{(m-1)\mu}N < - \frac{2\mu} N. $$ Indeed this holds, for given $(x,y,z) \in g(Q'_N)$ because according to inequality (ii) a single negative term $\widehat{\phi_{g,N}}(x,y,z)$ is larger in absolute value by at least $\frac{2\mu}N$ than the sum of all positive terms (the denominator $N$ appears because of the scaling factor of the function in the definition of $\phi_{g,N}$).
nodes.statement_short: Bound the sum on $U'\times S^1$

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 8.6
nodes.statement: Let $U={\rm Int\,} \Delta$ and $U'\Subset U$ be a star-shaped subset such that $K|_{U\setminus U'}>0$. Apply Lemma \ref{lm:positive-decomposition}, providing an integer $N>0$, and a finite set $\Lambda\subset\widehat\Theta_N$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 8.6

nodes.name: Bounds on the sum $\Phi$
nodes.statement: Then the corresponding function $$\Phi=\Phi^{S^1,N}=\frac\mu N+\sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{g,N} :\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}}$$ satisfies $\Phi (w,t)< K(v)$ for $w\in \Delta\setminus U'$ and $\Phi|_{U'\times S^1}<-\frac\mu N$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on the sum $\Phi$

nodes.name: Proposition 4.9 gives $\widetilde K\geq\Phi$ dominated by $K$
nodes.statement: According to Proposition \ref{prop:shallow} there exists a contact Hamiltonian $\widetilde K$ so that $\eta_{\widetilde K}$ is dominated by $\eta_K$, where $\widetilde K|_{\Delta\setminus U'}=K|_{\Delta\setminus U'}$ and $\widetilde K|_{U'}>-\frac\mu N$. Therefore $\Phi(w,t)<\widetilde K(w)$ for all $(w,t) \in \Delta \times S^1$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 4.9 gives $\widetilde K\geq\Phi$ dominated by $K$

nodes.name: Reduce to the shell $\eta_\Phi$
nodes.statement: The function $\Phi$ is equal $\frac\mu N>0$ near $\partial \Delta\times S^1$ and hence defines a circular shell model $\eta_{\Phi}$ which is dominated by $\eta_{\widetilde K}$. Hence it sufficient to prove the required extension result for $\eta_{\Phi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the shell $\eta_\Phi$

nodes.name: Partial sums $\Phi_k$
nodes.statement: We order $\Lambda$ using the chosen ordering of $\widehat\Theta$ and define functions $$\Phi_k= \frac\mu N+\sum\limits_{j=1}^k \phi_{g_j,N}:\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}},\; k=0,\dots,|\Lambda|,$$ where $|\Lambda|$ is the cardinality of $\Lambda$. We have $\Phi_0=\frac\mu N$ and $\Phi_{|\Lambda|}=\Phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Partial sums $\Phi_k$

nodes.name: Consecutive shells differ by a saucer from Lemma 8.5
nodes.statement: The shells $\eta_{\Phi_k}$ and $\eta_{\Phi_{k-1}}$ differ by one of the regular saucers $(B_p,\zeta_p)$, from the finite list provided by Lemma \ref{lm:finite-contact}, while the shell $\eta_{\Phi_0}$ is solid, since $\Phi_0>0$ everywhere.
nodes.statement_short: Consecutive shells differ by a saucer from Lemma 8.5

nodes.name: Reduce to regular saucers (Proposition 6.2)
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:to saucers} allows us to assume that $\xi$ is contact outside of a finite collection of disjoint saucers $\{B_i\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$, so that the restriction $\xi|_{B_i}$ for each $i=1,\dots, N$, is a regular semi-contact saucer.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to regular saucers (Proposition 6.2)

nodes.name: Replace saucers by circle models (Proposition 6.12)
nodes.statement: Using Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle} we replace saucers by circular model shells defined by time-independent contact Hamiltonians.
nodes.statement_short: Replace saucers by circle models (Proposition 6.12)

nodes.name: Reduce to finitely many saucers (Proposition 8.1)
nodes.statement: Applying Proposition \ref{prop:circular-to-universal-saucers} we can further reduce to the case of a contact structure in the complement of saucers from the finite list $(B_p,\zeta_p)$, $p=1,\dots, L$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finitely many saucers (Proposition 8.1)

nodes.name: Replace them by circle models $K_p$
nodes.statement: Using again Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle} we replace saucers by circular model shells $\left(B_{K_p},\eta_{K_p}\right)$ defined by time-independent contact Hamiltonians.
nodes.statement_short: Replace them by circle models $K_p$

nodes.name: Choose $K_{\mathrm{univ}}<\min_p K_p$
nodes.statement: We may then choose any special Hamiltonian $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ satisfying $K_{\mathrm{univ}}(x) < {\rm min}_p K_p(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $K_{\mathrm{univ}}<\min_p K_p$

nodes.name: Saucers are solid for small $s$
nodes.statement: We note that there exists $\delta>0$ such that the regular saucer $(B_p,\zeta^{s}_p)$ is solid for $s\in[0,\delta]$, i.e.\ the contact structure on its boundary is extended inside as a genuine contact structure.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Saucers are solid for small $s$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.13: circle models below the saucer families
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle-param} implies that the family of saucers $(B_p,\zeta^{s}_p)$ dominates a family of circular models $\eta_{\widetilde K^{s}_p}$, where $\widetilde K^{s}_p>0$ for $s\in[0,\delta']$, $p=1,\dots, 2^m$, for some $\delta'<\delta$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 6.13: circle models below the saucer families

nodes.name: Lemma 4.6: take the domain $\Delta_{\rm cyl}$
nodes.statement: We also note that Lemma \ref{lm:changing-B} allows us to assume that the domain $\Delta$ in the definition of the Hamiltonians $\widetilde K_p^{s}$ coincides with $\Delta_{\rm cyl}$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.6: take the domain $\Delta_{\rm cyl}$

nodes.name: Choose $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ and $\theta$
nodes.statement: Choose as $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ any special contact Hamiltonian which satisfies $$K_{\mathrm{univ}}<\mathop{{\rm min}}\limits_{s\in[0,1],p=1,\dots, L=2^m}\widetilde K^s_p.$$ (See Example \ref{ex:special}.) There exists $\delta''\in(0,\delta')$ such that $\widetilde K^s_p>K^{(0)}_{\mathrm{univ}}$ for all $s\in[0,1],\; p=1,\dots, 2^m$. Choose a non-decreasing function $\theta:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such that $\theta(s)=0$ for $s\in[0,\tfrac{\delta'}2]$ and $\theta(s)=1$ for $s\in[\delta'',1]$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Choose $K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ and $\theta$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 gives the subordination maps
nodes.statement: Then $K_{\mathrm{univ}}^{(\theta(s))}<\widetilde K^s_p$ for all $s\in[0,1], p=1,\dots, 2^n$. Hence, by Lemma \ref{l:HamiltonianShellsAnnulus} one can arrange the inclusion maps $\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}^{(\theta(s))}}\to \eta^s_p$ be subordinations.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.1 gives the subordination maps

nodes.name: Reduce to a family $\overline K^{||\tau||}$
nodes.statement: First, we can choose $\overline K^s: \Delta \to {\mathbb{R}}$, $s \in [0,1]$, so that $\overline K^{||\tau||} \leq K^{ \tau }$ everywhere, $\overline K^1 > 0$ and $\overline K^s|_{\partial \Delta} >0$ for all $s\in[0,1]$. It, therefore, suffices to prove the proposition for the family $\overline K^{||\tau||}$. We can also assume that $\overline K^0(x) \leq \overline K^s(x)$ for any $x \in \Delta$, $s \in [0,1]$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a family $\overline K^{||\tau||}$

nodes.name: Choose $U'$ and $\delta$
nodes.statement: Let $U={\rm Int\,} \Delta$ and $U'\Subset U$ be a star-shaped subset such that $\overline K^{||\tau||}|_{U\setminus U'}>0$ for all $\tau\in T$. We also choose $\delta>0$ so that $\overline K^s > 0$ for all $s \in [1-\delta, 1]$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Choose $U'$ and $\delta$

nodes.name: Lemma 8.6 gives $\Phi$ and $\Psi$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{lm:positive-decomposition} to $\overline K^0$, providing an integer $N>0$, and a finite set $\Lambda=\{g_1,\dots, g_k\}\subset\widehat \Theta_N$, so that the function $$\Phi=\Phi^{S^1,N}=\frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{g,N} :\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}}$$ satisfies $\Phi (w,t)< \overline K^s(w)$ for $w\in \Delta\setminus U'$ and $\Phi|_{U'\times S^1}<-\frac\mu N$. Choosing $N$ large enough we can also arrange that $\mathop{{\rm min}}\limits_{||\tau||\geq1-\delta} \overline K^\tau> \Psi =\Psi^{S^1,N}=\frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\phi_{+,g,N}=\frac\mu N+ \frac1N\sum\limits_{g\in \Lambda}\left(\phi_{+}\circ C_N\circ g^{-1}\right)$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 8.6 gives $\Phi$ and $\Psi$

nodes.name: Proposition 4.10 gives $\widetilde K^s$
nodes.statement: According to Proposition \ref{prop:shallow-param} there exists a family of functions $\widetilde K^s $, $s\in[0,1]$, such that \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde K^s=\overline K^s$ on $\Delta \setminus U'$, $\widetilde{K}^s > -\frac\mu N$, $s\in[0,1]$; \item $\widetilde K^s= \overline K^s$ for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$; \item there exists a family of subordination maps $h^s: \eta_{\overline K^s}\to \eta_{\widetilde{K^s}}$ which are identity maps for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$. \end{itemize} In particular, $\Phi(w,t)<\widetilde K^s(w)$ for all $w\in \Delta, t\in S^1, s\in[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 4.10 gives $\widetilde K^s$

nodes.name: Unchanged off $U'$, bounded below
nodes.statement: $\widetilde K^s=\overline K^s$ on $\Delta \setminus U'$, $\widetilde{K}^s > -\frac\mu N$, $s\in[0,1]$;
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Unchanged off $U'$, bounded below

nodes.name: Unchanged for $s$ near 1
nodes.statement: $\widetilde K^s= \overline K^s$ for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$;
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Unchanged for $s$ near 1

nodes.name: Subordination maps
nodes.statement: there exists a family of subordination maps $h^s: \eta_{\overline K^s}\to \eta_{\widetilde{K^s}}$ which are identity maps for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$. \end{itemize} In particular, $\Phi(w,t)<\widetilde K^s(w)$ for all $w\in \Delta, t\in S^1, s\in[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Subordination maps

nodes.name: Reparametrize by $\widetilde\theta=\theta\circ f$
nodes.statement: Recall the notation $\phi^s= \phi_+-s\phi_-,\; \phi^s_{g_j,N}=\frac1N\phi^s\circ C_N\circ g_i^{-1} $ from Section \ref{sec:equi-cov}. Choose a diffeomorphism $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such $f(1-\frac\delta2)=\frac23, f(1-\delta)=\frac13$. Then the function $\widetilde\theta:=\theta\circ f$ satisfies $\widetilde\theta|_{[0,1-\delta]} = 1$ and $\widetilde\theta|_{[1-\frac\delta2,1]} = 0$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Reparametrize by $\widetilde\theta=\theta\circ f$

nodes.name: Interpolated partial sums $\Phi^s_i$
nodes.statement: We define the families of functions $\Phi^s_i:= \frac\mu N+ \sum\limits_{j=1}^i \left( \phi^{\widetilde{\theta}(s)}_{g_j,N}\right):\Delta\times S^1\to{\mathbb{R}}$, so we have $\Phi^s_0=\frac1N$, $\Phi^s_{|\Lambda|}=\Phi$ for $s\leq 1-\delta$, and $\Phi^1_{|\Lambda|}=\Psi$. Here ${|\Lambda|}$ is the cardinality of $\Lambda$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Interpolated partial sums $\Phi^s_i$

nodes.name: $\Phi^s<\widetilde K^s$, reducing to $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}}$
nodes.statement: The function $\Phi^s:=\Phi^s_k$ for each $s\in[0,1]$ is equal $\frac1N>0$ near $ \partial \Delta\times S^1$, and it satisfies the inequality $\Phi^s<\widetilde K^s$. Indeed, for $s\in[0,1-\delta]$ we have $\Phi^s=\Phi<\widetilde K^s$, and for $s\in[1-\delta,1]$ we have $\Phi^s<\Psi<\overline K^u=\widetilde K^s$. Therefore, the family of circular shell models $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}}$ is dominated by $\eta_{\widetilde K^{||\tau||}}$, and hence it is sufficient to prove the required extension result for the family $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}}$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi^s<\widetilde K^s$, reducing to $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}}$

nodes.name: Consecutive shells differ by saucer families from Lemma 8.5
nodes.statement: The family of model shells $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}_i}$ and $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}_{i-1}}, \tau\in T$, differ by one of the regular saucer families $(B_p,\zeta^{\widetilde\theta(||\tau||)}_p)$, $p=1,\dots, L=2^m$, from the finite list provided by Lemma \ref{lm:finite-contact}. The shell $\eta_{\Phi^{||\tau||}_0}$ is solid for all $\tau\in T$, since $\Phi^{||\tau||}_0>0$ everywhere. Similarly the saucers $(B_p,\zeta^{||\tau||}_p)$ for $\tau\in{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T$ are solid for $\tau\in{\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial T$, because we have $\Phi^{||\tau||}_j\geq\Phi^{||\tau||}_{j-1}$ for all $j=1,\dots, |\Lambda|$. But the fibered saucer corresponding to the family $(B_p,\zeta^{\widetilde\theta(||\tau||)}_p)$ is equivalent to ${}^T\eta_p$, $p=1,\dots, L$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Consecutive shells differ by saucer families from Lemma 8.5

nodes.name: Reduce to fibered regular saucers (Proposition 7.6)
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:to-saucers-param} allows us to assume that ${}^T\xi_0$ is fibered contact outside of a finite collection of disjoint $\{B_i\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$, so that the restriction for each $i=1,\dots, N$, $\xi_0|_{B_i}$ is a fibered regular semi-contact saucer.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to fibered regular saucers (Proposition 7.6)

nodes.name: Reduce to finitely many fibered saucers (Proposition 8.9)
nodes.statement: Applying Proposition \ref{prop:circular-to-universal-param} we further reduce the holes to a finite list of fibered saucers ${}^T\eta_p, p=1,\dots, L=2^m$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finitely many fibered saucers (Proposition 8.9)

nodes.name: Replace them by fibered circle models (Proposition 6.13)
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{prop:saucer-to-circle-param} allows us to replace each saucer ${}^T\eta_p$, $p=1,\dots, L,$ by a fibered circular model shell ${}^T\eta_{K_p}$ defined by a family of time-independent contact Hamiltonian $K_p^\tau, \tau\in T$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Replace them by fibered circle models (Proposition 6.13)

nodes.name: Lemma 8.7: each dominates the universal model
nodes.statement: But then, using Lemma \ref{lm:universal-eps} we conclude that each circular model shell ${}^T\eta_{K_p}$ dominates the fibered circular model ${}^T\eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}:=\{\eta_{K^{ (\theta(||\tau||)}_{\mathrm{univ}}})\}_{\tau\in T}$.
nodes.section: 8.2 The standardization of the holes in the parametric case
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 8.7: each dominates the universal model

nodes.name: Induction on $k$
nodes.statement: We will prove the statement by induction in $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$

nodes.name: Base case $k=0$
nodes.statement: When $k=0$ the statement follows from the fact that the space of maps of the contractible set $T$ into the space of pairs of disjoint embeddings of $B$ into $U$ is connected, and hence by a fiberwise isotopy we can assume that the embeddings $s_\pm(\tau,\cdot):B\to U$ are independent of $\tau$, i.e. $s_\pm(\tau,x)=\widetilde s_\pm(x)$ for all $(\tau,x)\in T\times B$. Then to construct the required embedding it is sufficient to connect the points $\widetilde s_\pm(p)$ by an embedded arc in $U$ which does not intersect the ball $\widetilde s_\pm(B)$ in its interior points.
nodes.statement_short: Base case $k=0$

nodes.name: Inductive hypothesis
nodes.statement: Suppose that the statement is already proven for $k=j$ (and any $U$).
nodes.statement_short: Inductive hypothesis

nodes.name: Case $T_k=T$
nodes.statement: Suppose first that one of the $k=j+1$ sets $T_1,\dots, T_k$, say $T_k$, coincides with $T$. By a fiberwise isotopy we can make the embedding $s_k(\tau,\cdot):B\to U$ independent of $\tau$, i.e. $s_k(\tau,x)=\widetilde s_k(x)$ for all $(\tau,x)\in T\times B$. Therefore, the statement reduces to the case of $k-1=j$ sets $T_1,\dots, T_j$ and their embeddings into $\widetilde U=U\setminus\widetilde s_k(B)$, which is connected as well.
nodes.statement_short: Case $T_k=T$

nodes.name: General case: restrict to $T_k$
nodes.statement: Consider now the general case. By an argument as above, we can assume that the embeddings $s_+(\tau, \cdot)$ are independent of $\tau$, i.e. $s_+(\tau,x)=\widehat s_+(x)$ for all $(\tau,x)\in T\times B$. Denote $\widehat U:= U\setminus \widehat s_+(B)$. Suppose that $T_k$ is a proper subset of $T$. Set $\widehat T:= T_k$, $\widehat T_i:= T_i\cap T_k$, $\widehat S_i:= S_i|_{\widetilde T_i\times B}$, $i=1,\dots, k-1$, $\widehat S_-:= S_-|_{T_k\times B}$, $\widehat S_+:= S_k|_{T_k\times B}$. Note that the sets $\widehat T_i$, $i=1,\dots, k-1$, and $\widehat T$ satisfy the condition $(\star)$.
nodes.statement_short: General case: restrict to $T_k$

nodes.name: Apply the inductive hypothesis over $T_k$
nodes.statement: Considering $\widehat S_i$ as embeddings into $\widehat T_i\times\widehat U$, and $\widehat S_\pm$ as embeddings into $\widehat T\times\widehat U$ we can apply the inductional hypothesis to construct a fiberwise embedding $\widehat S:\widehat T\times [-1,1]\to \widehat T\times\widehat U$ such that \begin{description} \item{--} $\widehat S(\tau,\pm 1)=S_\pm(\tau,\widehat p)$, $\tau\in \widehat T$, where $\widehat p\in \partial B$, is a point different from $p$; \item{--} $\widehat S (\widehat T\times[-1,1])\cap\bigcup\limits_1^{k-1}\widehat S_j(\widehat T_j\times B)=\varnothing$; \item{--} $\widehat S (\widehat T\times(-1,1))\cap\left(\widehat S_-(\widehat T\times B)\cup \widehat S_+(\widehat T\times B)\right)=\varnothing$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inductive hypothesis over $T_k$

nodes.name: Endpoint condition
nodes.statement: {--} $\widehat S(\tau,\pm 1)=S_\pm(\tau,\widehat p)$, $\tau\in \widehat T$, where $\widehat p\in \partial B$, is a point different from $p$;
nodes.statement_short: Endpoint condition

nodes.name: Avoids the other embeddings
nodes.statement: {--} $\widehat S (\widehat T\times[-1,1])\cap\bigcup\limits_1^{k-1}\widehat S_j(\widehat T_j\times B)=\varnothing$;
nodes.statement_short: Avoids the other embeddings

nodes.name: Interior avoids the end balls
nodes.statement: {--} $\widehat S (\widehat T\times(-1,1))\cap\left(\widehat S_-(\widehat T\times B)\cup \widehat S_+(\widehat T\times B)\right)=\varnothing$.
nodes.statement_short: Interior avoids the end balls

nodes.name: Fiberwise connected sum $\widetilde S_-$
nodes.statement: Using the embedding $\widehat S$ we can make a fiberwise connected sum of the embeddings $\widehat S_\pm$ to construct a fiberwise embedding $\widetilde S_-:T\times B\to T\times \widehat U$ with the following properties: \begin{itemize} \item $\widetilde S_-(T\times B)\cap \bigcup\limits_1^{k-1}S_j(T_j\times B)=\varnothing$; \item $\widetilde S_-(T\times B)\supset S_-(T\times B)\cup S_k(T_k\times B)$; \item the embeddings $\widetilde S_-$ and $S_-$ coincides near $T\times p\in T\times \partial B$.
nodes.statement_short: Fiberwise connected sum $\widetilde S_-$

nodes.name: Disjoint from the other embeddings
nodes.statement: $\widetilde S_-(T\times B)\cap \bigcup\limits_1^{k-1}S_j(T_j\times B)=\varnothing$;
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint from the other embeddings

nodes.name: Contains $S_-$ and $S_k$
nodes.statement: $\widetilde S_-(T\times B)\supset S_-(T\times B)\cup S_k(T_k\times B)$;
nodes.statement_short: Contains $S_-$ and $S_k$

nodes.name: Agrees with $S_-$ near $p$
nodes.statement: the embeddings $\widetilde S_-$ and $S_-$ coincides near $T\times p\in T\times \partial B$.
nodes.statement_short: Agrees with $S_-$ near $p$

nodes.name: Apply the inductive hypothesis again
nodes.statement: Hence, by applying again the inductional hypothesis to the embeddings $\widetilde S_-, S$ and $S_j, j=1,\dots k-1$, we can construct a fiberwise embedding $S:T \times [-1,1]\to T\times U$ with the required properties.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inductive hypothesis again

nodes.name: Reformulate as a relative homotopy problem over a ball $T$
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be an $m$-ball. We need to prove that any map $$ (T,\partial T)\to (\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_N)), \mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_N)) $$ is homotopic rel. $\partial T$ to a map into $\mathfrak{Cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_N)$. In other words, let $\xi_\tau\in\mathfrak{cont}_{\mathrm{ot}}(\mathcal{F}; h_1,\dots, h_n)$, $\tau\in T$, be a family of leafwise almost contact structures which are genuine leafwise contact structures for $\tau\in\partial T$. We will construct a homotopy rel. $\partial T$ to a family of genuine leafwise contact structures $\widetilde\xi_\tau, \tau\in T$.
nodes.statement_short: Reformulate as a relative homotopy problem over a ball $T$

nodes.name: Pass to the foliation $\widehat{\mathcal F}$ on $T\times V$
nodes.statement: Consider a foliation $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}$ on $T\times V$ with leaves $\tau\times L$ where $\tau\in T$ and $L$ a leaf of $\mathcal{F}$. Let $\widehat h_j:T\times T_j\times B\to T\times V$ be the embeddings, given by $$\widehat h_j(\tau, \tau',x)=(\tau,h_j(\tau',x), (\tau,\tau',x)\in T\times T_j\times B, j=1,\dots, N.$$ The family $\xi_\tau,\tau\in T$, can be viewed as a leafwise almost contact structure $\Xi$ from $\mathfrak{cont}(\widehat \mathcal{F};\widehat h_1,\dots,\widehat h_N)$ which is genuine on leaves $\tau\times L$ for $ \tau\in\partial T$. Moreover, we can assume that $\Xi$ is a genuine leafwise contact structure on a neighborhood $U\supset \partial T\times V$ and neighborhoods $U_j\supset \widehat h_j(T\times T_j\times B)$, $j=1,\dots, N$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the foliation $\widehat{\mathcal F}$ on $T\times V$

nodes.name: Choose a triangulation transverse to the foliation
nodes.statement: There exists a triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ of $T\times V$ with the following properties: \begin{itemize} \item there are compact {\em subcomplexes} $\widehat U , \widehat U_j$, $j=1,\dots, N$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ such that $\partial T\times V\subset\widehat U\subset U,\; \widehat h_j(T\times T_j\times B)\subset\widehat U_j\subset U_j$, $j=1,\dots, N$; \item the restriction $\mathcal{T}_0$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ to $T\times V\setminus {\rm Int\,}(\widehat U\cup\bigcup\limits_1^N\widehat U_j)$ is transverse to the foliation $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}$; \item For every top-dimensional simplex $\sigma$ of $\mathcal{T}_0$ there exists a submersion $\pi_\sigma:{\rm Int\,}\sigma\to B^{q+m}$ which is a fibration over an open $(q+m)$-ball with the ball fibers, and such that the pre-images $\pi_\sigma^{-1}(s), s\in B^{q+m},$ are intersections of the leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$ with ${\rm Int\,}\sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a triangulation transverse to the foliation

nodes.name: Subcomplexes near the boundary and overtwisted balls
nodes.statement: there are compact {\em subcomplexes} $\widehat U , \widehat U_j$, $j=1,\dots, N$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ such that $\partial T\times V\subset\widehat U\subset U,\; \widehat h_j(T\times T_j\times B)\subset\widehat U_j\subset U_j$, $j=1,\dots, N$;
nodes.statement_short: Subcomplexes near the boundary and overtwisted balls

nodes.name: Transversality
nodes.statement: the restriction $\mathcal{T}_0$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}$ to $T\times V\setminus {\rm Int\,}(\widehat U\cup\bigcup\limits_1^N\widehat U_j)$ is transverse to the foliation $\widehat{\mathcal{F}}$;
nodes.statement_short: Transversality

nodes.name: Simplices fiber over balls
nodes.statement: For every top-dimensional simplex $\sigma$ of $\mathcal{T}_0$ there exists a submersion $\pi_\sigma:{\rm Int\,}\sigma\to B^{q+m}$ which is a fibration over an open $(q+m)$-ball with the ball fibers, and such that the pre-images $\pi_\sigma^{-1}(s), s\in B^{q+m},$ are intersections of the leaves of $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$ with ${\rm Int\,}\sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplices fiber over balls

nodes.name: Gromov's h-principle near the codimension-1 skeleton
nodes.statement: Applying Gromov's parametric $h$-principle for contact structures on open manifolds (see \cite{Gro69} and Theorem \ref{thm:Gromov-open}) inductively over skeleta of the triangulation we can deform $\Xi$, keeping it fixed on $\widehat U\cup\bigcup\limits_1^N\widehat U_j$ to make it leafwise genuinely contact in a neighborhood of the codimension $1$ skeleton of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Gromov's h-principle near the codimension-1 skeleton

nodes.name: Work on one top simplex as a fibration
nodes.statement: Our next goal is to further deform $\Xi$ on each top-dimensional simplex $\sigma$ of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}_0$, keeping it fixed on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\sigma$, to make in leafwise genuine contact structure on $\sigma$. Let us choose one of such simplices. There exists a compact subset $\overline\sigma\subset{\rm Int\,}\sigma$ such that the leafwise almost contact structure $\Xi$ is genuine on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,(\sigma\setminus{\rm Int\,}\overline\sigma)$ and $\pi_\sigma|_{\overline\sigma}$ is a fibration over a closed $(m+q)$-ball $X $ with fibers diffeomorphic to a closed $(2n+1)$-ball.
nodes.statement_short: Work on one top simplex as a fibration

nodes.name: Proposition 7.6: reduce to fibered saucers $Z_i$
nodes.statement: Hence, $\Xi|_{\overline\sigma}$ can be viewed as a fibered over $X$ almost contact structure on $\overline\sigma$, and applying Proposition \ref{prop:to-saucers-param} we can further deform $\Xi$ keeping it fixed on ${\mathcal O}{\it p}\,\partial\sigma$, to make it genuine away from a finite number of disjoint domains $Z_i$ fibered over $X_i\subset X$ with piecewise smooth boundary, $i=1,\dots, K$. These domains are not necessarily disjoint but could be chosen arbitrary small and in such a way that all non-empty intersections $X_{i_1}\cap\dots\cap X_{i_k}$, $1\leq i_1<\dots<i_k\leq K$, are again balls with piecewise smooth boundaries. Let $Y$, $Y\subset\overline\sigma$, and $Y_i,\; Y_i\subset Z_i,$ be subfibrations of the fibrations $\overline\sigma\to X$ and $Z_i\to X_i , \; i=1,\dots, K$, formed by boundaries of the corresponding ball-fibers.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 7.6: reduce to fibered saucers $Z_i$

nodes.name: Lemma 9.1: paths from the saucers to overtwisted balls
nodes.statement: Next, we use Lemma \ref{lm:choosing-paths} to construct for each $X_j$ a fiberwise embedding $S_j:X_j\times[0,1]\to\overline Z_j\setminus \bigcup\limits_{i\neq j}Z_i$ with $S_j(\tau,0)\in Y_j$ and $S_j(\tau,1)\in Y$. Recall that by assumption every point $(\tau,x)\in Y$ can be connected to a point on the boundary of one of the overtwisted balls $B_{i,\tau,\tau'}:=h_i(\tau\times\times\tau' B_i), \; i=1,\dots, N,\;\tau\in T,$ by an embedded path in the corresponding leaf. This path can be chosen inside an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the codimension $1$ skeleton of the triangulation $\mathcal{T}_0$. Hence, if the sets $X_j$ are chosen sufficiently small we can extend each of the embeddings $S_j$ to a leafwise embedding $\widetilde S_j:X_j\times[0,2]\to V$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $S_j(\tau,0)\in Y_j$; \item $S_j(\tau,2)\in h_i(T_i\times\partial B) $ for some $i=i(\sigma,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.1: paths from the saucers to overtwisted balls

nodes.name: Proposition 3.8: enough disjoint overtwisted balls
nodes.statement: Moreover, using Proposition \ref{prop:neighb-ot} to increase the number of embeddings $h_i$ we can additionally arrange that the map $(\sigma,j)\mapsto i(\sigma,j)$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 3.8: enough disjoint overtwisted balls

nodes.name: Theorem 3.12 fills each neighborhood
nodes.statement: Then, successively applying Theorem \ref{thm:main-existence-T} to neighborhoods of $Z_j\cup S_j(X_j\times[0,2])\cup \bigcup\limits_{\tau\in X_j}h_{i(\sigma,j)}(S(\tau,2)\times B)$ for all top-dimensional simplices $\sigma$ of the triangulation we deform $\Xi$ to make it leafwise genuinely contact on these neighborhoods.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3.12 fills each neighborhood

nodes.name: Choose a representative germ and a collar $U$
nodes.statement: Choosing a representative $\eta$ of the contact germ along $\Sigma_{K_+}$ let $U$ be a neighborhood of $\partial \widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl} $ such that $K|_{U\cap\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-}>0$ and the contact structure $\eta$ is defined on $\{(x,v,t); x\in U\cap\{z\geq 0\}, v\leq K_+(x)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a representative germ and a collar $U$

nodes.name: Claim: a contact embedding $\Phi$ into the collar
nodes.statement: There is a contact embedding $\Phi: \Delta_{\rm cyl}^-:= \widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-$ such that $\Phi(\partial\Delta_{\rm cyl}\cap \Delta_{\rm cyl}^-)\subset U$ and $\Phi(\Delta_{\rm cyl}^-\cap\{z=0\})\subset \{z=0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: a contact embedding $\Phi$ into the collar

nodes.name: The vector field $Z$ has Hamiltonian $z$
nodes.statement: Indeed, the contact vector field $Z=L+z\frac{\partial}{\partial z}$, $L=\sum\limits_1^{n-1}\limits u_i\frac{\partial}{\partial u_i}$ is given by the contact Hamiltonian $z$ with respect to the standard contact form $\lambda_{\rm st}=dz+\sum\limits_1^{n-1}u_id\phi_i$.
nodes.statement_short: The vector field $Z$ has Hamiltonian $z$

nodes.name: Cut off to $\widetilde Z$, tangent to $\{z=0\}$
nodes.statement: Consider a cut-off function $\sigma:{\mathbb{R}}^{2n-1}\to{\mathbb{R}}_+$ which is equal to $1$ on $\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}\setminus U$ and supported in ${\rm Int\,}\widetilde\Delta_{\rm cyl}$, and let $\widetilde Z$ denote the contact vector field defined by the contact Hamiltonian $K:=z\sigma$. Let us observe that $\widetilde Z$ is tangent to the hyperplane $\{z=0\}$ because $K$ vanishes on this hyperplane. Let $Z^t$ and $\widetilde Z^t$ be the contact flows generated by $Z$ and $\widetilde Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Cut off to $\widetilde Z$, tangent to $\{z=0\}$

nodes.name: $\Phi=\widetilde Z^{\widetilde C}\circ Z^{-C}$
nodes.statement: Then the formula $\Phi:= \widetilde Z^{\widetilde C}\circ Z^{-C}$ is the required contact embedding for appropriately chosen positive constants $C,\widetilde C$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi=\widetilde Z^{\widetilde C}\circ Z^{-C}$

nodes.name: Find $K_-<\Phi_*K<K_+$
nodes.statement: For an appropriate choice of a special Hamiltonian $K<K_{\mathrm{univ}}$ we have $\Phi_*K< K_+$. On the other hand, there exists $K_-\in C_+$ such that $\Phi_*K>K_-$.
nodes.statement_short: Find $K_-<\Phi_*K<K_+$

nodes.name: $D_K$ embeds near $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$
nodes.statement: Hence, the overtwisted disc $D_{\mathrm{ot}}=D_K$ embeds into an arbitrarily small neighborhood of $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$, i.e. $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$ is overtwisted.
nodes.statement_short: $D_K$ embeds near $\widehat U_{K_-,K_+}$

nodes.name: Identify $M\times T^*_+S^1$ with $M\times(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus0)$
nodes.statement: $(M\times T_+^*S^1, \lambda+vdt)$ is contactomorphic to $(M\times {\mathbb{R}}^2\setminus 0, \lambda+xdy-ydx$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $M\times T^*_+S^1$ with $M\times(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus0)$

nodes.name: Embed $M\times D^2_R$ via the Reeb flow
nodes.statement: On the other hand, there exists a contact embedding $(M\times D^2_R,\lambda +xdy-ydx)\to (M\times {\mathbb{R}}^2\setminus 0, \lambda+xdy-ydx)$. It can be defined, for instance, by the formula $(w,x,y)\mapsto (\frak{R}^{-2Ry}(w), x+2R,y)$, where $\frak{R}^t$ is the Reeb flow of the contact form $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: Embed $M\times D^2_R$ via the Reeb flow

nodes.name: Theorem 10.2 makes $M\times D^2_R$ overtwisted
nodes.statement: But according to Theorem \ref{thm:stab} the product $(M\times D^2_R, \{\lambda+xdy-ydx=0\})$ is overtwisted if the radius of the $2$-disc $D^2_R$ is sufficiently large, and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 10.2 makes $M\times D^2_R$ overtwisted

nodes.name: Corollary 10.3: $V^+(K)$ is overtwisted
nodes.statement: According to Corollary \ref{cor:stab2} for a sufficiently large contact Hamiltonian $K>0$ the domain $V^+(K)$ is overtwisted.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 10.3: $V^+(K)$ is overtwisted

nodes.name: Corollary 1.4 gives $g_{2K}\lessapprox g_K$, so the order is trivial
nodes.statement: Hence, Corollary \ref{cor:isocontact} from allows us to construct an isotopy of $V^+({2K})$ into $V^+(K)$ inside $Y\times T^*S^1$. This isotopy extends to a global diffeotopy, and hence $g_{2K}\lessapprox g_K$, where $g_H$ denotes a time 1 map of the contact Hamiltonian $H$. On the other hand, we clearly have $g_{K}\lessapprox g_{2K}$, i.e. the order $\lessapprox $ is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 1.4 gives $g_{2K}\lessapprox g_K$, so the order is trivial

nodes.name: Make $\xi$ contact on a ball $B$ with an overtwisted disc
nodes.statement: Choose a ball $B\subset M\setminus A$ with piecewise smooth boundary and deform the almost contact structure $\xi$ to make it a contact structure on $B$ with an overtwisted disc $(D_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}) \subset (\partial B, \xi)$ on its boundary. This can be done since any two almost contact structures on the ball are homotopic if we do not require the homotopy to be fixed on $\partial B$.
nodes.statement_short: Make $\xi$ contact on a ball $B$ with an overtwisted disc

nodes.name: Proposition 3.1: universal holes
nodes.statement: Using Proposition \ref{prop:unique-model} we deform the almost contact structure $\xi$ relative to $A\cup B$ to an almost contact structure $\xi$ on $M$, which is genuine in the complement of finitely many disjoint balls $B_1,\dots, B_N\subset M\setminus (A\cup B)$ where each $(B_i, \xi|_{B_i})$ is isomorphic to $(B_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}}, \eta_{K_{\mathrm{univ}}})$ as almost contact structures.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 3.1: universal holes

nodes.name: Proposition 3.8 and ambient connected sums
nodes.statement: According to Proposition \ref{prop:neighb-ot} we can pick disjoint balls $B_i' \subset {\rm Int\,}(B)$, $i=1,\dots, N$, each with an overtwisted disc on their boundary $(D^i_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}^i) \subset (\partial B_i', \xi)$. As we will describe in Section~\ref{sec:BCS} we can perform an ambient boundary connected sum $B_i \# B_i' \subset M \setminus A$ such that the sets $B_i \# B_i'$ are disjoint for $i=1, \dots, N$ and there are isomorphisms of almost contact structures $$ (B_i \# B_i', \xi|_{B_i \# B_i'}) \cong (B_i \# B_i', \xi|_{B_i} \# \xi|_{B_i'}) \cong (B_K \# B_i', \eta_K \# \xi|_{B_i'}). $$
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 3.8 and ambient connected sums

nodes.name: Proposition 3.9 fills each connected sum
nodes.statement: Now for $i=1, \dots, L$ by definition we have $(D^i_{\mathrm{ot}}, \eta_{\mathrm{ot}}^i) = (D_{K_i}, \eta_{K_i})$ for special contact Hamiltonians $K_i$ such that $K_i < K_{\mathrm{univ}}$. Therefore we can apply Proposition \ref{p:ConnectSumDisc} to homotope $\xi|_{B_i \# B_i'}$ relative to the boundary to a genuine contact structure on $B_i \# B_i'$ for each $i=1,\dots, N$. The result will be a contact structure on $M$ that is homotopic relative to $A$ to the original almost contact structure.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 3.9 fills each connected sum

nodes.name: Two routes: direct or via the classification
nodes.statement: This can be seen directly by finding a copy of $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\xi_{\mathrm{ot}})$ in a neighborhood of the traditional overtwisted disc, or indirectly, from the classification theorem from \cite{Eli89}.
nodes.statement_short: Two routes: direct or via the classification

nodes.name: Contact ball containing $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ in the standard class
nodes.statement: Indeed, one can first find a contact structure on the ball with standard boundary which contains $(D_{\mathrm{ot}},\xi_{\mathrm{ot}})$ and which is in the standard almost contact class.
nodes.statement_short: Contact ball containing $D_{\mathrm{ot}}$ in the standard class

nodes.name: Implanting it does not change the isotopy class
nodes.statement: Then, implanting this ball in an overtwisted contact manifold does not change the isotopy class of this structure.
nodes.statement_short: Implanting it does not change the isotopy class
